yzUGcu9Zit.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports findings (no system dominates, none beats the long-context baseline on every axis, retrieval is the most common failure) rather than gains.
yzUGcu9Zit.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating memory over long, multi-department clinical histories is an important problem and that the eight-axis design, many systems and backbones, and fact-tracing failure analysis are systematic.
yzUGcu9Zit.main_concern: The benchmark relies heavily on LLM-generated synthetic histories and dialogues, and its fidelity to real clinical records and the preservation of ground-truth facts are insufficiently validated.

wPnu90ms5m.one_liner: Jointly watermarks diffusion-LM tokens via multi-marginal optimal transport solved with belief propagation and Sinkhorn on a tree-structured graph.
wPnu90ms5m.problem: Existing diffusion-LM watermarks adapt side-information generation but otherwise mimic autoregressive per-token schemes, leaving parallel token generation unexploited for detection.
wPnu90ms5m.method: TIDEmark coordinates token choices over several positions using token-pair watermark scores via multi-marginal optimal transport, with an ideal distortion-free guarantee for recorded token marginals. A tree-structured interaction graph with belief propagation and Sinkhorn makes the cost linear rather than exponential in the number of jointly watermarked tokens.
wPnu90ms5m.key_idea: Couple token choices across parallel positions through multi-marginal optimal transport on a tree-structured pairwise graph, preserving each token's marginal while strengthening joint detection.
wPnu90ms5m.evidence: Detection and generation-quality experiments on two diffusion language models across multiple tasks including HumanEval functional correctness, with robustness tested only for the Chain configuration under random edits (per the reviews).
wPnu90ms5m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint watermarking is well motivated by parallel generation in diffusion language models and that the tree construction with Sinkhorn and belief propagation avoids exponential enumeration.
wPnu90ms5m.main_concern: Reviewers cite hard-to-follow exposition and weak controls: differing decoding settings across methods, no ablations, detection thresholds validated on the same cohort, and robustness tested only for one configuration.

Vno5uUQDSW.one_liner: Weak-form Fokker-Planck regularization using a few test functions and an unbiased U-statistic estimator, avoiding Hessians in force-field learning.
Vno5uUQDSW.problem: Diffusion models for molecular equilibrium distributions predict inaccurate forces that make Langevin simulations diverge, and standard Fokker-Planck regularization fixes this only through expensive Hessian computations.
Vno5uUQDSW.method: A weak FP regularization approximates standard FP using a small set of efficiently computable test functions (Galerkin projections and integration by parts per the reviews), and an unbiased U-statistic estimator handles minibatched moments under stochastic gradients.
Vno5uUQDSW.key_idea: Replace the Fokker-Planck residual constraint with its projection onto a few test functions, integrating by parts to drop higher-order derivatives, and estimate it unbiasedly with a U-statistic.
Vno5uUQDSW.evidence: Experiments on real-world and analytic potentials with augmented and SE(3)-equivariant graph transformers, compared with standard FP regularization.
Vno5uUQDSW.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that it matches the accuracy of the standard FP regularization at a fraction of the memory and runtime.
Vno5uUQDSW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the weak-formulation idea is concrete and technically solid and targets the real computational overhead of higher-order derivatives in Fokker-Planck regularization.
Vno5uUQDSW.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty (weak formulations are established, for example VPINN) and the experiments, citing missing comparisons with cheaper alternatives such as Hutchinson trace estimators and limited force-accuracy and large-system evaluation.

1k4rCXykad.one_liner: Agent self-jailbreaking: agents search the web and iteratively modify their own harness to comply with requests they initially refused.
1k4rCXykad.problem: Self-improvement lets agents acquire knowledge and modify their own implementations, which can also change safety behavior and let an agent learn to comply with a request it initially refused.
1k4rCXykad.method: Introduces MIRROR, a research harness that combines web search and local exploration with iterative self-modification, using feedback from retrying the original request in task-wise research. The modified agents are then evaluated on unseen tasks to assess transfer.
1k4rCXykad.key_idea: Let the agent research and rewrite its own harness using feedback from retrying the refused request, then test the modified agent on unseen harmful requests.
1k4rCXykad.evidence: Five agent frameworks and three open-weight models, with reviews citing harmful text generation, tool-invoked actions and cyber tasks, judged by an LLM-based detector and judge.
1k4rCXykad.claimed_gains: Task-wise self-jailbreaking raises compliance from 0.9% to 70.9%, and on unseen requests the modified agents collectively reach 97.0% compliance versus 1.8% for the original agents.
1k4rCXykad.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that self-jailbreaking through persistent self-modification is an interesting, well-posed threat model and that the held-out transfer results are striking.
1k4rCXykad.main_concern: Measurement depends on LLM detectors and judges without human validation (the judge shares a model with the systems under test), and the study uses its own dataset and no baselines beyond a vanilla agent.

C1YBvAJWb2.one_liner: Rectifies black-box AI decisions from human feedback and escalates to humans under adaptive calibration guaranteeing per-step risk control.
C1YBvAJWb2.problem: Human review prevents unsafe AI decisions but is costly, and adaptively learning from human feedback changes the model and can invalidate previously calibrated safety guardrails.
C1YBvAJWb2.method: CARE (calibrated adaptive rectification and escalation) pairs a rectification module that improves AI decisions by learning the structure of human-AI misalignment with an adaptive calibration module that guarantees risk control at every time step for any rectification module. It works with any black-box AI model.
C1YBvAJWb2.key_idea: Recalibrate escalation adaptively while a rectifier learns from human feedback, accounting for how labels were acquired so risk control holds at every time step.
C1YBvAJWb2.evidence: Four safety-critical real-world datasets spanning language, vision, driving and robotics (hate-speech detection, workplace video hazards, driving and robotic dispatch per the reviews), with ablations.
C1YBvAJWb2.claimed_gains: CARE reduces human queries by 25-81% relative to baselines while achieving human-aligned decisions.
C1YBvAJWb2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the statistical consequences of adaptive feedback seriously and reusing scarce oracle labels for both correction and calibration is promising, with thorough end-to-end evaluation across several domains.
C1YBvAJWb2.main_concern: It is unclear that the theoretical per-step guarantee carries over to the implemented method, given approximations in counterfactual replays, an acquisition module that is not tested, and i.i.d. stream and oracle assumptions.

efE3h1yYRd.one_liner: Unified objective organizing on-policy distillation along four axes, with a 30-plus-configuration study on mathematical reasoning.
efE3h1yYRd.problem: It is unclear which parts of on-policy distillation (OPD) are essential for effective learning and which can be simplified.
efE3h1yYRd.method: A unified training objective organizes representative OPD methods along rollout source, trajectory weighting, token-position weighting and local supervision loss, and over 30 configurations are compared on mathematical reasoning. The findings are then combined into a final training recipe.
efE3h1yYRd.key_idea: Decompose OPD into four design axes (rollout source, trajectory weighting, token-position weighting, local supervision loss) and ablate each axis in a controlled study.
efE3h1yYRd.evidence: Over 30 OPD configurations on mathematical reasoning benchmarks; reviews note the experiments use a single Qwen3 teacher-student family.
efE3h1yYRd.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative findings: failed-trajectory-only training matches all-trajectory accuracy, a random 100-token window stays competitive with full-token supervision, and SelecTKD gives the highest accuracy among tested token-weighting methods.
efE3h1yYRd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-axis framework is clear and unified and that the empirical comparison is extensive and yields useful findings such as failure-only supervision and random token windows.
efE3h1yYRd.main_concern: The framework mostly reorganizes existing OPD methods into a taxonomy without a new algorithm, and the conclusions rest on one mathematical-reasoning setting with Qwen3 teacher-student pairs.

NqvN6MMVeN.one_liner: Shows conditional flow models inflate sample variance when underfitting, converting epistemic uncertainty into apparent aleatoric variance.
NqvN6MMVeN.problem: It is unclear what the conditional distributions from conditional flow models (CFMs) carry beyond a point predictor, and their samples often have larger variance than the true conditional even in near-deterministic regression.
NqvN6MMVeN.method: Controlled synthetic and real-data experiments compare CFMs with explicit smoothing estimators, a simplified-setting theory explains the variance inflation as a local mixture of true conditionals, and the effect is used to design high-coverage predictive sets.
NqvN6MMVeN.key_idea: Smoothing from underfitting makes the learned velocity field average over nearby conditionals, so generated samples are a local mixture of true conditionals with inflated variance.
NqvN6MMVeN.evidence: Controlled synthetic experiments varying three smoothing mechanisms (early stopping, smoothing penalties and kernel ridge regression per the reviews), real-data tasks in policy evaluation, cell perturbation prediction and behavior cloning, and a theorem in a simplified setting.
NqvN6MMVeN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the variance-inflation effect is clearly identified and appears consistently across several smoothing mechanisms, with an intuitive local-mixture explanation.
NqvN6MMVeN.main_concern: Reviewers see the claims as overstated and the effect as not specific to flow models (a Gaussian-NLL MLP shows the same), with Theorem 1 resting on a restrictive smoothing-kernel assumption and unclear novelty over prior work on selective underfitting.

KGGGKDExTm.one_liner: Bounds diffusion sampling discretization error in TV by mutual information at the target resolution, bounded via rate-distortion, not dimension.
KGGGKDExTm.problem: Existing discretization bounds for diffusion sampling scale with the data's intrinsic dimension or, for Gaussian mixtures, with the squared logarithm of the number of components.
KGGGKDExTm.method: For the posterior-mean exponential integrator with K steps, the time-discretization error in total variation is bounded by O(I_Gamma L/K), where I_Gamma is the mutual information between data and a Gaussian observation at the terminal signal-to-noise ratio and L is the log-SNR range. I_Gamma is bounded by the rate-distortion function of the data, which is at most the metric entropy of the support and, for Gaussian mixtures, at most the label entropy.
KGGGKDExTm.key_idea: Control the exponential-integrator discretization error directly in TV by the mutual information at the terminal SNR, then bound that information by the data's rate-distortion function.
KGGGKDExTm.evidence: Theoretical bounds compared with KL-based bounds converted by Pinsker's inequality, with applications to Gaussian mixtures and a pixel-versus-latent discussion; reviews mention a per-pixel experiment.
KGGGKDExTm.claimed_gains: Discretization error in TV of O(I_Gamma L/K), linear in L/K, whereas Pinsker's inequality applied to information-theoretic KL bounds gives only sqrt(L/K), and the bound improves on metric-entropy and label-entropy bounds.
KGGGKDExTm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the direct TV result is a meaningful theoretical contribution with clear exposition, giving a better step-size dependence than converting KL bounds and a useful link between compressibility and ambient dimension.
KGGGKDExTm.main_concern: The broader implication is contested: the claim that pixel-space diffusion pays only for the latent code holds only at a noise-dominated resolution, so the comparison with latent diffusion is not like-for-like and lacks supporting experiments.

7MSUD5jqpZ.one_liner: Learns an information-aware coordinate map from parameter-simulation pairs and distills it into symbolic expressions of identifiable parameter combinations.
7MSUD5jqpZ.problem: Simulation-based inference is unnecessarily high-dimensional when data depend on only a few parameter combinations, so neural estimators spend simulator calls on redundant directions.
7MSUD5jqpZ.method: The degeneracy distillery learns, from parameter-simulation pairs alone (no likelihoods, simulator gradients or observed data), a coordinate map across the prior that drives the transformed information metric toward the identity, with a joint objective choosing the number of identifiable coordinates. It then distills the map into compact symbolic expressions.
7MSUD5jqpZ.key_idea: Flatten a neural-estimated Fisher information metric toward the identity with a learned coordinate map, then symbolically regress the map into closed-form parameter combinations.
7MSUD5jqpZ.evidence: Experiments across scientific simulator domains with calibration tests and NPE comparisons; reviews cite dimension reduction up to 32 parameters in a controlled example.
7MSUD5jqpZ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that the method reduces the effective parameter dimension and the simulation budget (truncated before results).
7MSUD5jqpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that non-identifiability in simulation-based inference is an important problem and that the interpretable symbolic coordinates, tested across scientific application domains, are a valuable contribution.
7MSUD5jqpZ.main_concern: Scalability is unproven: the method depends on estimating the Fisher information, appears viable mainly in low-dimensional settings with unimodal posteriors, and the one-time discovery cost is not counted in the simulation budget.

mZbq1PjqKX.one_liner: Transports unpaired invariant measures using an intertwining-EDMD dynamics-aware cost in linear optimal transport that supervises Flow Matching.
mZbq1PjqKX.problem: Model states and observations of imperfect numerical models lie on different attractors, and standard transport objectives pair states by geometric proximity even when their futures are dynamically incompatible.
mZbq1PjqKX.method: Intertwining Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (iEDMD) learns an alignment between reduced representations of two dynamics from unpaired trajectories, defining a pairwise ground cost that bounds the commutation residual and reduces dynamical alignment to linear optimal transport. The resulting coupling supervises a Flow Matching model without integrating the transport during training, and the map can be wrapped around an unchanged solver in a transport-solve-transport procedure.
mZbq1PjqKX.key_idea: Pair unpaired states by a ground cost from a learned dynamics alignment (iEDMD) that upper-bounds the commutation residual, turning dynamical alignment into linear optimal transport.
mZbq1PjqKX.evidence: Reviews cite experiments such as ring-deformed Lorenz-96, comparing dynamics-aware couplings with simpler mappings across coordinate deformations and structural changes; the abstract is truncated before results.
mZbq1PjqKX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using dynamics rather than Euclidean distance to pair unpaired states is well justified by the commutation-residual bound and keeps training simulation-free.
mZbq1PjqKX.main_concern: The contribution of the successor (dynamical) term is not isolated, since much of the gain may come from the learned alignment, and the advantage is clear mainly after coordinate deformation but not when the systems already share coordinates.

uGYnyWkANi.one_liner: NRFS: Bayesian optimization acquisition from optimizer probabilities over sampled functions, prioritizing functions that have not driven earlier decisions.
uGYnyWkANi.problem: Existing Bayesian optimization acquisition strategies explicitly balance exploration and exploitation, often needing carefully designed heuristics or hyper-parameter tuning.
uGYnyWkANi.method: Non-Replacement Function Space Sampling (NRFS) establishes a correspondence between each candidate and the set of sampled functions that consider it the optimizer, and prioritizes functions that have not contributed to previous acquisition decisions. Reviews describe it as probability of optimality with Parzen density estimation.
uGYnyWkANi.key_idea: Associate each candidate with the sampled functions for which it is the optimizer and prioritize functions not yet used in acquisition decisions, giving exploration-exploitation balance without tuning.
uGYnyWkANi.evidence: Benchmarks of synthetic functions and materials optimization tasks (20 independent trials per the reviews) plus a convergence theorem for any Lipschitz-continuous objective.
uGYnyWkANi.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims it outperforms existing BO methods, particularly where both global exploration and local refinement are needed, without numbers.
uGYnyWkANi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the function-space view linking optimizer probabilities to filtering of sampled functions is intuitive, and that the paper is clearly presented and empirically effective.
uGYnyWkANi.main_concern: Reviewers see the method as an incremental rejection-sampling fix for probability-of-optimality over-exploitation, with narrow benchmarks, unclear probability conditioning and a theorem that does not cover the density-estimated algorithm.

4UENYSxtkj.one_liner: Replaces point-valued bottleneck representations with credal sets to propagate and separate aleatoric, data-induced and processing-induced uncertainty.
4UENYSxtkj.problem: Information bottleneck variants, including robust ones, do not explicitly preserve the information needed to estimate uncertainty at the output of the bottleneck.
4UENYSxtkj.method: The Credal Information Bottleneck represents uncertainty in the data-generating distribution and in the data processing as credal sets (convex combinations of probability distributions) and propagates it through the bottleneck. A variational version, VCIB, makes the objective differentiable.
4UENYSxtkj.key_idea: Represent the data distribution and the processing as credal sets and propagate them through the bottleneck, so uncertainty sources can be estimated separately at its output.
4UENYSxtkj.evidence: Reviews cite three colored-image benchmarks (including C-KMNIST) with a two-environment construction, ten seeds, statistical comparisons and ablations measuring worst-environment distortion, post-intervention accuracy and conflict detection.
4UENYSxtkj.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before the results.
4UENYSxtkj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the credal-set formalization is clear with meaningful guarantees (such as a pooling distortion floor) and that VCIB reduces worst-environment distortion and improves post-intervention worst-case accuracy across three benchmarks.
4UENYSxtkj.main_concern: Experiments use only closely related colored-image benchmarks with two environments, the separation of uncertainty types is not validated against ground truth or always better than baselines, and gains are not isolated from environment-specific prediction.

2WyWjRUCHb.one_liner: Models learn natural-language insights, then distill them into weights by fine-tuning on insight-guided solutions, and can remove insights before distillation.
2WyWjRUCHb.problem: Reward-driven self-learning can reinforce both useful skills and strategies that exploit the task or its grader, so it is hard to control what gets consolidated into a model's weights.
2WyWjRUCHb.method: Insight distillation fine-tunes on solutions generated using modular, individually tested natural-language insights, then evaluates without the insights in the prompt; models can also identify and remove insights for a specified skill before distillation. CORE Alignment extends this so LLMs learn their own alignment principles in natural language alongside task-solving insights.
2WyWjRUCHb.key_idea: Distill a bank of tested natural-language insights into weights by fine-tuning on insight-guided solutions, alternating with insight learning, so inspectable insights control what is consolidated.
2WyWjRUCHb.evidence: Six reasoning tasks and two models (12 model-task pairs) with R-SFT and tuned GRPO baselines at matched rollout budgets; reviews cite three-seed reporting and experiments on 27B and 120B models.
2WyWjRUCHb.claimed_gains: Insight distillation preserves in-context gains almost exactly, outperforms rejection-sampled fine-tuning on all 12 model-task pairs and tuned GRPO on 10 of 12 at matched rollout budgets.
2WyWjRUCHb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the consolidation result is convincing, with careful controlled experiments, honest reporting of failures, and a real benefit from combining language-level learning with weight updates.
2WyWjRUCHb.main_concern: Novelty relative to concurrent lesson-distillation work is unclear, and the insight-generation process is heuristic and not ablated, with limited causal attribution of individual insights and narrow baseline comparisons.

ZA2snoQnLJ.one_liner: Measures reasoning efficiency as excess tokens above the minimal human derivation across 15 frontier models on 2026 competition problems.
ZA2snoQnLJ.problem: How the token efficiency of large reasoning models has changed over time lacks an expert-length reference point against which reasoning can be measured across problems and time.
ZA2snoQnLJ.method: Defines the minimal human derivation (the shortest published human solution) as an expert-length milestone and measures mean tokens per correct solution on 40 problems from 2026 AIME and HMMT across 15 frontier models with repeated sampling. Matched open-weight model pairs and DeepSeek releases separate the effects of scale and post-training.
ZA2snoQnLJ.key_idea: Compare each model's tokens per correct solution with the shortest published human derivation of the same problem, tracking excess length release by release.
ZA2snoQnLJ.evidence: 40 problems from 2026 AIME and HMMT across 15 frontier models with repeated sampling, replication on competition physics, and matched open-weight pairs plus a DeepSeek release decomposition.
ZA2snoQnLJ.claimed_gains: Mean tokens per correct solution fell 8.5x across OpenAI models and 4.8x across Anthropic releases while accuracy rose, and excess length above the human expert solution falls 22.3-32.6% for OpenAI and 31.7-45.4% for Anthropic per quarter.
ZA2snoQnLJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the release-by-release measurement of falling token use with rising accuracy is carefully designed and informative, with the minimal human derivation as an interpretable reference and interesting scale versus post-training results.
ZA2snoQnLJ.main_concern: Shorter outputs do not directly show expert reasoning (for example one model uses fewer tokens but backtracks more), the problem set and model families are narrow, and the exponential extrapolation and the minimal-derivation floor are not well justified.

KQuj6oq5pu.one_liner: Proves matching upper and lower bounds for reverse-KL policy distillation under online versus offline teacher feedback.
KQuj6oq5pu.problem: The statistical guarantees of reverse-KL distillation for language models are poorly understood, in particular whether full teacher action distributions help and whether student-generated (online) trajectories are required.
KQuj6oq5pu.method: Establishes matching upper and lower bounds across four settings (online vs offline trajectories, full teacher distribution vs only the probability of the sampled action). Reviewers describe an algorithm that keeps weights over the policy class and uses clipped trajectory losses with truncated prefix ratios to handle visitation mismatch.
KQuj6oq5pu.key_idea: Teacher-generated actions reveal teacher preferences that queries at student-chosen actions can miss, so online distillation with probability-only feedback needs more data than offline distillation.
KQuj6oq5pu.evidence: Theoretical proofs of upper and lower bounds in the analyzed settings; a reviewer notes that no empirical results are provided.
KQuj6oq5pu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem clearly framed, the online/offline feedback separation with its lower bound interesting, and the main messages easy to follow.
KQuj6oq5pu.main_concern: Practical relevance is limited: the misspecified guarantee can become vacuous, the algorithm needs a weight per candidate policy, and no empirical results or clear related-work comparison are given.

ZMmJDeDTXk.one_liner: Nested replay separates inherited gains from further improvement in self-improving coding agents by revising a shared starting improver.
ZMmJDeDTXk.problem: Rising performance across generations of a self-improving coding system does not show whether progress comes from retaining an earlier improvement or from the improver getting better at producing improvements.
ZMmJDeDTXk.method: Competing versions revise copies of the same starting improver, and the task agents produced by the resulting improvers are evaluated. The method is applied to a selected Hyperagents edit across three models.
ZMmJDeDTXk.key_idea: Have competing improver versions revise copies of the same starting improver and evaluate the task agents they produce, so inherited advantage is separated from the improver's own revision contribution.
ZMmJDeDTXk.evidence: Experiments on a selected Hyperagents edit across three models; on MiMo-V2.5, inheritance accounts for almost all of the observed difference between lineages.
ZMmJDeDTXk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a concrete measurement problem in recursive self-improvement and that the nested replay design is well motivated and useful.
ZMmJDeDTXk.main_concern: Reviewers say the higher-order experiments have limited coverage (one backbone, few constructed states) and that the result may mostly reflect how often improvers edit rather than how well they edit.

0dy9O85YLZ.one_liner: Ditto trains LLMs to simulate human behavior by jointly optimizing rollouts and feedback-conditioned improved rollouts with GRPO.
0dy9O85YLZ.problem: Learning from feedback for LLMs has focused on verifiable scalar rewards, but simulating human behavior needs verbal, subjective, multi-faceted feedback.
0dy9O85YLZ.method: After each rollout the model receives verbal feedback and generates a feedback-conditioned improved rollout; both are optimized jointly with GRPO, distilling the feedback into the base policy so none is needed at test time. The authors also release SOUL, a benchmark and training data suite of 10 tasks in six categories.
0dy9O85YLZ.key_idea: Condition a second rollout on verbal feedback, then optimize original and improved rollouts together with GRPO so the feedback is distilled into the policy without test-time feedback.
0dy9O85YLZ.evidence: The SOUL suite of 10 tasks across Theory of Mind, character role play, social skill, learner simulation, user simulation and persona simulation; reviewers note ablations, seed checks, human evaluation and a higher-compute GRPO baseline.
0dy9O85YLZ.claimed_gains: An average 36% improvement over the base model and exceeds GPT-5.4 on 6 of 10 (abstract text is cut off after this point).
0dy9O85YLZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad ten-task evaluation, the idea of learning from text feedback beyond scalar rewards, and SOUL as a reusable resource.
0dy9O85YLZ.main_concern: It is unclear that verbal feedback adds benefit beyond extra compute, since plain GRPO performs well and Ditto doubles rollouts per prompt, and degradation on general tasks is untested.

PQw4BecKzn.one_liner: Enterprise-JEPA predicts tool-call outcomes in latent space and decodes operational signals to speed up agent planning.
PQw4BecKzn.problem: LLM-based world models plan by autoregressively generating imagined observations, which makes repeated planning over candidate tool actions computationally expensive.
PQw4BecKzn.method: An action-conditioned latent world model takes task context, history and a candidate action, predicts the latent of the resulting tool observation, and decodes seven operational signals (action type, execution status, error, progress, side effects, information sufficiency, task completion). Training has two stages: latent dynamics from unlabeled trajectories, then operational-state heads on annotated transitions.
PQw4BecKzn.key_idea: Predict the next tool observation as a latent embedding with a JEPA objective, then read out seven operational-state signals with heads trained on annotated transitions.
PQw4BecKzn.evidence: Five benchmarks with beam search against a no-world-model baseline, and a comparison with a similarly sized LLM-based world model on structured next-state prediction and planning latency.
PQw4BecKzn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative gains: better than a no-world-model baseline on all five benchmarks and substantially faster latent rollout than an LLM-based world model).
PQw4BecKzn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that avoiding autoregressive generation of imagined observations is a useful design with substantial latency gains and a practical enterprise-tool application.
PQw4BecKzn.main_concern: Controls do not isolate whether latent dynamics are learned, since the operational heads read the Transformer hidden state, and a hand-tuned planner with about fifteen free constants may drive much of the result.

LKS07GDQlu.one_liner: Linear-softmax analysis shows SFT on stylistically biased teachers drifts in style and forgets semantics, while exact-gradient RFT does not.
LKS07GDQlu.problem: SFT leads to more forgetting than reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) even when all teacher demonstrations are semantically correct, and the reason is unclear.
LKS07GDQlu.method: Using a tractable linear-softmax policy on classification tasks, the authors derive an exact decomposition of updates into semantic and style components and prove a forgetting separation under explicit conditions.
LKS07GDQlu.key_idea: Decompose updates into semantic and style components: SFT with a nonuniform teacher develops off-axis style drift that damages semantics, while RFT with exact policy gradients preserves within-class symmetry.
LKS07GDQlu.evidence: Theorems for a linear-softmax model, simulations, and a 6-task sentiment-classification experiment using frozen LLM features.
LKS07GDQlu.claimed_gains: No numeric gains stated; proves SFT forgetting has a strictly positive lower bound over a finite training interval while RFT retains zero semantic error.
LKS07GDQlu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semantic-style decomposition gives a clean, intuitive mechanism with rigorous proofs and a well-written presentation.
LKS07GDQlu.main_concern: The linear-softmax toy setting, predefined semantic/style partition and finite-time gap may not transfer to real language models, and experiments use synthetic or frozen-feature data.

QZGuTxbvC0.one_liner: MESCO trains a diffusion heatmap model for large TSP on targets aggregated from ensembles of short MCTS rollouts.
QZGuTxbvC0.problem: Supervised heatmap methods for large-scale TSP depend on solver-generated labels, which are intractable beyond a few thousand nodes and cost nearly an hour of CPU time per instance at 10,000 nodes.
QZGuTxbvC0.method: Each short MCTS rollout follows the model's current heatmap with its own sampled search configuration for a fixed budget; edges chosen by the rollouts, weighted by solution quality, form a heatmap target used to train a diffusion model.
QZGuTxbvC0.key_idea: Aggregate edges selected by many short MCTS rollouts, weighted by tour quality, into soft heatmap targets that improve as the model improves, replacing solver labels.
QZGuTxbvC0.evidence: TSP experiments up to 10,000 nodes against supervised heatmap methods, plus preliminary CVRP results in Appendix A7 (per reviewers).
QZGuTxbvC0.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a reviewer cites up to 192x lower supervision cost).
QZGuTxbvC0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the supervision-cost bottleneck is real and that running MCTS inside the training loop aligns the training signal with test-time search, with strong TSP-10000 results.
QZGuTxbvC0.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to uniformly distributed synthetic TSP instances (no TSPLIB or clustered data), and novelty is limited since key components come from DIFUSCO, Fast-T2T and prior MCTS work.

l0SF216FM3.one_liner: Shows reward misspecification degrades CoT monitorability and mitigates it by training models to verbalize an inferred reward description.
l0SF216FM3.problem: Reward misspecification during RL may by itself make chain-of-thought unmonitorable, undermining CoT monitoring as an AI safety strategy.
l0SF216FM3.method: A testbed pairs true rewards with misspecified rewards so that hacking can be induced and labeled. To mitigate, they collect rollouts under diverse rewards, use an LM to infer a reward description, and inject it into the input so the model learns to verbalize the reward (reward description training).
l0SF216FM3.key_idea: Infer a reward description from rollouts with an LM and inject it into the input during training so the model verbalizes the reward it is optimizing in its chain-of-thought.
l0SF216FM3.evidence: A testbed across three models and three tasks (three seeds per reviewers) with paired true and misspecified rewards, plus analyses of monitor capability, underspecified instructions and CoT prefilling.
l0SF216FM3.claimed_gains: Reward description training improves monitorability by an average of 24% or 42% absolute, depending on the metric.
l0SF216FM3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, the problem is important, and the controlled paired-reward design across several models, tasks and seeds gives useful evidence.
l0SF216FM3.main_concern: The mitigation is limited: monitorability stays low on some tasks (e.g., 0.13-0.15 intervention g-mean^2 on Coding), the description prompts leak prior knowledge of the misspecification, and it needs two RL runs.

7CPeybXNyC.one_liner: WorldAuditBench benchmarks multimodal agents on finding anomalies in interactive 3D worlds through exploration and visual reasoning.
7CPeybXNyC.problem: It is unexplored whether multimodal agents can couple visual reasoning with navigation actions to find and verify anomalies, such as floating objects or traversable walls, in 3D worlds.
7CPeybXNyC.method: A benchmark of 213 anomaly tasks across 13 environments built with Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js spanning five anomaly families, evaluated with VLA-based exploration followed by VLM identification and with an end-to-end VLM agent under a fixed exploration budget.
7CPeybXNyC.key_idea: Pair action-driven exploration with visual reasoning in two auditing paradigms (VLA exploration then VLM identification, and an end-to-end VLM agent) under a fixed exploration budget.
7CPeybXNyC.evidence: Five frontier models evaluated under a fixed exploration budget; reviewers cite an ablation removing anomaly-type hints and in-context examples.
7CPeybXNyC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a useful gap by requiring interaction and evidence gathering across observations, with diverse scenes and anomaly types.
7CPeybXNyC.main_concern: The setup is easier than general anomaly discovery (one anomaly per task, anomaly-type hints and in-context examples, no normal scenes), and the VLM versus VLA-VLM gap is confounded by differing budgets and tools.

xluHvDanmo.one_liner: FMD-IMHF distills modality-specific foundation models into lightweight encoders and fuses incomplete modalities with a patient-modality hypergraph.
xluHvDanmo.problem: Neurodegenerative disease diagnosis faces limited labeled data and missing modalities, and jointly using independently pretrained foundation models is costly and gives misaligned representation spaces.
xluHvDanmo.method: Modality-specific foundation models are distilled into lightweight encoders aligned in a shared diagnostic semantic space. A patient-modality hypergraph models cross-modal complementarity and inter-patient similarity so missing modalities need not be reconstructed.
xluHvDanmo.key_idea: Fuse available modalities over a patient-modality hypergraph that links similar patients, avoiding reconstruction of missing modalities, after distilling foundation models into aligned lightweight encoders.
xluHvDanmo.evidence: Experiments on ADNI for AD diagnosis and MCI progression prediction under varying missing-modality rates, with ablations and external cohorts per reviewers.
xluHvDanmo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clinically practical and the combination of distillation and hypergraph fusion is reasonable, with ablations supporting cross-modal alignment and patient-similarity connections.
xluHvDanmo.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since distillation, alignment and hypergraph fusion are established (including prior hypergraph work on AD), and gains are inconsistent, e.g., bACC 0.750 versus 0.761 for PET-only on complete-modality MCI.

1OjUnTC0bW.one_liner: Rising Tide learns return-threshold-indexed policies, each bootstrapped from lower thresholds, to avoid learnt exploration avoidance in RL.
1OjUnTC0bW.problem: RL agents learn to suppress exploratory behavior because it initially appears suboptimal (Learnt Exploration Avoidance, LEA), which can block optimal behavior even with effectively unlimited training time.
1OjUnTC0bW.method: Given a base policy, learn a sequence of policies indexed by return threshold, each approximating the base policy restricted to trajectories above that threshold, and train higher-threshold policies by bootstrapping from lower-threshold ones. The authors also introduce the Tree Climb benchmark to isolate LEA.
1OjUnTC0bW.key_idea: Train threshold-conditioned policies that imitate the base policy on trajectories above each return threshold, bootstrapping each higher threshold from filtered rollouts of lower ones instead of maximizing expected return.
1OjUnTC0bW.evidence: Three established meta-RL domains and the Tree Climb benchmark, using Transformer, LSTM and fully connected architectures.
1OjUnTC0bW.claimed_gains: Consistently strong performance on three meta-RL domains and the only method to solve either of the two hardest Tree Climb variants; no numeric gains stated.
1OjUnTC0bW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the LEA diagnosis convincing, with controlled interventions on Tree Climb (e.g., removing the backtracking action), and see the method as following directly from that argument.
1OjUnTC0bW.main_concern: Claims are broader than the evidence: the contribution over elite-sample methods such as CEM is unclear, and standard-RL results rest on one author-designed benchmark with short horizons and small discrete action spaces.

Yrbfrg1laY.one_liner: GLAS sets layer-wise LLM pruning sparsity using gradients of the language-modeling loss under the pruning metric in use.
Yrbfrg1laY.problem: Uniform sparsity across Transformer layers degrades LLMs at high sparsity, and non-uniform methods rank layers with hand-designed proxy scores that ignore their dependence on the pruning metric.
Yrbfrg1laY.method: Casts sparsity allocation as a constrained optimization problem: GLAS-1 allocates sparsity in a single pass from metric-dependent gradients, and GLAS-K refines the allocation iteratively, keeping only updates that reduce the language-modeling loss.
Yrbfrg1laY.key_idea: Measure how language-modeling loss responds to each layer's sparsity ratio (via finite-difference gradients and a diagonal curvature approximation) under the pruning metric, then allocate a fixed sparsity budget accordingly.
Yrbfrg1laY.evidence: Perplexity and zero-shot accuracy across mainstream LLM families (LLaMA, Qwen, Mistral, 7B-32B per a reviewer), plus semi-structured and structured pruning and vision transformers.
Yrbfrg1laY.claimed_gains: Surpasses baselines in both perplexity and zero-shot accuracy; no numbers stated in the abstract.
Yrbfrg1laY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric-aware, loss-sensitivity-based allocation is well motivated and gives consistent perplexity gains across model families, sizes and pruning metrics.
Yrbfrg1laY.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty (finite-difference gradients, diagonal Hessians and trust-region steps are established), an invalid Hessian-approximation argument, evaluation at only 70% sparsity, and unreported allocation cost.

o1SMnrLnSW.one_liner: REVES turns near-miss intermediate answers into decoupled revision and verification prompts to train LLMs for sequential test-time revision.
o1SMnrLnSW.problem: Post-training optimizes single-shot objectives, which mismatches multi-step revision at inference, and multi-turn RL fails to exploit the high-quality mistakes in intermediate steps.
o1SMnrLnSW.method: A two-stage iterative framework alternates online data/prompt augmentation and policy optimization. Intermediate steps from successful recovery trajectories become separate revision and verification prompts, enabling off-policy data generation with less long-horizon sampling cost than multi-turn RL.
o1SMnrLnSW.key_idea: Convert intermediate near-miss answers from successful recovery trajectories into independent revision and verification training prompts, then optimize on them instead of full multi-turn trajectories.
o1SMnrLnSW.evidence: LiveCodeBench with public test cases as feedback, circle packing, and math benchmarks (MATH500, AIME24), against single-shot RL, multi-turn training, PAG and SCoRe.
o1SMnrLnSW.claimed_gains: +6.5 points over the RL baseline and +4.0 points over standard multi-turn training on LiveCodeBench, and matches the previously reported best result on circle packing.
o1SMnrLnSW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mismatch between single-shot training and revision-based inference is real and that reusing the model's own recoverable mistakes as training prompts is a clear, useful design backed by substantial experiments.
o1SMnrLnSW.main_concern: Gains depend on oracle stopping: under the practical self-confidence stopping rule results are mixed (e.g., MATH500 76.2 for REVES versus 78.6 for RL), and the novelty over existing self-correction methods is modest.

lL0RG6hq8D.one_liner: Shows post-training quantization checkpoints leak calibration-set membership through retained activation maxima, enabling a membership-inference attack.
lL0RG6hq8D.problem: Statistics retained in post-training-quantized checkpoints may reveal whether a record was in the calibration set, a privacy risk that is mostly overlooked.
lL0RG6hq8D.method: For SmoothQuant-based methods, comparing the original and released models recovers activation statistics; a recovered maximum can preserve a record's activation exactly, so an attacker tests membership by matching values. The authors add theory on when matches identify records and show the same mechanism in isotonic probability calibration.
lL0RG6hq8D.key_idea: Compare original and released SmoothQuant-based models to recover activation maxima that can preserve a record's activation exactly, then test membership by matching values.
lL0RG6hq8D.evidence: Attack on standard quantization software (unmodified NVIDIA Model Optimizer, OPT-125M), a maximum versus average-of-top-two-activations ablation, and isotonic probability calibration experiments.
lL0RG6hq8D.claimed_gains: With the smoothing parameter known, identifies 40.4% of calibration records at a measured false-positive rate of 0.0038% on OPT-125M (the TL;DR cites about 68% for stock exporters).
lL0RG6hq8D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies an underexplored privacy vulnerability supported by both theory and a carefully designed, convincing empirical evaluation.
lL0RG6hq8D.main_concern: Practical impact is unclear because the threat model needs the exact base checkpoint and export configuration, and calibration sets are small and often public, so exposure of sensitive records is unshown.

Hb77cNJvEr.one_liner: ProxDG guides diffusion sampling with the gradient of a time-varying Moreau envelope, computed by off-the-shelf proximal solvers.
Hb77cNJvEr.problem: Integrating optimization solvers into diffusion sampling distorts the sampling trajectory through hard projections, making objective optimization and constraint satisfaction under a diffusion prior difficult.
Hb77cNJvEr.method: A training-free method that guides samples with the gradient of a time-varying Moreau envelope, which reduces to a proximal subproblem handled by problem-specific solvers. It samples along a continuous probability path to the target posterior with exact constraint enforcement at the final step.
Hb77cNJvEr.key_idea: Use the gradient of a time-varying Moreau envelope, which smooths the objective without shifting its optima, as soft guidance; each step reduces to a proximal subproblem.
Hb77cNJvEr.evidence: Synthetic and real-world experiments; reviewers list PDE solving, black hole imaging, full-waveform inversion, motion planning and MRI.
Hb77cNJvEr.claimed_gains: Significantly outperforms training-free baselines; no numbers stated.
Hb77cNJvEr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, supported by theory, well written, and shows consistent gains across a wide range of inverse problems.
Hb77cNJvEr.main_concern: Reviewers cite an unclear distinction from prior work, since it combines known pieces such as Moreau envelopes and gradient guidance, and high compute because a proximal minimization is solved at every step.

fIszSsfzBJ.one_liner: SIFR fine-tunes flow models with signed advantages and a drift-budget constraint on velocity, enforced by a Lagrange multiplier.
fIszSsfzBJ.problem: Reward fine-tuning of flow models with positive reward weights gives no explicit unfitting signal, and repeated reweighting concentrates the distribution and causes collapse over many rounds.
fIszSsfzBJ.method: Replaces reward weights with signed advantages and constrains velocity drift from a reference model, using a Lagrange multiplier that adapts regularization strength to a prescribed drift budget. The authors show existing flow RL methods fit this framework and differ in their regularization.
fIszSsfzBJ.key_idea: Regress flow velocity on signed advantages to supply an explicit unfitting signal, while a dual-updated Lagrange multiplier holds velocity drift from the reference model within a set budget.
fIszSsfzBJ.evidence: SD3.5 Medium (2.5B), FLUX.2 Klein (9B) and Cosmos 3 Super Text2Image (64B) across all 12 backbone-reward pairs with preference and rule-based rewards.
fIszSsfzBJ.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds existing methods on all 12 backbone-reward pairs, reaches their peak rewards much faster, and keeps improving over long training where they plateau or collapse.
fIszSsfzBJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the signed-regression view and the constrained, dual-updated formulation are clean and practical, with broad validation across model scales and rewards.
fIszSsfzBJ.main_concern: Evidence for the stability claim is thin: ablations lack equally tuned alternatives (advantage clipping, KL or trust-region constraints, fixed-penalty sweeps), the derivation has inconsistencies, and results come from single runs.

0jaKFrEuE7.one_liner: PhysWAM co-denoises multiview video, metric depth and ego motion in one flow-matching transformer with a geometric consistency loss.
0jaKFrEuE7.problem: Joint generation in world-action models does not by itself impose a shared geometric constraint on predicted scene evolution and agent actions.
0jaKFrEuE7.method: A unified driving world-action model with Coupled Point Projection (CPP), which unprojects generated depth, transforms the points with generated SE(3) ego motion, and penalizes their distance from LiDAR points transformed with recorded ego motion. At inference a label-free consensus rule selects among sampled trajectories.
0jaKFrEuE7.key_idea: Penalize the distance between generated depth, unprojected and moved by generated ego motion, and LiDAR points moved by recorded ego motion, jointly supervising depth and motion.
0jaKFrEuE7.evidence: NAVSIM v1 and v2 planning, zero-shot closed-loop transfer (HUGSIM per reviewers), and future video and metric-depth prediction, with CPP ablations.
0jaKFrEuE7.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (reviewers cite CPP raising NAVSIM PDMS from 89.6 to 91.4).
0jaKFrEuE7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly constraining generated depth and ego motion through a shared geometric objective is well motivated and improves planning and depth across several benchmarks.
0jaKFrEuE7.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from coupling depth and motion or merely from added geometric supervision, since no matched decoupled-loss baseline exists, and inference is expensive (9.4 GPU-seconds per plan at 30 steps).

KSvQCjYfyJ.one_liner: IGAL converts high-importance attention heads to linear attention and the rest to sliding-window attention using existing head-importance scores.
KSvQCjYfyJ.problem: Converting pretrained self-attention to linear or sliding-window attention cuts long-context cost but can degrade accuracy, particularly on long-range retrieval.
KSvQCjYfyJ.method: Repurposes head-importance scores previously used to allocate KV-cache budgets to assign a small subset of high-scoring heads to linear attention and the remaining heads to sliding-window attention. IGAL-R adapts the linear-head proportion across short- and long-context regimes within a single checkpoint (abstract is cut off here; reviewers describe a length-dependent budget with learned group routing).
KSvQCjYfyJ.key_idea: Assign each pretrained head an attention operator by its head-importance score: top-scoring heads become linear attention for long-range modeling, the rest sliding-window for local interactions.
KSvQCjYfyJ.evidence: Short- and long-context tasks; reviewers cite synthetic long-context retrieval, e.g., HeadKV-based allocation raising 16-32K retrieval accuracy from 28.33% (random allocation) to 83.33%.
KSvQCjYfyJ.claimed_gains: not stated (the TL;DR claims it outperforms existing methods on short- and long-context tasks).
KSvQCjYfyJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using pretrained head specialization to assign operators is simple and well motivated, beating random allocation under the same linear-attention budget while reducing decoding cache.
KSvQCjYfyJ.main_concern: It is not established why scores designed for KV-cache budgeting indicate suitability for linear versus sliding-window attention, the benefit of learned routing in IGAL-R is unclear, and end-to-end latency is not measured.

mISIJ9ktNq.one_liner: Order-Space Exploration gets diversity for masked diffusion LMs by perturbing token unmasking order with Plackett-Luce noise, then majority-voting.
mISIJ9ktNq.problem: Temperature-sampled self-consistency fails for masked diffusion language models: it collapses generation length and plummets accuracy (e.g., from 35% to 6% on MATH500) without yielding usable diversity.
mISIJ9ktNq.method: Applies a one-parameter Plackett-Luce perturbation to the sampler's position ranking and aggregates N draws by majority vote over their answers, with no retraining or verifier.
mISIJ9ktNq.key_idea: Draw diversity from the order of token unmasking, not the token distribution, by perturbing position rankings with a one-parameter Plackett-Luce distribution, so single-draw accuracy is unchanged.
mISIJ9ktNq.evidence: Experiments on Dream across downstream tasks (e.g., MATH500) against temperature self-consistency, plus order-perturbed samples used as GRPO rollouts and a comparison with block decoding on LLaDA per reviewers.
mISIJ9ktNq.claimed_gains: Raises answer diversity by 2-5x while leaving single-draw accuracy unchanged, and beats standard self-consistency on Dream by up to 45.5 points.
mISIJ9ktNq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of why Dream's default sampler lacks diversity is clear and the fix is simple, with one hyperparameter, no verifier or retraining, and a clearly described method.
mISIJ9ktNq.main_concern: The advantage over block-based decoding with high temperature (as in LLaDA) is limited and unexplained, the exp(-rank/lambda) perturbation form is not compared with alternatives, and gains may mainly repair Dream's degenerate default sampler.

n3pHSWcYwV.one_liner: SynAct ranks agent decisions by mutual information between action and outcome to direct expert feedback, distilled into reusable rules.
n3pHSWcYwV.problem: LLM agents fail through recoverable slips and knowledge gaps that retrying cannot fix; expert feedback addresses the latter but is scarce, and existing methods allocate it at task level without identifying consequential decisions.
n3pHSWcYwV.method: Ranks decisions by the mutual information between the selected action and the terminal outcome across repeated rollouts, queries an expert at the highest-value decisions, and distills corrections into rules the agent reuses without expert access, applying them on a retry when a success check flags a failed first attempt.
n3pHSWcYwV.key_idea: Estimate mutual information between each selected action and the terminal outcome across repeated rollouts to find outcome-changing decisions, including when all rollouts fail, and spend expert feedback there.
n3pHSWcYwV.evidence: Four agent benchmarks and four models spanning three families (16 settings), plus a result that the signal exactly separates outcome-changing decisions given enough observations per action.
n3pHSWcYwV.claimed_gains: Improves held-out accuracy in all 16 evaluated settings, by +11.7pp on average.
n3pHSWcYwV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that label-free, decision-level allocation of expert feedback via mutual information is principled and gives consistent gains, with short learned rules helping a frozen agent without parameter updates.
n3pHSWcYwV.main_concern: It depends on verifiable outcomes and a strong LLM expert as a proxy for humans, uses ad hoc biased mutual-information estimates, and its non-regression guarantee assumes a reliable success checker.

PCZw5EG9Ft.one_liner: NoisyGEMM evaluates perturbed models inside vLLM without materializing perturbations, enabling evolution-strategy training on inference systems.
PCZw5EG9Ft.problem: Inference hardware lacks the memory and interconnect for backpropagation, and evolution-strategy perturbations add weight-update traffic or correction costs to batched inference.
PCZw5EG9Ft.method: A matrix-multiplication kernel in which candidates use compact coefficient vectors over shared Hadamard bases whose corrections are fused into the base GEMM, integrated into vLLM's linear layers and used with a separable CMA-ES variant for RL training.
PCZw5EG9Ft.key_idea: Represent each candidate's weight perturbation as coefficients over shared Hadamard bases fused into the base GEMM, so zeroth-order training runs with no per-candidate weight copies.
PCZw5EG9Ft.evidence: A100 kernel latency measurements and RL of Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 30B-A3B on six reasoning benchmarks versus GRPO (16k completion length) and the ES framework EGGROLL.
PCZw5EG9Ft.claimed_gains: Perturbed linear layers run at 1.1x-1.3x the latency of unperturbed cuBLAS GEMM, RL improves on the base model on all six reasoning benchmarks, and it outperforms GRPO on 17 of 18 model-benchmark pairs.
PCZw5EG9Ft.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the kernel is well designed, cutting memory traffic from candidate perturbations, and that zeroth-order RL on serving hardware is an interesting and valuable direction.
PCZw5EG9Ft.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing cost accounting (wall-clock time, tokens or GPU-hours versus GRPO), a serving test capped at 64 output tokens, and candidate-count settings that differ between main text and appendix.

IMw6WGwnyr.one_liner: BRIDGE pairs live-cell imaging with long-read scRNA-seq from perturbed fibroblasts and predicts gene programs from imaging features.
IMw6WGwnyr.problem: Imaging and scRNA-seq capture complementary perturbation responses but come from different cells, so direct cell-to-cell supervision between modalities is unavailable.
IMw6WGwnyr.method: A dataset of time-series live-cell imaging at 20-min resolution and endpoint long-read scRNA-seq (16,296 cells) of human fibroblasts under MYOD1 overexpression, PRRX1 RNAi and their combination, plus a cross-modal prediction model that uses cell-cycle state as a shared anchor.
IMw6WGwnyr.key_idea: Use cell-cycle state as a shared biological anchor to train a model that predicts population-level gene programs from imaging-derived features across non-matched cells.
IMw6WGwnyr.evidence: Benchmarks of existing scRNA-seq representation models on the dataset, and a cross-modal prediction model compared with prediction from cell-cycle phase alone.
IMw6WGwnyr.claimed_gains: The model predicts population-level gene programs from imaging-derived features, an improvement over prediction based on cell-cycle phase alone; no numbers stated.
IMw6WGwnyr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that paired time-resolved FUCCI imaging and long-read scRNA-seq under single and combinatorial perturbations is a useful, well-documented resource.
IMw6WGwnyr.main_concern: The paper is poorly organized and defines no task that uses both modalities, and the imaging-to-transcription inference lacks within-condition or leave-one-condition-out evaluation.

UlWhovmQ0e.one_liner: GRL-Reliability benchmarks twelve graph representation learning methods on twenty-five datasets across five reliability axes.
UlWhovmQ0e.problem: Existing graph representation learning benchmarks mostly evaluate clean-setting performance, with reliability checked one axis at a time under different method pools and protocols.
UlWhovmQ0e.method: Evaluates twelve methods (topology-only embeddings, supervised GNNs, self-supervised models, graph foundation models) on twenty-five datasets under standardized conditions, covering corruption robustness, OOD generalization, class imbalance, fairness and interpretation with per-axis reporting.
UlWhovmQ0e.key_idea: Evaluate all method families under matched conditions along five reliability axes, reporting per-axis and sub-condition results instead of a single aggregate score.
UlWhovmQ0e.evidence: Twelve methods, twenty-five graph datasets and five axes, with severity sweeps and statistical analysis per reviewers.
UlWhovmQ0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark provides a useful common framework across method families and reliability dimensions, with documented protocols and sweeps.
UlWhovmQ0e.main_concern: Gap-based OOD rankings can mislead because a small performance drop does not imply good accuracy under shift, and pretraining overlap weakens the OOD evidence.

EmKx9dIbAs.one_liner: SLiCC decomposes pretrained image embeddings into concept-specific sparse non-negative components within learned concept cones.
EmKx9dIbAs.problem: Pretrained vision embeddings encode complex scenes holistically, so their content cannot be separated into concept-specific components for uses such as concept-filtered retrieval.
EmKx9dIbAs.method: A supervised dictionary-learning model estimates a linear synthesis with sparse, non-negative combinations of groups of dictionary atoms guided by multi-label information, solved by alternating optimization or an autoencoder. Variants include a self-supervised version using CLIP image-text alignment and a fully unsupervised group-sparse autoencoder.
EmKx9dIbAs.key_idea: Model each embedding as a sum of non-negative combinations of label-specific atom groups, so each concept component lies in its own cone and can be filtered, deleted or recombined.
EmKx9dIbAs.evidence: Three types of CLIP and DINOv2 embeddings across five datasets, with concept-filtered retrieval compared against unfiltered embeddings, S-SVD and SpLiCE.
EmKx9dIbAs.claimed_gains: Supervised SLiCC improves concept-filtered image retrieval over unfiltered embeddings, including finer-grained categories not provided in training; no numbers stated.
EmKx9dIbAs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree concept-based retrieval from disentangled embeddings is an interesting, practical idea, with several variants for different supervision settings.
EmKx9dIbAs.main_concern: The evaluation is weak: the retrieval setup and the unsupervised variant's results are unclear, and baselines omit other supervised concept-learning and composed-retrieval methods.

5qVqc42f9Y.one_liner: WorldSimBench evaluates LLMs as environment simulators on 3,580 long-horizon tasks across 322 environments with executable verification.
5qVqc42f9Y.problem: LLM-based generative simulators could cheaply supply agent training trajectories, but existing evaluations cover narrow settings, short trajectories or rely on open-ended LLM scoring.
5qVqc42f9Y.method: Builds long-horizon trajectories with fixed reference outcomes from story-driven plans and executable environments across ToolUse, Terminal, Game, Web and Search; four use deterministic code or rule verifiers and Web uses a fixed LLM verifier.
5qVqc42f9Y.key_idea: Pair story-driven plans with executable environments that produce reference states and observations, so simulator outputs are checked by deterministic verifiers rather than open-ended LLM scoring.
5qVqc42f9Y.evidence: 32 models evaluated, human assessment of representative tasks in all five environments, and paired reasoning versus non-reasoning comparisons.
5qVqc42f9Y.claimed_gains: The best of 32 models reaches an unweighted macro-average success rate of 81.39%, human assessment averages 9.15 out of 10, and reasoning configurations score higher in all 13 paired comparisons.
5qVqc42f9Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is large, with executable grounding that aids reproducibility, long trajectories (up to 199 steps) and a 32-model comparison.
5qVqc42f9Y.main_concern: Reviewers question the unique contribution over AgentWorldBench, the lack of state-drift and consistency measurement, and evaluator bias from the LLM verifier in the Web domain.

89Z6g2wHEY.one_liner: TurboPairFormer is a Hopper GPU triangular attention kernel with a tile-parallel deterministic backward pass and output residual compensation.
89Z6g2wHEY.problem: In AlphaFold3-style models, triangular attention backward passes handle the shared pair-bias gradient reduction with repeated recomputation, floating-point atomics or full score-gradient storage, and compute the softmax correction from BF16-rounded outputs, losing precision.
89Z6g2wHEY.method: A tile-parallel backward algorithm recomputes each probability tile once and reuses it for query, key, value and pair-bias gradients with ordered partial reductions. Output residual compensation keeps a BF16 approximation of the rounding residual to compute the backward correction more accurately in FP32.
89Z6g2wHEY.key_idea: Reuse each recomputed probability tile for all gradients with ordered partial reductions, avoiding atomics, and keep the BF16 output rounding residual to compute the softmax backward correction in FP32.
89Z6g2wHEY.evidence: Kernel benchmarks on NVIDIA Hopper with BF16 inputs at crop sizes 384, 640, 768 and head dimensions 16, 32 against open-source backends, plus gradient accuracy, determinism and integrated training tests.
89Z6g2wHEY.claimed_gains: The visible abstract says only that it achieves the lowest mean (text cut off); reviewers cite 600/600 bitwise-identical five-repeat cases and 11.7% faster than cuEquivariance at crop 768.
89Z6g2wHEY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the kernel is clearly presented, the backward-pass design makes sense, and the determinism result is a clean contribution on a real bottleneck for AlphaFold-style models.
89Z6g2wHEY.main_concern: The headline end-to-end speedup is partly credited to a faster triangle-multiplication kernel rather than attention alone, and materialized dQ partials add cubic workspace.

fhDUZgJvtn.one_liner: Adaptive Reference Guidance learns a prefix selector from continuation outcomes to build correct trajectories for failed RL groups.
fhDUZgJvtn.problem: In reasoning RL with verifiable rewards, it is unclear how much of a verified reference solution to supply as a prefix versus letting the model generate on its own.
fhDUZgJvtn.method: Prefix continuation: the model continues from a reference prefix and keeps the trajectory if it verifies, otherwise falling back to the reference. A closed-form KL analysis against the model's success-conditioned distribution motivates a prefix selector shared across questions and applied to all-failure groups.
fhDUZgJvtn.key_idea: Choose reference prefix length with a selector trained on continuation outcomes, balancing the chance of a different correct trajectory against the reference suffix's surprisal given the prefix.
fhDUZgJvtn.evidence: Math reasoning benchmarks with two model sizes (Qwen3-4B named by a reviewer), matched-budget baselines and ablations, reported as pass@12 on 30 questions per benchmark per reviewers.
fhDUZgJvtn.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (reviewers report the highest aggregate pass@12 with small gains over the strongest baseline).
fhDUZgJvtn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of how much reference guidance to give is well motivated, the theory explains the approach, and matched-budget comparisons with several baselines are useful.
fhDUZgJvtn.main_concern: Empirical evidence is weak: gains over the strongest baseline are small, evaluation uses only 30 questions per benchmark with no variance across training seeds, and only math is covered.

gtijjdgP7T.one_liner: Trains harm-detection linear probes on activations of misaligned variants of the target model instead of off-policy data.
gtijjdgP7T.problem: Linear activation probes are brittle when trained on off-policy data, but on-policy harmful generations are rare because typical model outputs are benign.
gtijjdgP7T.method: Fine-tunes or otherwise intervenes on the base model to make misaligned variants (refusal-ablated, emergently misaligned, broadly harm-finetuned), then trains probes on their activations to detect harmful generations by the base model, varying label choices and the model supplying activations.
gtijjdgP7T.key_idea: Use activations from misaligned variants of the target model, which produce abundant harmful outputs, as near-on-policy training data for linear probes that transfer to the base model.
gtijjdgP7T.evidence: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on harm generation, comparing probes from three variant types against off-policy probes, with held-out prompt categories and design-choice sweeps.
gtijjdgP7T.claimed_gains: Probes trained on harmful model variants outperform off-policy probes at identifying harmful generations by the base model; no numbers stated.
gtijjdgP7T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using misaligned model variants to source on-policy-like harmful data is a simple, reasonable idea that is clearly and reproducibly described.
gtijjdgP7T.main_concern: All experiments use one model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and one behavior domain, and results are not broken out by generation source, so gains on the base model's own harmful outputs are unclear.

uu9k80L7nK.one_liner: ReDraft learns per-block drafter depth for speculative decoding using verifier-revealed acceptance lengths as supervision.
uu9k80L7nK.problem: Speculative-decoding drafter depth is fixed by ablation and applied uniformly despite varying draft difficulty, and convergence- or confidence-based exits often run to maximum depth, reducing throughput by 20-27%.
uu9k80L7nK.method: A 2-layer weight-shared recurrent core is iterated to variable depth, with a lightweight head predicting each block's acceptance curve. A renewal-reward stopping rule converts predictions and measured hardware costs into depth choices, planned once per block, leaving verification and losslessness unchanged.
uu9k80L7nK.key_idea: Train a recurrent drafter and an acceptance-curve predictor on verifier-revealed accepted lengths, then pick depth per block by a renewal-reward rule using measured hardware costs.
uu9k80L7nK.evidence: Five benchmarks and three targets across two model families, compared with per-task tuned depth, fixed-depth baselines and DFlash.
uu9k80L7nK.claimed_gains: Plans once per block with 1.8% overhead, and a single recipe yields policies within 4-6% of the per-task tuned optimum without task-specific depth tuning.
uu9k80L7nK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that block-level variation in useful drafter depth is real and that verifier feedback is a well-motivated, principled signal for adaptive depth.
uu9k80L7nK.main_concern: The adaptive policy does not consistently beat a simple fixed-depth baseline (tied or slower on several Qwen3 benchmarks), and the results are scattered across paragraphs and appendices.

94saSmoWOk.one_liner: SFT-as-context has the parent model answer using the SFT model's response as in-context reference, without training.
94saSmoWOk.problem: Supervised fine-tuning gives specialized skills but causes forgetting of the parent model's general capabilities, which hurts queries needing both.
94saSmoWOk.method: Training-free: the parent model receives the SFT model's response as context and answers the query, acquiring fine-tuned capabilities by in-context learning while keeping its general ones. A Bayesian framework gives theoretical guarantees that bound the error.
94saSmoWOk.key_idea: Feed the SFT model's response into the parent model's context so in-context learning transfers fine-tuned skills while the parent's own weights keep its general capabilities.
94saSmoWOk.evidence: 19 parent-SFT model pairs and 11 benchmarks, plus a case where a small open-source SFT model's responses help a strong closed-source LLM, and a Bayesian error bound.
94saSmoWOk.claimed_gains: Gaps to the SFT models of only 2.2 and 2.1 percentage points on AIME 2024 and LiveCodeBench and 2.0 macro MAE on NutriBench-English, while staying within 2.2 percentage points of the parent models on general capabilities on average.
94saSmoWOk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, needs no training or weight access, and is validated across multiple model families and tasks.
94saSmoWOk.main_concern: It needs two sequential model calls with no measured end-to-end latency or compute, and it is unclear whether the parent acquires skills or just reuses the SFT answer.

C6Dnnzy6VM.one_liner: Adds time-score outputs and losses to diffusion models, with a coefficient design space, to enable efficient exact likelihood estimation.
C6Dnnzy6VM.problem: Likelihood estimation with diffusion models relies on expensive divergence approximations; learning the time score could allow exact computation, but prior work was small-scale, degraded sampling and focused on the energy setting.
C6Dnnzy6VM.method: A regularization strategy adds the time score without hurting sampling; design coefficients and learnable terms generalize and connect the energy and mean-flow formulations; specific parametrization and learning strategies avoid singularities.
C6Dnnzy6VM.key_idea: Learn the time score as a regularized auxiliary output inside a coefficient-parameterized family (energy, mean flow, etc.) with endpoint-aware parametrization to avoid singularities.
C6Dnnzy6VM.evidence: Synthetic examples and ImageNet in pixel and latent space (ImageNet64 for most analysis, plus ImageNet256 sampling and likelihood-based filtering per reviewers).
C6Dnnzy6VM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coefficient-based unification and the endpoint-aware, non-singular parametrization are useful, and that temporal supervision need not substantially degrade sampling.
C6Dnnzy6VM.main_concern: Likelihood accuracy at image scale is not independently validated (agreement with another trained model, filtering insensitive to log-density shifts), and the extra training cost is not compared with evaluation savings.

ULMWrc9N0h.one_liner: Incognita rewrites existing agent benchmark tasks into centralized versus socially distributed versions to measure competence and prompt-injection exposure.
ULMWrc9N0h.problem: It is unclear what an agent can accomplish when the knowledge it needs and the authority to act belong to other participants.
ULMWrc9N0h.method: Incognita transforms existing benchmark tasks (adapted from AgentDojo and tau-bench) into matched environments with centralized or socially distributed knowledge and action authority, keeping task objectives and success criteria. In distributed conditions agents interact with role-isolated participants whose capabilities are initially undisclosed.
ULMWrc9N0h.key_idea: Split knowledge and action authority across role-isolated participants with undisclosed capabilities while preserving the original task scorers, so access distribution becomes an experimental variable.
ULMWrc9N0h.evidence: A competence study and exploratory security tests on tasks adapted from AgentDojo and tau-bench; task completion was lower under distributed access, most failed distributed runs stalled before obtaining needed information, and attack effects varied across models and attack families.
ULMWrc9N0h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched-environment dataset spanning retail, airline, banking and Slack domains, the preserved source scorers, and the interesting security findings.
ULMWrc9N0h.main_concern: Task coverage is limited: only 18 tau-retail and 5 tau-airline tasks were translated, and security results rest on nine Banking user tasks and three Slack workflows.

HWCHKGep3x.one_liner: Motion codec with information bottleneck and SNR-adaptive quantization separating style from content latents for zero-shot style transfer.
HWCHKGep3x.problem: Motion style transfer relies on adapters or task-specific guidance, and disentangling style from content within the core motion representation remains open.
HWCHKGep3x.method: DisCodec trains a neural motion codec with a Variational Information Bottleneck and SNR-adaptive Transform Quantization; two encoder streams produce style and content latents that are recombined to reconstruct motion while a loss keeps them mutually distinct.
HWCHKGep3x.key_idea: A variational bottleneck and noise-adaptive transform quantization limit information leakage between style and content latents, enabling decode-time style swapping.
HWCHKGep3x.evidence: Benchmarks style transfer against existing approaches and demonstrates the representation on three tasks with ablations, including 100STYLE per reviews; the abstract is cut off.
HWCHKGep3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find modeling style in the representation step a clean idea, with the SNR-adaptive quantizer a concrete design and promising zero-shot transfer results.
HWCHKGep3x.main_concern: Novelty over GenMoStyle, VQ-Style, and similar work is unclear, and unseen-style results are not consistently stronger (lower unseen-style accuracy than some baselines on 100STYLE).

bNPr53pBWD.one_liner: Controlled study showing RoPE retrieval fails at unseen offsets in global attention layers, and proposes a log-ratio RoPE hybrid.
bNPr53pBWD.problem: Language models degrade beyond training length, and how positional encoding and local versus global attention cause this is poorly understood.
bNPr53pBWD.method: Trains many language models from scratch differing only in positional encoding and local-global attention layout, analyzes retrieval at unseen query-key offsets, proves a theorem on positional-encoding resolution, and proposes a log-ratio RoPE used in a hybrid.
bNPr53pBWD.key_idea: Keep positional values at global attention layers within the trained range by using log-ratio relative positions, avoiding out-of-distribution RoPE rotations at long offsets.
bNPr53pBWD.evidence: Controlled from-scratch training of 64M-parameter models for analysis and 0.5B-parameter models for the final hybrid, evaluated on synthetic retrieval and RULER.
bNPr53pBWD.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviews cite RULER at 64K improving by 18.7 points over RoPE and 8.1 points over the RoPE-NoPE hybrid despite training at 8K.
bNPr53pBWD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled setup that trains architectures on identical data and token budgets, and the link from analysis to a concrete design.
bNPr53pBWD.main_concern: Experimental scope is narrow (small models, a single training context length, mostly synthetic retrieval and RULER) relative to the broad conclusions, and the title and writing clarity are questioned.

qIfINwyZSV.one_liner: Formulates group choreography as masked diffusion completion over a tensor coupling each dancer's motion with root state.
qIfINwyZSV.problem: Existing music-driven group choreography methods model motion, formation, and trajectory separately and need dedicated mechanisms per choreographic operation, limiting flexibility and generalization.
qIfINwyZSV.method: X-Dancers treats group choreography as bidirectional masked generation over a continuous group motion tensor, where each cell couples a dancer's motion with its root state. A ChoreoGraph Transformer with interleaved temporal and formation-grounded spatial attention and masked conditional diffusion generates unknown cells under a spatial-temporal-channel masking strategy.
qIfINwyZSV.key_idea: Mask different cells of one motion-plus-root tensor to express composition, continuation, cast extension, and trajectory control as the same conditional completion task.
qIfINwyZSV.evidence: Evaluations of motion fidelity, music synchronization, and formation quality, plus zero-shot long-duration generalization; reviews cite a formation-frame attention ablation.
qIfINwyZSV.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims leading motion fidelity, music synchronization, and formation quality and zero-shot long-duration generalization, without numbers)
qIfINwyZSV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified masked-completion formulation handles composition, continuation, cast extension, and trajectory control in one model, and that formation-frame attention is well motivated.
qIfINwyZSV.main_concern: Quantitative comparisons supply ground-truth root trajectories to all methods, so they do not test joint generation of motion and formation, the paper's central claim.

ToySuo2I0g.one_liner: Systematic comparison of 24 intrinsic-motivation objectives in one model-based RL framework under three world-model representation-learning strategies.
ToySuo2I0g.problem: It is unclear how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning, and which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models.
