ToySuo2I0g.method: They integrate 24 intrinsic objectives spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency into a common model-based RL framework and evaluate the resulting world models on zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control. Three representation-learning strategies are compared: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction.
ToySuo2I0g.key_idea: Hold the model-based RL backbone fixed and vary the intrinsic objective and the representation-learning strategy, then test transfer across control settings.
ToySuo2I0g.evidence: Locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments with three representation-learning strategies.
ToySuo2I0g.claimed_gains: not stated (empirical study: curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction gives the strongest aggregate family profile, though the best pairing depends on the experiment).
ToySuo2I0g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large-scale, unified evaluation of intrinsic objectives across transfer settings and representation strategies is thorough and could serve as a reusable benchmark.
ToySuo2I0g.main_concern: Novelty and takeaways are weak and the presentation is hard to follow: findings are descriptive, there is no dedicated related-work section, and prior work such as Plan2Explore and URLB overlaps.

U72H3DEjLP.one_liner: WDDQ trains a Minecraft diffusion world model from scratch in under 50 GPU hours using compressed latents and masked prediction.
U72H3DEjLP.problem: Video diffusion world models are expensive to train, which limits open-source research to fine-tuning existing models or inference-time approaches.
U72H3DEjLP.method: A training recipe combining an autoencoder with a highly compressed latent space, a high-fidelity causal diffusion decoder, and a world model that pairs an efficient masked predictor with a diffusion model generating latent frames conditioned on predictor outputs.
U72H3DEjLP.key_idea: Split prediction from rendering: a masked predictor models dynamics in highly compressed latents and a diffusion model generates latent frames conditioned on its outputs.
U72H3DEjLP.evidence: Minecraft experiments comparing against open-source world models on FVD, action controllability (inverse-dynamics metrics), and inference speed per reviews.
U72H3DEjLP.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing open-source models while training from scratch in under 50 GPU hours and without distilling pretrained visual encoders; the abstract gives no FVD numbers (a review cites FVD 63.4).
U72H3DEjLP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training a competitive world model from scratch within a small compute budget is a practical contribution that lowers the barrier to world-model research, with strong FVD and action controllability.
U72H3DEjLP.main_concern: The components are largely established (compressed latents, diffusion decoding, tube masking, decoupled predictor-diffuser), and results are limited to Minecraft with baselines that differ in data, size, and resolution rather than matched compute.

xr8ckcC6CT.one_liner: Diagnoses learner-side pathologies in unsupervised environment design curricula and stabilizes training with weight clipping and HL-Gauss.
xr8ckcC6CT.problem: UED work focuses on how curricula are built, but learners may lose trainability under the resulting distributions, showing parameter growth, degraded value-outcome ordering, and loss of representational diversity.
xr8ckcC6CT.method: The authors study multiple UED mechanisms, environment complexities, and long training horizons to identify recurring learner-side pathologies, then run controlled interventions that mitigate selected pathologies without changing the curriculum rule or adding environment interaction. Reviews identify the stabilizers as weight clipping and HL-Gauss.
xr8ckcC6CT.key_idea: Stabilize the learner with weight clipping and HL-Gauss, since adaptive curricula couple the learner's optimization state to its future training distribution.
xr8ckcC6CT.evidence: Experiments across four curriculum mechanisms, mostly on Kinetix, with five seeds, IQM and bootstrap reporting, component ablations, and a five-billion-interaction run per reviews.
xr8ckcC6CT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting attention from curriculum construction to learner trainability is an important, underexplored perspective, backed by systematic evidence of gains across four curriculum mechanisms.
xr8ckcC6CT.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the fix combines existing weight clipping and HL-Gauss, and it is not established that the pathologies stem from adaptive curricula rather than general PPO issues.

JdbIyJJCUI.one_liner: Routes queries through a model set ordered by co-failure coverage, stopping at a conformally calibrated cutoff to certify all-miss risk.
JdbIyJJCUI.problem: Existing risk-controlled set routing scores each model in isolation and ignores that models sharing training data or architecture tend to fail on the same queries.
JdbIyJJCUI.method: CopRoute orders models by how many new queries each answers correctly beyond those already selected, decides per query how far down the order to go, and picks the smallest cutoff that meets the target risk using a separate calibration step.
JdbIyJJCUI.key_idea: Greedy ordering by marginal co-failure coverage (linked to minimum-sum set cover), followed by split-conformal calibration of the cutoff.
JdbIyJJCUI.evidence: RouterBench and RouterEval experiments, a theorem that the ordering attains the best guarantee for efficient fixed-ordering algorithms on design data, and a calibration guarantee for the all-miss risk.
JdbIyJJCUI.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports the fewest certified calls on RouterBench and RouterEval without visible numbers)
JdbIyJJCUI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, works with existing routers without retraining, and has clearly stated guarantees and assumptions.
JdbIyJJCUI.main_concern: Dependence is used only for ordering, the theory does not directly establish the call-efficiency claim, and some gains overlap within error bars with no fixed-depth baseline.

eK6raLPN0M.one_liner: Defines the Monty gap, posterior information lost by masking rejected answers, and tests whether verifier selection evidence improves LLM decisions.
eK6raLPN0M.problem: A verifier's choice of which answer to reject may carry evidence beyond the rejection itself, but it is unclear whether using that selection evidence actually improves model decisions.
eK6raLPN0M.method: Proves that every conclusive verifier that always spares the model's committed answer at a positive fixed budget is non-ignorable, and derives a threshold decision rule under uniform selection among wrong alternatives. Tests it empirically with prompted critics, scripted oracles, and a decoder that enforces the selection rule in code.
eK6raLPN0M.key_idea: Treat which answer a verifier rejects as non-ignorable evidence and switch answers when the surviving rival's prior relative to the commitment's exceeds (N-1-k)/(N-1).
eK6raLPN0M.evidence: Theorems on non-ignorability and the threshold rule, experiments with prompted critics and scripted oracles on real model output distributions, a separate confidence study, and a pre-specified follow-up with a code-enforced decoder.
eK6raLPN0M.claimed_gains: The decoder gains 8.2 points over the unaided model with the strongest critic at the largest budget, but not reliably across critics and well below adopting the critic's answer.
eK6raLPN0M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between information gain and decision improvement useful and the theory mostly coherent, and note the combined theoretical and large empirical study.
eK6raLPN0M.main_concern: The theory assumes an infallible critic that never rejects the correct answer, and the negative empirical results do not isolate whether protocol violations, decoder misspecification, or missing selection evidence cause the failure.

4xVIVfLBxn.one_liner: Penalizes hidden-state covariance spectra with a likelihood-gated Renyi-2, spectral-entropy, or ridge Log-Det term to speed up grokking.
4xVIVfLBxn.problem: Overparameterized networks can memorize a small algorithmic training set long before they generalize.
4xVIVfLBxn.method: Applies a trace-based Renyi-2 proxy, spectral entropy, or ridge Log-Det to hidden-state covariance only as predictive confidence grows, with Log-Det computed exactly through the smaller of the batch Gram and feature covariance matrices via Sylvester's identity.
4xVIVfLBxn.key_idea: Compress the hidden-state covariance spectrum, gated by predictive confidence, so the network reuses a concentrated set of representational directions across examples.
4xVIVfLBxn.evidence: A fixed six-task algorithmic suite with matched comparisons, bootstrap intervals, full-run ModAdd trajectories, and UCI Superconductivity regression; reviews mention matched seeds and a five-seed MNIST extension.
4xVIVfLBxn.claimed_gains: ASR lowered 15 of 18 task-objective means and won 66 of 87 matched comparisons, cutting the required data fraction by 7.37 percentage points on average (95% stratified bootstrap interval [5.71, 9.27]), or 11.40% relative.
4xVIVfLBxn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea good and the execution comprehensive, with substantial improvements in controlled settings (multiple regularizers, tasks, matched seeds) reported with explicit protocols.
4xVIVfLBxn.main_concern: Evidence comes from small datasets and networks, and the gains may reflect general regularization (for example weight decay) rather than the spectral penalty, with some closely related grokking work missing.

9vFNz8qhBj.one_liner: Detects whether a document's ideas came from a human or AI by classifying discourse-role outlines instead of prose.
9vFNz8qhBj.problem: AI detectors identify who wrote the words, but emerging policies on AI use depend on who came up with the ideas.
9vFNz8qhBj.method: Documents are converted to outlines of items that each pair a discourse role with a brief paraphrased description, minimizing word-level overlap with the text. IdeaLens is trained on 1M FineWeb documents with silver labels from the prose detector Pangram.
9vFNz8qhBj.key_idea: Training a detector on paraphrased discourse-role outlines with prose-detector silver labels forces the labels to be fit through ideas instead of surface wording.
9vFNz8qhBj.evidence: A controlled study writing from human versus AI plans, a new dataset of 50 stories that humans wrote from AI-generated plans, and 19 existing detection benchmarks.
9vFNz8qhBj.claimed_gains: AI flag rate drops from 95% to 7% as models write from more detailed human plans while Pangram 4 still flags 92%, and on 50 human-written stories from AI plans IdeaLens flags 68% as AI versus 8% for Pangram 4.
9vFNz8qhBj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and ambitious, the evaluation is broad and rigorous with limitations acknowledged, and the new datasets and the IdeaLens versus ProseLens control are useful.
9vFNz8qhBj.main_concern: The classifier may exploit artifacts of the LLM outline pipeline instead of idea provenance, and performance is imperfect (32% of AI-planned human stories missed and 8.2% false positives on LLM-polished human abstracts).

wwHFoX9QWl.one_liner: Merges hypernetwork-generated LoRAs continually by averaging in hypernetwork coordinates under an activation-induced metric.
wwHFoX9QWl.problem: In streaming settings, keeping every hypernetwork-generated LoRA grows storage and spreads information across adapters, and weight-space merging ignores the shared hypernetwork.
wwHFoX9QWl.method: MOSAIC measures adapter differences through layer-output contributions on frozen target-model activation probes and pulls this metric back to hypernetwork coordinates through the frozen decoder's Jacobian, giving a matrix-weighted barycenter with additive sufficient statistics. Covariance shrinkage stabilizes the accumulated metric.
wwHFoX9QWl.key_idea: Pulling an activation-induced adapter metric back through the decoder's Jacobian gives a matrix-weighted barycenter in latent coordinates with additive statistics, so memory stays independent of stream length.
wwHFoX9QWl.evidence: Experiments across multiple hypernetwork-based LoRA generation families and target LLMs, plus an approximation error bound (Section 5.2 per reviews).
wwHFoX9QWl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is interesting and the formulation is coherent, reducing to a matrix-weighted quadratic problem that supports one-pass updates with storage independent of stream length.
wwHFoX9QWl.main_concern: The contribution of each component is unclear: ablations do not isolate latent merging, activation matching and Jacobian weighting, the full metric does not consistently beat latent averaging, and the formulation resembles Fisher-weighted averaging and RegMean.

BUZpPGPXq4.one_liner: Aligns the Markov state abstraction training objective with the original theoretical conditions to learn coarser abstractions.
BUZpPGPXq4.problem: Current Markov state abstraction implementations satisfy a stronger kinematic-inseparability condition, producing over-refined abstractions that keep all transition regularities in the observation.
BUZpPGPXq4.method: The authors derive a training objective that matches the original theoretical MSA conditions, which makes the representation Markov but does not guarantee minimality, and add a heuristic that pushes the representation toward minimality.
BUZpPGPXq4.key_idea: Replace the kinematic-inseparability-style objective with one enforcing only the original sufficient Markov conditions, plus a heuristic to shrink the representation toward minimality.
BUZpPGPXq4.evidence: Experiments in pixel-based domains, including toy experiments and offline and online RL settings per reviewers.
BUZpPGPXq4.claimed_gains: Learned abstractions recover the underlying complexity of the problem and improve downstream performance; no numbers stated.
BUZpPGPXq4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is interesting, and those listing strengths find the approach clear, the mismatch between theory and prior objective precisely identified, and the toy experiments illuminating.
BUZpPGPXq4.main_concern: Nothing shows the abstraction preserves optimal-policy learning, comparisons with deep representation-learning baselines are missing, and the memoryless formulation is not positioned against history-based approaches.

t9GJpyE2n0.one_liner: Explorer policies trained with a novelty bonus are filtered and distilled into a student trained without it, over rounds.
t9GJpyE2n0.problem: Strong novelty incentives in RLVR have seen limited success and can degrade model quality in ways that are hard to recover from.
t9GJpyE2n0.method: ExpDis trains one or more explorer policies with a novelty bonus in the reward, filters their trajectories for correctness and quality, and distills them into a separate student policy that is trained without the bonus. The procedure repeats for several rounds, alternating exploration and optimization.
t9GJpyE2n0.key_idea: Keep the novelty bonus only in explorer policies and transfer their filtered correct trajectories to a student via SFT, so the student is never directly pushed toward novelty.
t9GJpyE2n0.evidence: Seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model families, compared with DAPO at the same wall-clock budget, with pass@k scaling up to pass@64 and a novelty-weight sensitivity analysis.
t9GJpyE2n0.claimed_gains: Outperforms DAPO at the same wall-clock budget across seven math benchmarks and two model families, with improved pass@k scaling; no numbers stated.
t9GJpyE2n0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating exploration from optimization is an elegant idea that gives improvements across two model families.
t9GJpyE2n0.main_concern: The pipeline is complex, student SFT compute may not be matched in the DAPO baseline, and closely related decoupling methods (R2PO, ICE) are not compared.

oqoEWLLDqZ.one_liner: Teacher-guided propositional trees transfer visual state abstractions and action values, then refine them online in new layouts.
oqoEWLLDqZ.problem: Value-driven source abstractions can encode layout-specific distinctions that hinder transfer to environments sharing task semantics.
oqoEWLLDqZ.method: NeuSAT learns a visual abstraction tree and policy, then distills their partition into a tree routed by automatically generated semantic propositions. It transfers the propositional tree and action values as a policy prior, updating values and locally refining the tree during target interaction.
oqoEWLLDqZ.key_idea: Rebuild a source visual abstraction with semantic proposition routing, transfer its action values, and refine the resulting tree online.
oqoEWLLDqZ.evidence: Experiments evaluate zero-shot transfer and online adaptation across discrete grid environments with deterministic rendering.
oqoEWLLDqZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motivated transition from source-specific visual abstractions to transferable symbolic rules with target adaptation.
oqoEWLLDqZ.main_concern: Missing baselines with the same parser and proposition vocabulary leave the teacher-guided pipeline's benefit over symbolic input alone unclear.

i1h0zQU3cl.one_liner: Depth attention selectively aggregates recent intermediate representations across repeated transformer blocks.
i1h0zQU3cl.problem: Standard residual connections merge recurrent-depth information into one stream without selective reuse of intermediate representations.
i1h0zQU3cl.method: ARLoop applies attention residuals to looped transformers so each layer attends over representations from model depth. A sliding window restricts this aggregation to recent depth history.
i1h0zQU3cl.key_idea: Replace a single residual stream with attention over intermediate representations from a sliding window of recurrent depth.
i1h0zQU3cl.evidence: Controlled experiments use 140M and 370M models with recurrence depths R=1--5, followed by 0.6B and 1.3B pretraining experiments and math and coding evaluations.
i1h0zQU3cl.claimed_gains: The 1.3B model pretrained on 0.5T tokens with three recurrences outperforms Huginn-3.5B across all evaluated tasks.
i1h0zQU3cl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find selective residual reuse interesting and value experiments examining how much recurrent history the model needs.
i1h0zQU3cl.main_concern: The sliding-window conclusions need stronger support across residual-history settings and recurrence depths, with uncertainty estimates for small performance differences.

zOpNGKdbY0.one_liner: Synthetic identity replacement and multi-recording adversarial training reduce linkage leakage in clinical speech embeddings.
zOpNGKdbY0.problem: Combining multiple recordings can reveal participant identity even when individual released embeddings appear private.
zOpNGKdbY0.method: MoIRAGE separates clinical content from identity-related information, replaces the original identity component with a synthetic alternative, and generates released embeddings. It trains against multi-recording linkage attacks while enforcing clinical consistency and diversity, without diagnosis labels at inference.
zOpNGKdbY0.key_idea: Replace identity-related embedding components with synthetic identities while training against attackers that jointly inspect multiple recordings.
zOpNGKdbY0.evidence: Evaluation uses the UNMC clinical speech dataset with five participant-disjoint outer folds covering 137 participants, including 127 with clinical labels, and multiple linkage attacks.
zOpNGKdbY0.claimed_gains: MoIRAGE achieves clinical-task AUROC of 0.643 compared with 0.567 for the original embeddings.
zOpNGKdbY0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focus on identity leakage accumulated across repeated recordings and the extensive attack evaluation.
zOpNGKdbY0.main_concern: Comparisons omit existing identity-replacement approaches, so the experiments do not establish an advantage over closely related methods.

S7QxxP5hFE.one_liner: Centered kernel distance admits unbiased estimation with error bounds accounting jointly for sampled neurons and experimental conditions.
S7QxxP5hFE.problem: Existing representation-similarity analyses lack realistic bounds that jointly capture neuron and experimental-condition subsampling.
S7QxxP5hFE.method: The paper studies centered kernel distance as a metric counterpart to CKA and RSA and derives an unbiased estimator. It bounds estimation error under assumptions on response scale and moments, considering both neuron and condition counts.
S7QxxP5hFE.key_idea: Use centered kernel distance to obtain unbiased estimation and bound error jointly in the numbers of neurons and experimental conditions.
S7QxxP5hFE.evidence: Theoretical results receive empirical checks in random shallow networks, trained neural networks, and macaque visual cortex data.
S7QxxP5hFE.claimed_gains: Under mild assumptions, CKD estimation error decays in proportion to 1/M + 1/N, with no experimental-condition dimensionality dependence in the rate.
S7QxxP5hFE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear statistical formulation and theoretical analysis of representation-comparison error.
S7QxxP5hFE.main_concern: The dimension-free rate may conceal dimension-dependent constants, so claims of avoiding the curse of dimensionality need qualification and broader validation.

zupJY6d00x.one_liner: Security bounds and black-box spoofing attacks examine how reused watermark randomness leaks information across generation contexts.
zupJY6d00x.problem: The relationship between formal watermark security and practical attacks remains unclear, especially for general design flaws versus implementation weaknesses.
zupJY6d00x.method: The paper connects spoofing resistance to undetectability under an additional terminal verification query and derives a bound exposing randomness-reuse effects. It tests SynthID-Text attacks that exploit either public hash-bucket equivalence or exact-context reuse.
zupJY6d00x.key_idea: Pool watermark observations across contexts sharing randomness, separating implementation-specific hash equivalence from reuse induced by repeated contexts.
zupJY6d00x.evidence: SynthID-Text experiments use Gemma-2B and Gemma-9B, held-out prompts, Qwen2.5-Instruct quality judges, and hash-patching and bucket-permutation controls.
zupJY6d00x.claimed_gains: At 450 tokens, the implementation-specific attack reaches joint detection-and-quality rates of 94.1% and 67.6% on Gemma-2B and Gemma-9B under a 32B judge, and 97.5% and 85.2% under its 7B counterpart.
zupJY6d00x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the concrete hash-bucket vulnerability and the connection between security analysis and practical spoofing experiments.
zupJY6d00x.main_concern: The strongest attacks depend on a particular public implementation, limiting generalization to other watermark implementations and designs.

RkmN93BOxy.one_liner: Ordinal-regression reward modeling on human-scored three-dimensional editing triplets automates instruction-guided video editing evaluation.
RkmN93BOxy.problem: Instruction-guided video editing lacks both a large-scale human-scored dataset of complete editing triplets and a specialized automated evaluator, relying instead on manual inspection or generic VLM judges.
RkmN93BOxy.method: The authors build VEFX-Dataset with 5,049 video editing examples across 9 categories and 32 subcategories annotated by humans along Instruction Following, Rendering Quality, and Edit Exclusivity, plus the 300-pair VEFX-Bench. They train VEFX-Reward to jointly process the source video, instruction, and edited video and predict per-dimension quality scores via ordinal regression.
RkmN93BOxy.key_idea: Train an ordinal-regression reward model over source video, instruction, and edited video using decoupled human scores for instruction, rendering, and exclusivity.
RkmN93BOxy.evidence: Evaluations test VEFX-Reward against generic VLM judges, prior reward models, and a same-backbone SFT baseline across 10 editing models and unseen systems with multi-rater consistency checks.
RkmN93BOxy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling instruction following, rendering quality, and edit exclusivity in a calibrated multi-rater dataset and dedicated evaluator fills a clear video-editing evaluation gap.
RkmN93BOxy.main_concern: Reviewers point out unspecified conditional-versus-cumulative probability handling in the ordinal objective, an overbroad visual-effects title without VFX-specific metrics, and no post-training experiment showing VEFX-Reward improves generators.

NZybxmI9Ek.one_liner: Emotion-vector probing and steering compare valence geometry with refusal behavior, attack trajectories, and verbal self-report.
NZybxmI9Ek.problem: The relationship between internal emotion representations, behavioral influence, and reported states remains unclear.
NZybxmI9Ek.method: The study maps emotion representations onto valence and arousal across model layers and training stages. It combines activation probes, steering interventions, multi-turn attack analysis, and conflicting textual cues to compare behavior with self-report.
NZybxmI9Ek.key_idea: Use a common valence coordinate to compare activation geometry, steering-induced behavior, and verbal endorsement of emotion labels.
NZybxmI9Ek.evidence: Experiments span 171 emotions and 15 models, including injected-emotion decoding across seven models and multi-turn attack trajectories.
NZybxmI9Ek.claimed_gains: Valence has R²=0.59–0.80 versus 0.39–0.70 for arousal and correlates with refusal at ρ=-0.82, while injected identity decodes at 99.5–100% but Qwen3.5-9B endorses negative labels in 5.9% of comparisons versus 91.9% for positive labels.
NZybxmI9Ek.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad cross-model study and evidence that internally decodable information need not appear in verbal self-report.
NZybxmI9Ek.main_concern: Emotion-specific interpretations remain insufficiently separated from narrative-topic confounds and pre-existing positive-label preferences.

cLFmDOSJvL.one_liner: Electro-Prot learns protein embeddings by predicting continuous Poisson–Boltzmann electrostatic fields through coordinate-to-atom cross-attention.
cLFmDOSJvL.problem: Sequence and structure pretraining do not explicitly model electrostatic interactions relevant to protein function.
cLFmDOSJvL.method: A 6.7 million-parameter encoder-decoder transformer predicts electrostatic potentials at arbitrary points around a protein. Coordinate queries cross-attend to atomic inputs, and learned embeddings support downstream tasks alone or combined with PLM embeddings.
cLFmDOSJvL.key_idea: Supervise protein representations with continuous electrostatic-potential predictions at coordinate queries that attend to atoms.
cLFmDOSJvL.evidence: Held-out electrostatic-field prediction and downstream protein-interfacing and mutation-induced binding-energy tasks test the representations and their fusion with PLM embeddings.
cLFmDOSJvL.claimed_gains: Electro-Prot attains r=0.969 and MAE = 0.81 kT/e on a held-out test set.
cLFmDOSJvL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find electrostatic supervision physically motivated and the compact model's downstream results promising.
cLFmDOSJvL.main_concern: The experiments do not separate electrostatic supervision from the advantage of richer atomic coordinates, partial charges, and radii.

hOogvtHd0H.one_liner: RecallGate evaluates cumulative KV-sharing substitutions on visual-recall probes to preserve object–attribute binding during cache compression.
hOogvtHd0H.problem: Similarity-based sharing gates and aggregate VQA scores can miss losses in specific visual capabilities.
hOogvtHd0H.method: The audit compares static and cumulative representation-similarity criteria under controlled sharing operations and cache-reduction budgets. RecallGate temporarily installs each substitution and accepts it based on a small recall battery evaluated on the cumulative configuration.
hOogvtHd0H.key_idea: Test each proposed KV substitution within the already modified model using a capability-specific visual-recall acceptance battery.
hOogvtHd0H.evidence: Cross-family evaluations compare reconstructed sharing methods and acceptance rules at matched cache budgets, with object–attribute binding and aggregate visual task measures.
hOogvtHd0H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that similarity and aggregate accuracy can conceal severe capability-specific compression failures.
hOogvtHd0H.main_concern: Repeated gating and evaluation on closely related synthetic binding templates risk adaptive overfitting and do not establish real-image generalization.

Iij0Gg7Hg5.one_liner: Controlled loss-weighting interventions reveal how target length changes the relative training weight of synthetic reasoning questions.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.problem: Comparisons of reasoning-data recipes conflate target content with the implicit question weighting induced by token-mean loss.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.method: The study constructs fixed-depth and mixed-depth targets from the same teacher pool and questions, then changes token-mean versus equal-example loss while holding targets fixed. Shared-weight and group-share controls probe whether weighting alone explains recipe differences.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.key_idea: Hold reasoning targets fixed while changing per-question loss weights to isolate length-induced weighting effects.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.evidence: Experiments use 11,853 shared questions, Qwen3-4B-Base and OLMo-3-7B students, four evaluation benchmarks, and three seeds per arm.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.claimed_gains: Equal-example weighting costs the mixed-depth corpus 8.6 and 5.5 accuracy points, expanding the fixed-depth lead from 1.6 to 9.9 and from 3.1 to 8.3 points.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled comparison of loss weighting and the shared-question-weight interventions.
Iij0Gg7Hg5.main_concern: Remaining attention-kernel differences and incomplete optimization tuning weaken causal attribution in some comparisons.

GRzdxu8H6O.one_liner: Elliptic schedules and tailored discretization use complex ODE analyticity to design condition-aware generative sampling.
GRzdxu8H6O.problem: Stochastic-interpolant sampling lacks a joint principled choice of interpolation schedule and probability-flow ODE discretization.
GRzdxu8H6O.method: Conformal mapping yields variance-preserving schedules parameterized by Jacobi elliptic functions and the target condition number. Zoloflow pairs these schedules with a discretization connected to Zolotarev rational approximation.
GRzdxu8H6O.key_idea: Optimize the analyticity region of complexified sampling trajectories and use its elliptic structure to choose schedules and discretization.
GRzdxu8H6O.evidence: Gaussian minimax bounds, log-concave sampling guarantees, Gaussian experiments, and learned-field image experiments evaluate the construction.
GRzdxu8H6O.claimed_gains: For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow reaches total-variation error ε with Θ(log κ log(√d/ε)) exact score queries, minimax-optimal among oblivious score-span algorithms.
GRzdxu8H6O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the rigorous Gaussian analysis and the connection between interpolation schedules and rational approximation.
GRzdxu8H6O.main_concern: Exact-score Gaussian guarantees do not establish a practical advantage for the proposed discretization on learned, non-Gaussian generative models.

86NMDsHvJT.one_liner: Hedge-Bench evaluates forecasts against resolved outcomes and analyst-derived research rubrics, then trains agents with turn-level GRPO credit.
86NMDsHvJT.problem: Agents' document-handling competence does not establish their ability to forecast uncertain future events from incomplete information.
86NMDsHvJT.method: Hedge-Bench derives tasks from hedge-fund analysts' reasoning traces and freezes the information available to agents. It evaluates research coverage and realized forecast correctness, while Muse-Glimmer training uses GRPO with turn-level credit assignment.
86NMDsHvJT.key_idea: Pair frozen evidence snapshots with analyst-derived research rubrics and subsequently resolved prediction questions.
86NMDsHvJT.evidence: The benchmark contains 92 tasks evaluated across 11 models with three trials each, and training uses 165 environments with 22 held-out tasks.
86NMDsHvJT.claimed_gains: Held-out coverage rises from 17.17% to 33.36% at low effort and from 30.19% to 47.02% at extra-high effort, with 47.9% fewer accepted trajectory tokens for the low-effort comparison and a 10.06 percentage-point forecasting gain at high effort.
86NMDsHvJT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the real analyst discussions, frozen environments, and separate evaluation of research quality and forecast accuracy.
86NMDsHvJT.main_concern: The forecasting evidence does not show that better research coverage yields better predictions, particularly against simple constant-answer baselines.

Ui2V1tDmNJ.one_liner: SIGMA turns a Model Spec into self-generated alignment tasks and training signals for safety adaptation.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.problem: Alignment training depends on stronger teachers or curated supervision while capability self-improvement can outpace safety training.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.method: The candidate model synthesizes spec-guided dilemma scenarios and training tasks, then supplies verification and supervision for its own adaptation. The pipeline studies supervised and reinforcement-learning variants and evaluates them with external graders.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.key_idea: Use the same model to convert behavioral specifications into alignment scenarios, checks, and self-training supervision.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.evidence: Reviewers describe single-base-model experiments transferring single-turn training to multi-turn agentic alignment benchmarks with external evaluation.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reducing reliance on stronger models and human annotation by generating alignment supervision from a Model Spec.
Ui2V1tDmNJ.main_concern: The evidence does not establish broad self-improvement beyond one model and training round or transfer to previously unseen alignment failure modes.

kY0EvTgJsL.one_liner: KVM combines block-local attention with compressed key-value memory that can remain fixed or expand on a chosen schedule.
kY0EvTgJsL.problem: Full attention incurs growing memory costs, while fixed-state recurrent models sacrifice long-context recall.
kY0EvTgJsL.method: KVM updates a block-recurrent state by compressing incoming tokens into existing slots or appending selected tokens. Standard operations support chunk-wise parallel training and prefill with adjustable memory growth.
kY0EvTgJsL.key_idea: Merge incoming key-value entries into compressed memory slots and append selected tokens according to a configurable expansion schedule.
kY0EvTgJsL.evidence: Reviewers describe long-context and needle-in-a-haystack comparisons, RULER evaluations at 120M and 350M scales, architectural ablations, and efficiency measurements.
kY0EvTgJsL.claimed_gains: Fixed-size KVM has O(N) complexity, while expansion permits prefill complexities between O(N) and O(N²), including subquadratic prefill with sublinear state growth.
kY0EvTgJsL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical architecture's adjustable trade-off between local exact attention, historical memory, and recall.
kY0EvTgJsL.main_concern: The specific benefit of KVM's memory-update and expansion choices remains insufficiently isolated from capacity changes and related designs.

2y1wpPfoAv.one_liner: MAS-BIT sends soft token-embedding messages from neural and phonetic experts to an arbiter for differentiable brain-to-text decoding.
2y1wpPfoAv.problem: End-to-end intracortical speech decoders have lagged cascaded systems in transcription accuracy.
2y1wpPfoAv.method: A neural agent interprets continuous recordings and a phonetic agent decodes soft phoneme posteriors, while an arbiter integrates both with direct neural access. Probability-weighted token embeddings preserve alternatives and let sentence-level supervision jointly train the components.
2y1wpPfoAv.key_idea: Communicate expert token distributions as weighted embedding messages so an arbiter can combine alternatives and backpropagate transcription supervision.
2y1wpPfoAv.evidence: Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks compare end-to-end and cascaded decoding, with single-agent and message-format controls discussed by reviewers.
2y1wpPfoAv.claimed_gains: MAS-BIT reports word error rates of 6.929% on '24, 3.606% on the '25 public test set, and 3.892% on its private test set.
2y1wpPfoAv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the useful combination of specialized neural and phonetic evidence through differentiable latent communication.
2y1wpPfoAv.main_concern: The comparisons do not isolate expert specialization from extra adapters, intermediate supervision, and repeated decoding.

C4VFESNXLV.one_liner: Historical-image selection and action-credit redistribution train agents to revisit candidates during compositional image refinement.
C4VFESNXLV.problem: Iterative image editing can degrade previously satisfied constraints when agents always continue from the latest image.
C4VFESNXLV.method: GenRevisit jointly selects the image to continue from and the editing action, using SFT followed by agentic reinforcement learning. NACA redistributes positive trajectory advantage according to each action's reduction of the remaining objective.
C4VFESNXLV.key_idea: Let the agent select earlier image states and weight positive learning credit by each action's contribution toward remaining objectives.
C4VFESNXLV.evidence: GenEval2 results, controlled teacher experiments, matched-prefix comparisons, and transfer to Z-Image-Turbo support the framework.
C4VFESNXLV.claimed_gains: GenRevisit reports a GenEval2 GM score of 84.3 with Qwen-Image-2512.
C4VFESNXLV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that revisiting historical images addresses damage caused by non-monotonic editing.
C4VFESNXLV.main_concern: Missing search, related refinement, and simpler credit-assignment baselines leave the specific contribution of the learned policy and NACA uncertain.

eHwcpYaVga.one_liner: Representation-conditioned observation-space flows transport source details toward target codes without an explicit reconstruction objective.
eHwcpYaVga.problem: Compact representations should discard presentation details, but reconstruction-based decoders require those details to recover observations.
eHwcpYaVga.method: PairedFM jointly learns representations and observation-space flows from ordered pairs sampled from one distribution. Generation starts from a source observation and follows a flow indexed by source and target representations.
eHwcpYaVga.key_idea: Learn representations through velocity prediction while transporting full observations under paired representation conditioning.
eHwcpYaVga.evidence: Identifiability and recovery guarantees accompany empirical studies on synthetic or simple datasets, including branching fractals and grouped factor transfer.
eHwcpYaVga.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the joint transport-representation formulation and theoretical connections between flow loss, recoverability, and generation.
eHwcpYaVga.main_concern: The generation comparisons provide limited evidence of practical superiority because conditioning differs across baselines and realistic modern generative benchmarks are absent.

7HPFlaMcTZ.one_liner: Controlled training-size sweeps separate tabular model scaling from distribution shift and validation-set choice.
7HPFlaMcTZ.problem: Large-scale tabular learning lacks controlled evidence about how more data affects performance under realistic distribution shifts.
7HPFlaMcTZ.method: The study compares GBDTs, MLP-based models, and tabular foundation models across training sizes with ID controls. It tests target-aligned validation for tuning and early stopping against ID validation and context augmentation.
7HPFlaMcTZ.key_idea: Vary training-set size within tasks while controlling distribution shift and the validation signal used for model selection.
7HPFlaMcTZ.evidence: Experiments cover eight datasets with up to ten million examples, natural temporal and query-based shifts, and 10-seed MLP evaluations.
7HPFlaMcTZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled ID/OOD scaling study across major tabular model families.
7HPFlaMcTZ.main_concern: Limited model-family and training-configuration coverage constrains how broadly the scaling findings apply.

Z7JKlRfoZ1.one_liner: Symplectic leapfrog updates replace unconstrained JEPA predictors with action-conditioned Hamiltonian dynamics over position and momentum latents.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.problem: Unconstrained autoregressive world-model predictors can contract latent distributions during long rollouts.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.method: LeHami learns an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow over structured position and momentum latents and integrates it with an exactly symplectic leapfrog step. Temporal derivatives of learned positions provide the momentum-like component.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.key_idea: Derive momentum-like latents from temporal position derivatives and advance both through a learned Hamiltonian with symplectic leapfrog integration.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.evidence: Volume-preservation guarantees and fixed-encoder predictor comparisons cover pixel-based pendulums, a mass-spring system, a two-body system, and a cart pole.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.claimed_gains: LeHami has the best long-horizon position accuracy on four of the five environments and velocity accuracy on three among the three compared predictors.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value integrating structured Hamiltonian dynamics and symplectic updates into latent world models.
Z7JKlRfoZ1.main_concern: Ambient volume preservation does not by itself establish preservation of the data manifold or explain practical world-model benefits.

sxpc4Z5zxv.one_liner: Finite gradient-descent trajectory supervision yields phase transitions in learned iterative reasoning and distinct overthinking mechanisms.
sxpc4Z5zxv.problem: Theory poorly explains how finite chain-of-thought supervision affects reasoning beyond the training horizon.
sxpc4Z5zxv.method: An in-context weight-prediction model trains on finite linear-regression gradient-descent trajectories. High-dimensional asymptotics characterize stability regimes and distinguish error accumulation from amplification.
sxpc4Z5zxv.key_idea: Analyze repeated learned state updates as training context and trajectory supervision vary to separate accumulated errors from unstable error amplification.
sxpc4Z5zxv.evidence: Asymptotic theory and experiments with fully trained linear and multi-head softmax attention support qualitative long-horizon failure regimes.
sxpc4Z5zxv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value linking finite trajectory supervision to long-horizon stability and distinguishing accumulation from amplification.
sxpc4Z5zxv.main_concern: The structured linear-regression teacher and restricted student support narrower conclusions than general claims about LLM chain-of-thought reasoning.

vSmAgYMj3K.one_liner: Sampling learned lower probability bounds converts residual distribution mass into abstention during language generation.
vSmAgYMj3K.problem: Language models need scalable selective prediction that separates epistemic uncertainty from ordinary output variability.
vSmAgYMj3K.method: Infrasampling samples from a lower bound on the predictive distribution and treats leftover mass as abstention. New autoregressive output heads learn epistemic uncertainty about a teacher distribution through soft distillation.
vSmAgYMj3K.key_idea: Replace average-density sampling with sampling from tokenwise lower probability bounds, assigning the remaining probability mass to abstention.
vSmAgYMj3K.evidence: Synthetic chess with exact verification and real-text soft-distillation experiments compare hallucination-abstention tradeoffs against heuristic baselines.
vSmAgYMj3K.reviewer_consensus: Positive reviews value the simple lower-bound sampling mechanism and the synthetic chess evaluation.
vSmAgYMj3K.main_concern: Limited comparisons with relevant hallucination-detection and abstention methods leave the method's advantage over existing approaches unclear.

gxVCzSV3rw.one_liner: Causal reasoning interventions diagnose driving-VLA misalignment, while validated code rewards train scene-grounded reasoning-trajectory consistency.
gxVCzSV3rw.problem: Driving VLAs can produce plausible textual explanations that do not align with or causally influence their trajectories.
gxVCzSV3rw.method: The paper probes Alpamayo using masking, clause reordering, paraphrasing, and other interventions to build a multi-axis faithfulness benchmark. TRACR applies GRPO with validated code-generated rewards for scene grounding and logical consistency.
gxVCzSV3rw.key_idea: Probe reasoning-to-action dependence with controlled interventions, then post-train with code-subtask rewards checking scene-grounded reasoning and trajectory consistency.
gxVCzSV3rw.evidence: Alpamayo intervention studies and held-out OOD driving scenarios compare TRACR against deterministic-rule and LLM-judge RL baselines.
gxVCzSV3rw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing reasoning-action agreement from causal faithfulness through varied controlled interventions.
gxVCzSV3rw.main_concern: Rewards and reported gains establish agreement more clearly than causal faithfulness, with worsened paraphrase invariance complicating the main claim.

vBEHc2BwYa.one_liner: PCA-based vector-field discovery identifies continuous symmetries and extends Lie-derivative regularization from invariance to equivariance.
vBEHc2BwYa.problem: Existing vector-field symmetry methods use heuristic selection criteria and underexplore nonlinear equivariance and scalability.
vBEHc2BwYa.method: The method uses PCA and SVD to improve symmetry discovery and select dimensions by explained variance. It extends Lie-derivative-based discovery and regularization to equivariance.
vBEHc2BwYa.key_idea: Find low-variation vector-field directions with PCA and impose Lie-derivative constraints relating input and output transformations.
vBEHc2BwYa.evidence: Symmetry-discovery benchmarks and out-of-sample generalization experiments test runtime, accuracy, and vector-field regularization.
vBEHc2BwYa.claimed_gains: The abstract reports at least an order of magnitude faster computation than competing methods.
vBEHc2BwYa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the computational efficiency of PCA-based symmetry discovery.
vBEHc2BwYa.main_concern: Predefined nonlinear bases and matched input-output generators require strong prior knowledge and restrict what the method discovers.

F5X4b3vdlh.one_liner: Spectral analysis of linear-network learning separates compositional laws that are unidentifiable from those that merely emerge slowly.
F5X4b3vdlh.problem: Knowing individual premises does not explain when a learner can compose them or whether available evidence determines the composition.
F5X4b3vdlh.method: The paper analyzes shallow and deep linear networks in structured synthetic relational environments. It links evidence structure to identifiability and learning trajectories, including the effects of adding linking facts.
F5X4b3vdlh.key_idea: Analyze relational-law identifiability and spectral learning dynamics separately to determine which compositions evidence permits and when networks retrieve them.
F5X4b3vdlh.evidence: Mathematical results and controlled synthetic experiments compare predicted and observed compositional learning, including networks with one, two, and three layers.
F5X4b3vdlh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit distinction between insufficient evidence and slow learning as causes of compositional failure.
F5X4b3vdlh.main_concern: Reviewers agree that linear networks and simple relational environments leave applicability to nonlinear models untested.

dj6Cf3ohHM.one_liner: PALMU updates the labeling model, regenerates pseudo-labels and selections, then corrects the downstream classifier after labeled-record deletion.
dj6Cf3ohHM.problem: Deleted labeled records can retain influence through stored pseudo-labels and selection decisions in self-training.
dj6Cf3ohHM.method: PALMU updates the labeling model on retained data and regenerates confidence-filtered supervision for the unlabeled pool. It then updates the downstream classifier without training both models to convergence.
dj6Cf3ohHM.key_idea: Regenerate deletion-affected pseudo-labels and confidence-based inclusion decisions before correcting the downstream classifier.
dj6Cf3ohHM.evidence: Fixed-representation theory bounds distance from full retraining, and four-dataset experiments evaluate deletion ratios of 5%, 10%, 20%, and 30%.
dj6Cf3ohHM.claimed_gains: PALMU meets agreement and utility criteria in 397 of 400 requests, lowers mean predictive total variation by 4.3 to 56.6 times versus the closest baseline, and retains 1.56 to 1.83 macro F1 points over labeled-only retraining on CommitBERT.
dj6Cf3ohHM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate addressing deleted records' indirect influence through generated supervision and the evidence of agreement with retraining.
dj6Cf3ohHM.main_concern: Reviewers agree that reliance on fixed, deletion-independent representations limits applicability when deleted data also affects the encoder.

5lR5j3jlMI.one_liner: LITE drops and reconstructs tokens separately at each hierarchical PDE-transformer stage while retaining dense latent processing.
5lR5j3jlMI.problem: High-resolution structured-grid PDE transformers face training-time and memory costs that restrict feasible three-dimensional models.
5lR5j3jlMI.method: Each encoder and decoder stage keeps one token per spatial block using an L2-norm score and processes only that subset. A depthwise spread convolution and learned fusion restore dropped positions using dense residual features before the next stage.
5lR5j3jlMI.key_idea: Repeat blockwise token selection, sparse processing, and dense reconstruction at each stage while keeping the latent stage dense.
5lR5j3jlMI.evidence: Experiments cover a 16-equation 2D benchmark and 3D structured-grid settings, including KdV volumes and comparisons with dense and whole-network dropping baselines.
5lR5j3jlMI.claimed_gains: In 2D, LITE halves wall-clock training time while reducing normalized RMSE by 23% on a 16-equation benchmark.
5lR5j3jlMI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method offers practical reductions in training cost and GPU memory for structured-grid PDE surrogates.
5lR5j3jlMI.main_concern: Reviewers question comparison fairness because architectural and tuning differences and missing memory-saving baselines obscure the gains attributable to token dropping.

bhCrdxOJ2D.one_liner: Endpoint decomposition explains why empirical closed-form flow couplings retain initialization noise and poorly supervise few-step generators.
bhCrdxOJ2D.problem: Closed-form empirical flow fields avoid teacher pretraining but produce much weaker few-step students than learned-teacher couplings.
bhCrdxOJ2D.method: The paper compares closed-form, random, and learned-teacher pairings and derives an endpoint identity separating initial noise from accumulated drift. Drift bounds and empirical diffusion collapse-time scaling characterize the informative coupling component.
bhCrdxOJ2D.key_idea: Decompose closed-form endpoints into initialization noise plus drift, then bound drift energy relative to endpoint energy.
bhCrdxOJ2D.evidence: Exact identities and drift bounds accompany matched-student comparisons on three natural-image datasets and experiments varying data dimension.
bhCrdxOJ2D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the negative result useful and appreciate the diagnostics and theoretical account of noise retention.
bhCrdxOJ2D.main_concern: Reviewers question whether small drift energy explains learnability and the advantage of learned-teacher couplings.

KnNCDECrXt.one_liner: CrossTF learns late-stage fusion of frozen time- and frequency-view denoisers using extreme-value objectives under a distributional constraint.
KnNCDECrXt.problem: Time-series generators struggle to preserve rare extremes without damaging overall distributional fidelity.
KnNCDECrXt.method: CrossTF trains and freezes time- and frequency-view denoisers, then learns step-specific fusion parameters in a late denoising window. An Extreme Value Theory objective permits interpolation or extrapolation between clean-sample estimates under an energy-distance constraint.
KnNCDECrXt.key_idea: Optimize late-stage movement along the difference between time- and frequency-view denoiser estimates while constraining energy distance.
KnNCDECrXt.evidence: Experiments cover seven real-world datasets and 11 baselines, with cross-view asymmetry analysis, window analysis, and single- and same-view ablations.
KnNCDECrXt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extreme-event generation problem and the breadth of empirical analysis.
KnNCDECrXt.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the analyses establish a specific advantage of time–frequency discrepancies over other denoiser-fusion directions.

KH8rKp1WyW.one_liner: Predictive contracts compare world-model text, generated motion, and physical references, while conditioning ladders test whether discrepancies can be repaired.
KH8rKp1WyW.problem: A multimodal world model can generate physical outcomes that contradict its textual forecasts or physical ground truth.
KH8rKp1WyW.method: The audit distinguishes internal alignment from physical correctness through matched event, magnitude, and timing contracts. Separate intervention ladders condition generation on model forecasts or physical references, and downstream tests filter supervision using forecasts.
KH8rKp1WyW.key_idea: Compare text and video against matched predictive contracts, then vary conditioning specificity to distinguish internal inconsistency from physical error.
KH8rKp1WyW.evidence: Controlled simulator studies with Cosmos3-Super and Cosmos3-Nano include 39/40 jointly valid text-correct/video-incorrect pairs and action-matched downstream push-planning controls.
KH8rKp1WyW.claimed_gains: Forecast-based action screening raises push-planning success from 0.338 to 0.635, while additional gains over the 0.615 matched-support control remain unresolved.
KH8rKp1WyW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distinction between internal consistency and physical correctness and the use of controlled evaluations.
KH8rKp1WyW.main_concern: Reviewers question generality beyond controlled simulator scenes and two checkpoints from the same model family.

gA0HpuoG9K.one_liner: Analytic noisy linear-RNN dynamics show how intrinsic noise breaks representational degeneracies and induces regularization-dependent phase transitions.
gA0HpuoG9K.problem: The effect of intrinsic neural noise on representation learning remains theoretically unclear.
gA0HpuoG9K.method: The paper analyzes a tractable linear recurrent network with white-noise inputs and intrinsic noise. It derives weight-alignment dynamics in the small-initialization regime and conditions under which noise makes non-degenerate solutions suboptimal.
gA0HpuoG9K.key_idea: Analyze the noise-averaged learning dynamics to expose how noise changes weight alignment and eliminates non-degenerate optima under scale constraints.
gA0HpuoG9K.evidence: Algebraic derivations establish learning dynamics and a critical-noise phase transition for a linear RNN with an exponential target filter.
gA0HpuoG9K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mathematical analysis clear and the account of noise-driven alignment and phase transitions interesting.
gA0HpuoG9K.main_concern: Reviewers note missing numerical and practical validation of the theory beyond the restrictive linear-RNN setting.

q6whzFSSwL.one_liner: Matched probabilistic diagnostics compare AI and numerical cyclone forecasts across tracks, intensity, calibration, and wind–pressure relationships.
q6whzFSSwL.problem: Strong average AI weather scores do not establish reliable probabilistic forecasting of tropical-cyclone extremes.
q6whzFSSwL.method: The study benchmarks GenCast, FourCastNet 3, and FGN against ECMWF IFS-ENS using common cyclone settings and probabilistic metrics. It examines intensity underestimation and rapid intensification, including debiasing and a Cyclone Alfred case study.
q6whzFSSwL.key_idea: Evaluate matched cyclone ensembles with separate track, intensity, calibration, and wind–pressure diagnostics rather than relying on aggregate forecast scores.
q6whzFSSwL.evidence: Evaluation covers 178 storms and compares probabilistic AI models with IFS-ENS, including paired 2025 storm results and Cyclone Alfred.
q6whzFSSwL.claimed_gains: FGN has the better track score than IFS-ENS on 90% of the 2025 storms.
q6whzFSSwL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the multi-diagnostic comparison of recent probabilistic AI models with an operational numerical ensemble.
q6whzFSSwL.main_concern: Reviewers question whether aggregate gains around selected storms establish performance during active extreme-intensity conditions.

IAbzUHzyEC.one_liner: A majorization–minimization solver fits item-response models through constrained matrix factorization for scalable, interpretable language-model evaluation.
IAbzUHzyEC.problem: Average accuracy ignores response stochasticity and item heterogeneity, while conventional item-response estimation can be expensive and unstable.
IAbzUHzyEC.method: The framework reformulates item-response parameter estimation as a sequence of constrained matrix-factorization subproblems. It analyzes identifiability and convergence and uses fitted abilities and item characteristics to interpret benchmarks.
IAbzUHzyEC.key_idea: Majorize the item-response objective and solve constrained matrix-factorization updates for model abilities and item parameters.
IAbzUHzyEC.evidence: Synthetic experiments and MATH-500 plus six Open LLM Leaderboard benchmarks test estimation accuracy, scalability, missingness, and ranking uncertainty.
IAbzUHzyEC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate addressing the practical cost of large-scale IRT fitting with theoretical analysis and extensive empirical comparisons.
IAbzUHzyEC.main_concern: Reviewers question item-difficulty identifiability because ability shifts can change item-intercept ordering without changing predicted probabilities.

FUpDz8VwWD.one_liner: Prefilling or banning common opening tokens tests whether reasoning initiation constrains measured chain-of-thought controllability.
FUpDz8VwWD.problem: Low measured chain-of-thought controllability may reflect default opening-token behavior rather than a general inability to control reasoning traces.
FUpDz8VwWD.method: The study intervenes on reasoning openings using prefilling and frequent-token bans with in-context examples. It separates addition and style control from suppression and compares their associations with monitorability.
FUpDz8VwWD.key_idea: Alter the first reasoning tokens to escape dominant default openings, then measure compliance for different control types.
FUpDz8VwWD.evidence: Across-model experiments use a suite of 240 question–control pairs covering 178 questions, alongside opening-token analyses and controllability–monitorability correlations.
FUpDz8VwWD.claimed_gains: Banning frequent opening tokens with in-context examples improves average compliance by 34-41 percentage points across models.
FUpDz8VwWD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that opening-token interventions reveal a concrete and actionable bottleneck in measured CoT compliance.
FUpDz8VwWD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the interventions isolate opening-token entropy from semantic prefix effects, particularly for suppression tasks.

EcT2XVgObU.one_liner: DiaCurate diagnoses agent behaviors, edits demonstrations, and retrains and re-diagnoses policies to detect collateral regressions.
EcT2XVgObU.problem: Outcome-filtered successful demonstrations can still teach inefficient search, verbosity, repetition, and poor evidence use.
EcT2XVgObU.method: DiaCurate applies targeted edits based on behavioral diagnostics and checks the retrained policy for regressions. Failed truncation interventions motivate an evidence-use refinement that aims to reduce unnecessary search without premature commitment.
EcT2XVgObU.key_idea: Close the curation loop by evaluating the behavior of retrained policies after targeted demonstration edits.
EcT2XVgObU.evidence: A deep-research agent on HLE and BrowseComp compares outcome-filtered SFT, truncation interventions, and evidence-use refinements using deterministic behavioral diagnostics.
EcT2XVgObU.claimed_gains: The refined policy reaches 35.2 and 34.1 avg@3 versus 33.5 and 33.3 for the reference on HLE and BrowseComp.
EcT2XVgObU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the concrete demonstration that outcome-filtered SFT can improve accuracy while worsening agent behavior.
EcT2XVgObU.main_concern: Reviewers question gain attribution and reliability because interventions change supervision or data and lack independent training repeats and uncertainty estimates.

t08NEb8pTY.one_liner: A coding agent writes persistent robot policies and revises them from execution feedback to study interaction and scaffolding choices.
t08NEb8pTY.problem: It remains unclear how to expose frontier-model capabilities to robots and how refinement budgets and scaffolding affect manipulation.
t08NEb8pTY.method: The paper compares action-by-action decision making with executable-policy synthesis in which a coding agent writes, executes, observes, and revises robot programs. It varies refinement budgets and human-designed scaffolding.
t08NEb8pTY.key_idea: Turn execution feedback into revisions of a persistent robot program rather than making every action decision through the model.
t08NEb8pTY.evidence: Experiments cover LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, and RoboCasa365 Target50, with refinement-budget studies and abstract-reported independent-retry and hard-budget controls.
t08NEb8pTY.claimed_gains: GPT-6 achieves 100% on LIBERO, 95.0% on LIBERO-Pro, and 88.0% on RoboCasa365 Target50 versus 78.0% for a matched execution-time baseline at roughly half the token usage; one-to-eight-turn refinement raises LIBERO-Pro success from 45% to 94% for GPT-6 and 70% to 100% for Claude Opus 5.5.
t08NEb8pTY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interaction-design questions and strong empirical manipulation results across multiple benchmarks.
t08NEb8pTY.main_concern: Reviewers agree that insufficiently controlled scaffolding comparisons do not support broad conclusions about its usefulness.

5oEKfiiTsZ.one_liner: Incidence-structured spatial factors construct latent modes from weighted unions of structural units to preserve hypergraph membership information.
5oEKfiiTsZ.problem: Pairwise operators derived from spatial memberships can lose information needed to determine latent causal coordinates.
5oEKfiiTsZ.method: The method builds spatial factors directly from structural-unit incidences and learns latent time series and their causal graph. The paper proves a pairwise-projection separation result and unsmoothed-factor identifiability under anchor and bridge conditions.
5oEKfiiTsZ.key_idea: Construct latent spatial modes from whole membership units rather than accessing memberships only through a pairwise operator.
5oEKfiiTsZ.evidence: Theory accompanies latent-graph recovery on a public grid benchmark and latent-recovery comparisons on random committee hypergraphs.
5oEKfiiTsZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical reason for preserving incidence information and its connection to latent identifiability.
5oEKfiiTsZ.main_concern: Reviewers agree that membership-specific benefits rely on synthetic hypergraphs, without real-data validation of the information lost by pairwise projection.

PrzxyZ4nav.one_liner: A controlled spectroscopy study combines environmental conditioning, synthetic augmentation, and detection-floor masking to predict molecular absorption spectra.
PrzxyZ4nav.problem: Limited measured spectra and source-dependent detection floors complicate prediction of temperature- and pressure-dependent molecular absorption.
PrzxyZ4nav.method: The study models absorption as a molecule-conditioned continuous function over wavenumber with environmental inputs. It compares data augmentation, threshold treatment, representations, losses, and architectures under molecule-wise cross-validation.
PrzxyZ4nav.key_idea: Condition continuous spectral regression on molecule and environment while masking simulated labels below the experimental detection limit.
PrzxyZ4nav.evidence: The study evaluates 29 configurations across six design axes on 570 experimental HITRAN species using four-fold molecule-wise cross-validation and 1493 held-out spectra.
PrzxyZ4nav.claimed_gains: 50% synthetic augmentation raises median R² from 0.46 to 0.60, while synthetic-only training yields median R²=-71.5 on measured spectra.
PrzxyZ4nav.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical spectroscopy task, leakage-aware molecule splits, and controlled exploration of modeling choices.
PrzxyZ4nav.main_concern: Reviewers question whether synthetic-augmentation gains reflect additional optimization updates under fixed-epoch training.

MFC7zwpsz9.one_liner: A particle-voxel autoencoder and action-conditioned latent dynamics jointly simulate 3D geometry, appearance, and spatially aligned tactile observations.
MFC7zwpsz9.problem: Image- and video-space world models struggle to maintain spatial consistency across viewpoints and long robot interactions.
MFC7zwpsz9.method: 3D World Simulator compresses point clouds into compact voxel latents using a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder. An action-conditioned dynamics model evolves this shared representation for multi-view rendering and tactile prediction.
MFC7zwpsz9.key_idea: Evolve shared particle-voxel latents under robot actions and decode spatially aligned visual, geometric, and tactile observations.
MFC7zwpsz9.evidence: Experiments evaluate long-horizon multimodal prediction, generated-data policy training, simulation-to-real policy correlations, and planning with unseen objects and robot configurations.
MFC7zwpsz9.claimed_gains: The model demonstrates interactive long-horizon multimodal prediction at 25 Hz.
MFC7zwpsz9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the shared 3D representation for cross-view consistency and tactile alignment and the downstream policy evaluations.
MFC7zwpsz9.main_concern: Reviewers question downstream generalization evidence because planning coverage is narrow and the generated-demonstration protocol is unclear.

UvbF0O7sFa.one_liner: StaVER samples latent expert assignments and uses a variationally motivated prior-matching term for mixture-of-experts routing.
UvbF0O7sFa.problem: Hard top-k routing changes expert sets abruptly under perturbations, impairing MoE training stability.
UvbF0O7sFa.method: StaVER treats expert assignment as a latent random variable and routes tokens by sampling from its distribution. A variationally motivated objective introduces prior matching to encourage balanced expert usage.
UvbF0O7sFa.key_idea: Replace discontinuous top-k assignment with sampled expert selection whose expected frequencies vary continuously under perturbations.
UvbF0O7sFa.evidence: Theoretical routing analysis and experiments on 1.8B to 6.6B MoE models cover downstream tasks, perplexity, expert utilization, ablations, and a second pretraining corpus.
UvbF0O7sFa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that experiments show useful performance gains and support studying probabilistic routing.
UvbF0O7sFa.main_concern: Reviewers question how sampling-induced variability affects actual expert-set stability and consistency between repeated inference or training passes.

zURqeRAZJb.one_liner: Variants of Angluin's condition characterize language identification with target-dependent or uniform order-independent bounds on distinct positive examples.
zURqeRAZJb.problem: Identification in the limit alone does not bound the required examples independently of their presentation order.
zURqeRAZJb.method: The paper derives characterizations of countable language collections admitting non-uniform and uniform identification. It extends the analysis to bounded lists, finite disagreements, and auxiliary information, including prefix labels.
zURqeRAZJb.key_idea: Characterize learnable language collections through finite-evidence conditions that guarantee correctness after enough distinct examples regardless of presentation order.
zURqeRAZJb.evidence: Theoretical characterizations and proofs examine standard identification and several relaxed-output or auxiliary-information variants.
zURqeRAZJb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear theoretical development and detailed treatment of identification variants.
zURqeRAZJb.main_concern: Reviewers seek clearer examples or practical demonstrations connecting the abstract characterizations to a broader audience.

o6YIvAjXBd.one_liner: ReComp uses low-rank neuron selection and residual prediction to reconstruct skipped MLP outputs within a fixed arithmetic budget.
o6YIvAjXBd.problem: Contextual sparsity discards individually small neuron outputs whose combined contribution can substantially degrade language-model predictions.
o6YIvAjXBd.method: A low-rank importance predictor selects neurons, while a low-rank affine map estimates the skipped neurons' aggregate output. The compensator uses reduced-rank ridge regression and dense-model distillation, with all components charged to one arithmetic budget.
o6YIvAjXBd.key_idea: Spend part of the sparse-MLP compute budget predicting the aggregate skipped-neuron residual from the MLP input.
o6YIvAjXBd.evidence: Experiments span Qwen2.5, Mistral, and Llama 3.1 families, testing perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, fused-kernel decoding, and dense-verified drafting.
o6YIvAjXBd.claimed_gains: At 10% MLP arithmetic, relative perplexity is 1.31 versus 9.7 on Qwen2.5-7B; compensation lowers TEAL perplexity from 1.42 to 1.16, while decoding gains reach 1.34-1.45× and lossless drafting up to 1.70×.
o6YIvAjXBd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate evaluations across model families and gains under tight compute budgets.
o6YIvAjXBd.main_concern: Reviewers question practical end-to-end speed benefits because arithmetic savings may not translate into latency gains across deployment settings.

Eq74LwgkjR.one_liner: WebMix routes a scout-generated interface manual into mixing weights over pretrained LoRA adapters for web-agent adaptation without target-side training.
Eq74LwgkjR.problem: Web agents must adapt to unseen sites and redesigns without repeatedly fine-tuning on each interface.
Eq74LwgkjR.method: A scout explores the target interface and produces a compact manual. A lightweight router uses that manual to mix a bank of source-interface adapters into one adapter for inference without target-side gradient updates.
Eq74LwgkjR.key_idea: Predict adapter-bank mixing coefficients from an exploration-derived interface manual and compose the existing weight updates.
Eq74LwgkjR.evidence: Qwen and Llama experiments test domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2 and version transfer on TimeWarp, with scouting and adapter ablations.
Eq74LwgkjR.claimed_gains: WebMix gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline on TimeWarp domain transfer with both models.
Eq74LwgkjR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate adapting web agents through interface exploration and adapter reuse without target-side retraining.
Eq74LwgkjR.main_concern: Reviewers question the absence of stronger routing, composition, and general-purpose agent baselines needed to isolate the router's value.

KaIhRgPxOe.one_liner: Readout–relay decomposition separates hidden-state directions supporting current predictions from future-only contributions and motivates temporal credit moderation.
KaIhRgPxOe.problem: How an autoregressive hidden state supports both next-token prediction and later predictions remains unclear.
KaIhRgPxOe.method: The study identifies a current-output-sensitive readout subspace and projects future gradients into readout reuse and an orthogonal relay. Interventions test their temporal effects, and Temporal Proximal Credit moderates future credit along readout directions during fine-tuning.
KaIhRgPxOe.key_idea: Project future-loss gradients onto a current-output-sensitive subspace and its complement to separate readout reuse from temporally selective relay.
KaIhRgPxOe.evidence: Gradient analyses and hidden-state interventions include donor controls, while TPC comparisons evaluate Qwen3-4B-Base and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct across six benchmarks.
KaIhRgPxOe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the functional view of current and future computation and the intervention controls connecting geometry with prediction changes.
KaIhRgPxOe.main_concern: Reviewers question whether TPC's modest advantage over a norm-matched control persists across training seeds.

tL9EuFUP3S.one_liner: Safety mid-training jointly trains on model-generated safety and utility reasoning traces before post-training.
tL9EuFUP3S.problem: Safety learned during post-training can degrade during later training and may trade off against general capability.
tL9EuFUP3S.method: A base model generates structured documents and reasoning traces from safety and utility prompts. An intermediate training stage uses this material to jointly develop intent understanding, relevant knowledge use, and consequence reasoning before subsequent SFT or GRPO.
tL9EuFUP3S.key_idea: Model-generated safety and utility traces share a reasoning structure and are jointly learned between pretraining and post-training.
tL9EuFUP3S.evidence: Experiments cover Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B models, additional Llama models, safety and capability benchmarks, data-ratio ablations, and subsequent general-only SFT and GRPO.
tL9EuFUP3S.claimed_gains: Safety mid-training reduces average attack success rate by 72% to 81% relative to Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B base models while improving general capability.
tL9EuFUP3S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical question of safety retention through later training and the broad experiments on joint safety and capability improvements.
tL9EuFUP3S.main_concern: Differences in training objectives, data format, and optimization budget prevent isolating the claimed shared reasoning mechanism and mid-training stage.

OPyh9q0cnB.one_liner: MedCOBE simulates clinician-model interactions and scores response behavior on cases models can already solve independently.
OPyh9q0cnB.problem: Standalone medical question-answering accuracy does not reveal failures that arise when models collaborate with clinicians.
OPyh9q0cnB.method: MedCOBE evaluates deployment-like clinician-AI interactions in a simulation sandbox while conditioning analysis on sufficient standalone knowledge. It scores reactions to clinician hypotheses and builds behavioral profiles linking interaction tendencies to collaboration outcomes.
OPyh9q0cnB.key_idea: Conditioning interaction evaluation on independently solvable cases separates collaboration behavior from missing medical knowledge.
OPyh9q0cnB.evidence: The study evaluates 20 LLMs, compares standalone and interactive outcomes, examines different simulators and scenarios, and checks a subset of judged responses with an ophthalmologist.
OPyh9q0cnB.claimed_gains: Claude-Opus-5 shows an 11.4% decision-accuracy drop during interaction, and MedCOBE correlates with collaboration outcomes at rho = 0.820 versus 0.409 for standalone accuracy.
OPyh9q0cnB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the gap between standalone diagnostic knowledge and effective clinical collaboration is meaningful and worth measuring.
OPyh9q0cnB.main_concern: The binary Affirm/Challenge behavior abstraction may misclassify clinically useful qualification, partial disagreement, and nuanced discussion.

Ir9shPsHPh.one_liner: Clean sketches SOAP preconditioners with Nyström approximation and retains residual curvature components to reduce optimizer-state memory.
Ir9shPsHPh.problem: Diagonal optimizers discard cross-parameter curvature, while full-curvature methods impose large optimizer-memory costs.
Ir9shPsHPh.method: Clean uses randomized Nyström sketches for SOAP's left and right preconditioners, maintaining detailed statistics in a dominant subspace and cheaper residual statistics outside it. Q-Clean further compresses optimizer states using low precision.
Ir9shPsHPh.key_idea: Nyström sketches approximate dominant covariance directions while residual updates retain contributions outside the low-rank preconditioning subspace.
Ir9shPsHPh.evidence: LLaMA-1.3B experiments compare memory, predictive performance, and wall-clock convergence against optimizers including AdamW, SOAP, and Muon, with larger-model feasibility demonstrations.
Ir9shPsHPh.claimed_gains: Q-Clean reduces optimizer memory by over 50% versus Muon on LLaMA-1.3B, Clean reaches AdamW's final performance 26% faster, and the methods enable 13B-parameter pretraining on a single 80GB GPU.
Ir9shPsHPh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find Nyström compression with residual updates practically promising and appreciate the reported memory savings and wall-clock convergence results.
Ir9shPsHPh.main_concern: Rank-dependent memory scaling and allocation across gradient components need stronger justification and evaluation.

2rkJrW4PHG.one_liner: Synthesizes 3D industrial point-cloud defects using seventeen sequential physics-based material mechanisms paired with triangulation scanner simulation.
2rkJrW4PHG.problem: Industrial 3D anomaly detection benchmarks suffer from scarce real defect data and synthetic pipelines restricted to clean, local analytic point-cloud displacements.
2rkJrW4PHG.method: PhysDefect simulates 17 physical defect mechanisms spanning elastoplastic deformation, transport-driven material removal, and continuous deposition with geometry and material state passed across sequential events, followed by a triangulation scanner simulator capturing occlusion, artifacts, and noise. The open-source dataset comprises 3,213 anomalous and 2,000 normal instances across 100 industrial geometries.
2rkJrW4PHG.key_idea: Simulates seventeen elastoplastic deformation, recession, and deposition mechanisms with sequential geometry-and-material state transfer followed by triangulation-scanner occlusion and noise modeling.
2rkJrW4PHG.evidence: Evaluates eight established 3D anomaly detection methods plus a geometric baseline across 3,213 anomalous and 2,000 normal simulated instances over 100 industrial geometries, alongside internal numerical mechanism checks.
2rkJrW4PHG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining 17 sequential physics-based defect mechanisms with simulated triangulation scanning broadens synthetic 3D anomaly diversity well beyond local geometric perturbations.
2rkJrW4PHG.main_concern: All reviewers highlight the absence of direct validation or sim-to-real transfer experiments against measured industrial scans containing real physical defects.

CAQeizWcB2.one_liner: Evaluates and calibrates LLM agents on pre-run, post-run, relative, and compositional estimation of their execution runtimes.
CAQeizWcB2.problem: Autonomous LLM agents misestimate their own task-completion runtimes, hindering scheduling, resource allocation, and real-time coordination.
