CAQeizWcB2.method: The paper introduces a diagnostic framework decomposing agent runtime self-estimation into pre-run, post-run, relative, and compositional tasks while separating workload volume from deployment execution rate. It also tests lightweight prompting- and training-based calibration interventions to reduce runtime estimation error.
CAQeizWcB2.key_idea: Decomposes agent runtime self-estimation into pre-run, post-run, relative, and compositional probes while applying prompting and training calibration to reduce duration error.
CAQeizWcB2.evidence: Evaluates LLM agents on recorded benchmark execution traces across pre-run, post-run, relative, and compositional duration-estimation tasks with prompting and training calibration baselines.
CAQeizWcB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying whether LLM agents can predict their own execution duration is a practically important, underexplored question structured by a clean four-part diagnostic taxonomy.
CAQeizWcB2.main_concern: Using uncontrolled historical benchmark logs confounds agent self-awareness with external deployment variability, while retrospective estimates match simple action-count linear rules and causal failure factors remain entangled.

lByQG27J9H.one_liner: Velocity-space physics residuals constrain flow matching for physiological signal translation with limited paired data.
lByQG27J9H.problem: Physiological signal translation lacks paired data and needs predictions consistent with known governing relationships.
lByQG27J9H.method: PEFM derives a closed-form residual from the source-target physiological relation and penalizes it on the local flow velocity at each flow time.
lByQG27J9H.key_idea: Translate a physiological governing relation into a local velocity-space residual and add it to the flow-matching objective.
lByQG27J9H.evidence: Error analysis and experiments translate virtual aortic flow and measured bioimpedance into pressure using a learned two-element Windkessel model.
lByQG27J9H.claimed_gains: On measured data, RMSE is 11.8% lower than the baseline closest in physical consistency, and physics residual is 63.6% lower than the baseline closest in RMSE.
lByQG27J9H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mathematical connection between physiological relationships, local velocity regularization, and endpoint consistency.
lByQG27J9H.main_concern: The velocity-space physics loss may simply reparameterize conventional physics regularization on locally reconstructed endpoints.

CiGvIrGXUa.one_liner: Dynamic programming schedules sparse-KV reselection layers using an online retained-importance surrogate for agreement with dense verification.
CiGvIrGXUa.problem: Sparse speculative verification can accept tokens that dense verification rejects, making acceptance counts misleading.
CiGvIrGXUa.method: SKIVE estimates true positives through retained selector importance and builds a reuse table during decoding. Dynamic programming selects reselection layers and their count without calibration data.
CiGvIrGXUa.key_idea: Optimize cache-reselection anchors by dynamic programming over online measurements of retained importance mass.
CiGvIrGXUa.evidence: The paper compares the surrogate with measured true positives and evaluates schedules in Hugging Face and SGLang, including GovReport output-similarity measurements.
CiGvIrGXUa.claimed_gains: Reusing one selection across all layers costs 15–27 true-positive points.
CiGvIrGXUa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate exposing false acceptances and turning layer-wise cache reuse into an explicit online scheduling problem.
CiGvIrGXUa.main_concern: Output-similarity evaluations do not adequately establish downstream quality preservation under the distribution shift from sparse verification.

PMX9L9scfU.one_liner: Production-profile enumeration and linear programming construct optimal payment menus for homogeneous-good procurement under private costs.
PMX9L9scfU.problem: A buyer must choose payments that maximize expected value minus compensation when suppliers privately know quantity-dependent production costs.
PMX9L9scfU.method: The single-agent algorithm enumerates production profiles and solves a linear program for each menu, with a faster exact algorithm under ordered costs. Sequential multi-agent algorithms use dynamic programming and menu enumeration.
PMX9L9scfU.key_idea: Enumerate production profiles across private cost types and optimize incentive-compatible payments for each candidate profile.
PMX9L9scfU.evidence: Theoretical results establish NP-hardness through unit-demand pricing reductions and exact algorithms for general and ordered costs, including sequential procurement.
PMX9L9scfU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the procurement model and its theoretical results, particularly the distinction between general and ordered costs.
PMX9L9scfU.main_concern: The static-menu result relies on the buyer choosing among a supplier's tied best responses differently across rounds.

i0CfTqMoYr.one_liner: Spatial affine coupling flows provide single-pass, analytically invertible latent transport for bidirectional cross-modal image translation.
i0CfTqMoYr.problem: Cross-modal translation methods trade inference efficiency against exact reversibility or rely on approximate cycle constraints.
i0CfTqMoYr.method: FlowCycle encodes modalities into a learned representation and transports between them through discrete normalizing flows with spatial affine couplings. Closed-form inverses reverse the latent mapping, while intermediate states expose translation trajectories.
i0CfTqMoYr.key_idea: Use analytically invertible affine coupling transformations as the latent transport operator between modality-specific encoders and decoders.
i0CfTqMoYr.evidence: Experiments cover Multimodal MNIST, Cityscapes, and multi-sequence brain MRI, assessing translation fidelity and exact latent round trips.
i0CfTqMoYr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the coherent latent invertibility formulation and its explicit distinction from image-space cycle error.
i0CfTqMoYr.main_concern: The contribution beyond established invertible latent architectures and standard translation losses remains insufficiently demonstrated.

HkRmyOsHE3.one_liner: A multi-agent system compiles text prompts into CARLA road maps, scene assets, and dynamic driving behaviors.
HkRmyOsHE3.problem: Autonomous-driving evaluation depends on fixed simulator towns that restrict scenario diversity and testing of unfamiliar environments.
HkRmyOsHE3.method: CARLAGen4D uses a domain-specific language to synthesize road topology efficiently and coordinates agents generating background assets and traffic behaviors. Route validation and rollout checks support executable scenarios.
HkRmyOsHE3.key_idea: Represent generated roads in a compact domain-specific language and coordinate map, asset, and behavior generation through multiple agents.
HkRmyOsHE3.evidence: CARLA experiments assess generated-map validity and prompt satisfaction, compare generation systems, and benchmark driving policies on generated layouts.
HkRmyOsHE3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value executable generation of road networks themselves as a practical extension beyond placing actors in existing towns.
HkRmyOsHE3.main_concern: The driving-policy evaluation lacks matched stock-town controls, leaving unclear whether performance changes reflect road topology or generated visual appearance.

iiyYu0Vo97.one_liner: Student-style teacher edits, action-informed token weights, and asymmetric KL regularization distill closed-model supervision into smaller web agents.
iiyYu0Vo97.problem: Closed teachers expose no logits, while offline demonstrations mismatch the states and writing style of smaller student web agents.
iiyYu0Vo97.method: WebKD asks a teacher to edit failed student episodes from the first mistake in the student's style. Action-informed reasoning weights and a role-asymmetric KL anchor constrain reasoning while allowing corrected actions to change.
iiyYu0Vo97.key_idea: Rewrite failed student trajectories minimally in student style and weight reasoning by its contribution to corrected actions.
iiyYu0Vo97.evidence: Experiments compare distillation and reinforcement-learning baselines on TimeWarp, unseen versions, and live-web evaluation, with ablations of editing components.
iiyYu0Vo97.claimed_gains: WebKD students gain about 5.5–10.7 pp on TimeWarp over behavior cloning, outcome-reward RL, and teacher editing baselines.
iiyYu0Vo97.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the treatment of teacher-student distribution mismatch well motivated and supported by empirical comparisons.
iiyYu0Vo97.main_concern: Limited training data and weak live-web results leave generalization to harder or larger-scale settings uncertain.

7f5vswm45x.one_liner: A zero-mismatch RL reference isolates how rollout and optimization probability discrepancies destabilize language-model training.
7f5vswm45x.problem: Implementation differences between rollout generation and policy optimization create probability mismatches entangled with off-policy drift and stabilization mechanisms.
7f5vswm45x.method: ExactRL provides a zero-mismatch diagnostic setting and compares training with and without numerical disagreement. The study analyzes changes to the effective optimization problem and examines mitigation strategies.
7f5vswm45x.key_idea: Remove rollout-optimization probability mismatch in a reference implementation to isolate its effects on reinforcement-learning stability.
7f5vswm45x.evidence: Single-update REINFORCE comparisons on dense and mixture-of-experts models track rewards, mismatch, losses, gradients, and KL estimates.
7f5vswm45x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the working zero-mismatch reference and clean experimental separation of numerical mismatch from other RL effects.
7f5vswm45x.main_concern: Most mechanistic conclusions rely on a single model-task combination, limiting their generality.

rIVk3e6pb1.one_liner: Adapts training-free scRNA-seq feature propagation using reciprocal-neighbor metric transforms, contrast-based stopping, and edge pruning.
rIVk3e6pb1.problem: Graph feature propagation for sparse scRNA-seq imputation suffers from corrupted neighbor rankings and over-smoothing when using static similarity metrics and fixed propagation depths.
rIVk3e6pb1.method: scRFP estimates within-pair variance from reciprocal cell neighbors to compute a closed-form linear metric transformation that recalibrates cell similarities across the dataset. It then halts hard feature propagation adaptively via neighborhood contrast monitoring and prunes low-confidence graph edges before running soft diffusion.
rIVk3e6pb1.key_idea: Learn a closed-form similarity metric from reciprocal cell pairs to suppress within-pair noise directions, paired with contrast-stopped propagation and edge pruning.
rIVk3e6pb1.evidence: Evaluated with a single hyperparameter configuration across seven benchmark scRNA-seq datasets on cell clustering (ARI), technical-dropout recovery, and runtime.
rIVk3e6pb1.claimed_gains: Achieves the best clustering performance on six of seven scRNA-seq datasets, improving ARI by up to 12.1% (relative) over the strongest baseline.
rIVk3e6pb1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free three-component pipeline is fast, simple, and achieves consistent clustering and dropout-recovery gains on six of seven scRNA-seq benchmarks.
rIVk3e6pb1.main_concern: Adaptive stopping hits the maximum iteration cap on several datasets and relies on cross-dataset ARI tuning while soft propagation remains fixed at 80 steps, leaving the stopping rule's true benefit unclear.

TPWVQb4Hu9.one_liner: Dual-masked contrastive JEPA pretrains a frozen time-series encoder on synthetic episodes for classification and horizon-conditioned event forecasting.
TPWVQb4Hu9.problem: Existing time-series foundation models predict full future value windows rather than whether and when brief target events will occur.
TPWVQb4Hu9.method: Saturn pretrains a time-series encoder under a joint-embedding predictive objective with a dual mask—one interior block and one window-end block—combined with a contrastive term over two augmented views on synthetic episodes containing matched precursor and precursor-free strata. One frozen encoder with lightweight task heads serves classification and horizon-conditioned binary event forecasting, evaluated on real corpora passing a statistical Precursor Check (PrecursorBench).
TPWVQb4Hu9.key_idea: Pretrain a time-series encoder on precursor-controlled synthetic episodes using dual interior-and-tail masking with view-contrastive regularization to prevent collapse without moving-average targets.
TPWVQb4Hu9.evidence: Pretrained exclusively on synthetic episodes and evaluated on time-series classification (UCR and UEA per reviews) and PrecursorBench event-forecasting corpora.
TPWVQb4Hu9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating event forecasting as horizon-conditioned classification with dual-masked contrastive pretraining and precursor-controlled evaluation is practical and well motivated.
TPWVQb4Hu9.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the gains of dual masking and the JEPA objective from contrastive learning, alongside numerical and dataset discrepancies across tables and appendices.

7PcXI3iqT0.one_liner: Freezes per-attack prototype routing gates and bonafide evidence in continual face anti-spoofing to prevent later sessions erasing routes.
7PcXI3iqT0.problem: In continual face anti-spoofing, bonafide samples from later sessions can alter router behavior and stop known attacks from reaching their designated experts.
7PcXI3iqT0.method: PRIME learns a fixed embedding space via Joint Token Attention—weighting all tokens across all layers of a frozen backbone pretrained on the paired synthetic FFHQ-SynthFAS corpus—and freezes each new attack class's routing test alongside the bonafide evidence it uses. This guarantees conditional zero forgetting on attack routing (ZF-A) across continual sessions.
7PcXI3iqT0.key_idea: Freeze each attack class's prototype routing gate and supporting bonafide reference evidence in a fixed multi-layer token-attention space upon class arrival.
7PcXI3iqT0.evidence: Formal proof of conditional zero forgetting on attack routing (ZF-A), pretraining on FFHQ-SynthFAS, and evaluations on OCIM leave-one-out and a three-dataset chronological chain tested on five unseen datasets.
7PcXI3iqT0.claimed_gains: Achieves 1.45% mean HTER on OCIM leave-one-out (versus 10.66% continual and 1.82% joint-training baselines) with 99.97% mAA and 98.63% mAGA, and 2.21% mean HTER on five unseen datasets while losing zero attack routes versus 1.5% to 15.7% reversed attack decisions for baselines.
7PcXI3iqT0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preventing subsequent bonafide data from invalidating established attack routes addresses a clear security failure in continual face anti-spoofing with strong cross-domain results.
7PcXI3iqT0.main_concern: Freezing attack routing does not guarantee accurate final predictions, as new-domain bonafide frames or realistic unseen attacks routed to existing experts can still be misclassified.

3DJISrwjRN.one_liner: Transforms 3D scenes into agent-centric coordinates and applies four-task egocentric alignment pre-finetuning for text-free situated 3D QA.
3DJISrwjRN.problem: Situated 3D question answering methods depend on costly natural-language situation descriptions or exhibit weak functional sensitivity to numerical agent pose.
3DJISrwjRN.method: EgoAlign represents 3D scenes in an agent-centric coordinate frame and introduces an egocentric alignment stage prior to downstream fine-tuning. The alignment stage trains the 3D language model on object category recognition, egocentric direction prediction, metric distance estimation, and spatial relation prediction.
3DJISrwjRN.key_idea: Represent 3D scenes in agent-centric coordinates and pre-align the model on category, direction, metric distance, and spatial relation prediction conditioned on numerical pose.
3DJISrwjRN.evidence: Evaluated on SQA3D, Real-3DQA, and MSQA, including ablations removing textual situation descriptions and shuffling numerical poses.
3DJISrwjRN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value diagnosing functional pose reliance through pose-shuffling and perturbation experiments and note strong, consistent benchmark results from a clean design.
3DJISrwjRN.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological differentiation from prior pose-conditioned 3D models, fairness of baseline pose-insensitivity comparisons, and generalization to continuous counterfactual pose changes.

khjzaxo6Rq.one_liner: Combines prefix-ordered action tokenization with frozen-decoder trajectory loss to inject physical distance feedback into discrete driving VLAs.
khjzaxo6Rq.problem: Training discrete trajectory-token driving VLAs with categorical cross-entropy penalizes all incorrect tokens uniformly regardless of physical metric error, causing closed-loop driving failures.
khjzaxo6Rq.method: The method adapts Ordered Action Tokenization (OAT) to map spatially nearby driving trajectories to shared sequence prefixes and introduces Coarse Trajectory Anchor Regularization (CTAR). CTAR backpropagates smooth-L1 trajectory errors directly into the first coarse action token via a frozen trajectory decoder.
khjzaxo6Rq.key_idea: Map nearby trajectories to shared token prefixes and backpropagate smooth-L1 physical trajectory errors through a frozen decoder into the first coarse action token.
khjzaxo6Rq.evidence: Evaluated on CARLA Bench2Drive-220 and NAVSIM v2 against discrete K-means token (K-DISK) and continuous driving baselines.
khjzaxo6Rq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing the mismatch between distance-blind cross-entropy and physical trajectory distance in closed-loop discrete driving VLAs is well motivated and outperforms K-DISK.
khjzaxo6Rq.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns over unclear distance-aware gradient behavior under teacher-forced OAT training, simultaneous multi-factor changes relative to K-DISK, unquantified 32-token autoregressive latency, and degraded comfort scores.

j75CM5OwMa.one_liner: Up-weights knowledge-bearing answer tokens via early-exit distributions to reduce trigger-free leakage in LLM unlearning.
j75CM5OwMa.problem: Gradient-based LLM unlearning relies on explicit forget-target trigger tokens to suppress representations, leaving target knowledge vulnerable on trigger-free queries where entities are inferred.
j75CM5OwMa.method: Using controlled trigger injection, activation patching, and attention knock-out, the paper identifies a token-triggered forgetting pathway driven by target-token attention concentration and forget-subspace collapse. To mitigate trigger-free leakage, EE-TNPO uses early-exit distributions to up-weight knowledge-bearing answer tokens such as names and factual attributes during unlearning.
j75CM5OwMa.key_idea: Use early-exit token distributions to up-weight knowledge-bearing answer tokens during unlearning so suppression does not depend on explicit prompt trigger tokens.
j75CM5OwMa.evidence: Mechanistic interventions (trigger injection, activation patching, attention knock-out) and unlearning evaluations across TOFU, RWKU, WMDP, and MUSE.
j75CM5OwMa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating trigger-free queries exposes an important blind spot in aggregate unlearning metrics and that EE-TNPO reduces name leakage while preserving aggregate utility.
j75CM5OwMa.main_concern: Activation patching does not fully isolate causal representation-rank collapse or test modern LLM families beyond Llama-2-7B-Chat, and shared entities can cause retention degradation.

VpsesG8S7U.one_liner: Ranks cached KV tokens by hidden-state shifts and recent query-key relevance to prevent reasoning loops without attention matrices.
VpsesG8S7U.problem: Attention-based KV-cache eviction requires materializing attention weights incompatible with fast inference kernels and degrades long-chain-of-thought reasoning mainly by inducing non-terminating loops.
VpsesG8S7U.method: After finding that tight-budget eviction accuracy drops primarily come from repetitive looping to the length limit rather than incorrect finished answers, the authors introduce EpiKV. EpiKV scores cached tokens using hidden-state shifts and recent query-key relevance exposed during the forward pass, running directly on unmodified attention kernels in vLLM.
VpsesG8S7U.key_idea: Rank cached KV tokens using hidden-state shifts and recent query-key relevance without forming the attention matrix to retain tokens that prevent generation loops.
VpsesG8S7U.evidence: Evaluated across five reasoning models against attention-based KV-cache eviction baselines across cache budgets in vLLM on unmodified kernels.
VpsesG8S7U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the failure-mode analysis showing KV eviction degrades reasoning primarily through length-cap looping rather than wrong completed answers, alongside training-free vLLM compatibility.
VpsesG8S7U.main_concern: Reviewers question incremental novelty over existing attention-free query-window eviction methods (such as SnapKV and R-KV), unmatched baseline memory occupancy, and whether the epiphany score actively drives token selection.

Rv0EbNpVx3.one_liner: Adapts bidirectional diffusion speech transformers into four-step chunk-streaming generators via block-causal finetuning, consistency distillation, and distribution matching.
Rv0EbNpVx3.problem: Offline diffusion and flow-matching speech generators rely on full-utterance bidirectional attention and iterative multi-step sampling, preventing real-time chunk-wise streaming playback.
Rv0EbNpVx3.method: CaDiS converts pretrained bidirectional speech diffusion transformers into streaming generators via block-causal diffusion adaptation, four-step causal consistency distillation, and distribution-matching refinement. Task-specific adaptations add normalized positional encoding for asynchronous text in text-to-speech and content-vector distillation with reference-anchored positional re-encoding for voice conversion.
Rv0EbNpVx3.key_idea: Convert offline bidirectional speech diffusion transformers to chunk-streaming models via block-causal finetuning, four-step consistency distillation, and distribution-matching refinement.
Rv0EbNpVx3.evidence: Evaluated with objective and subjective listening metrics on streaming text-to-speech and voice conversion across natural human and expressive anime voices.
Rv0EbNpVx3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear three-stage training ablations and broad evaluation across streaming text-to-speech and voice conversion, including expressive and multilingual settings.
Rv0EbNpVx3.main_concern: Reviewers note the pipeline largely transfers existing causal diffusion distillation recipes with insufficient ablations of speech-specific components and unmatched latency comparison conditions.

opxmEQSwah.one_liner: Continuously generates utility-directed thought tokens during streaming video, deciding adaptively when to speak.
opxmEQSwah.problem: Reactive multimodal assistants leave incoming streams unexamined until users speak, delaying answers and preventing proactive help.
opxmEQSwah.method: Stream-of-Thought combines two-stage SFT on curated streaming thoughts with Think–Speak Group Policy Optimization, and introduces UnpromptedBench for open-ended proactive assistance.
opxmEQSwah.key_idea: Caches utility-directed thoughts during perception and separately optimizes thinking and speaking decisions for reactive and proactive assistance.
opxmEQSwah.evidence: Evaluations cover reactive and proactive streaming-video benchmarks, a single 4B model, UnpromptedBench, and ablations of hidden-quiz and decision-local rewards.
opxmEQSwah.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly learning when to think and speak is well motivated and supported by extensive evaluations and useful reward ablations.
opxmEQSwah.main_concern: Reviewers most often question practical proactive utility because UnpromptedBench coverage is only 2.11%, approximately five of 237 annotated opportunities.

MMGaX2MzDX.one_liner: Builds parameter-free n-gram embeddings from host-stored counts and reused language-model unembedding rows.
MMGaX2MzDX.problem: Learned n-gram embeddings require expensive GPU memory, while cheap host memory remains underutilized for memory-based LM scaling.
MMGaX2MzDX.method: COUNT stores conditional n-gram frequencies on host and uses them to weight existing next-token unembedding rows as an additional input embedding, with switchable tables for adaptation.
MMGaX2MzDX.key_idea: Weights the LM's existing unembedding rows by conditional n-gram frequencies, creating input embeddings without learned parameters.
MMGaX2MzDX.evidence: Pretraining experiments span seven model sizes and three token budgets, with validation loss, task loss, and accuracy comparisons.
MMGaX2MzDX.claimed_gains: At fixed compute, adding COUNT while pretraining 1B-parameter LMs improves validation loss as much as an LM with 57% more compute.
MMGaX2MzDX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing unembeddings with host-stored counts is an elegant parameter-free construction with broad and consistent pretraining effects.
MMGaX2MzDX.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that n-gram counts use much more data than model training, leaving compute-matched gains confounded by unequal data exposure.

MttTD0Z27c.one_liner: Turns failed agent trajectories into interactive dependency-graph environments for evidence-guided error localization.
MttTD0Z27c.problem: Long-horizon agent diagnosis is difficult when relevant evidence is dispersed across dependent steps and trajectories are treated as passive context.
MttTD0Z27c.method: TIDE constructs a dependency graph over execution steps, organizes it into hierarchical processes, and lets an Agent-as-a-Judge navigate abstraction levels and inspect related evidence.
MttTD0Z27c.key_idea: Organizes execution steps into a dependency graph and hierarchical processes that a judge actively navigates for diagnostic evidence.
MttTD0Z27c.evidence: Experiments on two benchmarks evaluate error localization across agentic systems and judge models, including trajectory-length analyses.
MttTD0Z27c.claimed_gains: TIDE reduces mean localization distance by up to 55% on long-horizon trajectories across two benchmarks.
MttTD0Z27c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that interactive, graph-structured exploration is a sensible and effective alternative to flat trajectory ingestion.
MttTD0Z27c.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether gains over prior methods are isolated, citing backbone and prompt mismatches and unclear differences from graph-based baselines.

BcEw8FcdEb.one_liner: Connects empowerment maximization to MDP centrality through reachable-occupancy geometry and skill learning.
BcEw8FcdEb.problem: The relationship between information-theoretic empowerment and structural centrality in Markov decision processes remains insufficiently understood.
BcEw8FcdEb.method: The paper links empowerment and skill-learning objectives through reachable polytopes, KL geometry, Gaussian widths, and theoretical analyses of adaptation and centrality.
BcEw8FcdEb.key_idea: Relates skill–future-state mutual information to KL divergence between reachable state occupancies and their geometric center.
BcEw8FcdEb.evidence: The support consists of formal theorems and geometric interpretations with visualizations in small-scale environments.
BcEw8FcdEb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formally connecting empowerment, skill learning, and convex geometry addresses a fundamental and interesting question.
BcEw8FcdEb.main_concern: Reviewers most often view the centrality result as a modest extension of prior skill-learning and channel-capacity results.

xJMHBa9LwL.one_liner: Routes corrupted wearable modalities using source-learned reliance and lightweight runtime abnormality detection.
xJMHBa9LwL.problem: Online cross-modal agreement can misrepresent corruption in heterogeneous sensors, and evaluating alternative modality subsets adds inference cost.
xJMHBa9LwL.method: CARAT uses asymmetric modality dropout, a frozen gradient-norm reliance proxy, and a one-class runtime detector to choose omission or attenuation without candidate-subset evaluation.
xJMHBa9LwL.key_idea: Decouples source-trained, backbone-specific modality reliance from runtime corruption detection to choose omission or attenuation without subset enumeration.
xJMHBa9LwL.evidence: Experiments span four wearable datasets, five corruption types, three backbones, eight TTA baselines, and 12 dataset–backbone settings.
xJMHBa9LwL.claimed_gains: CARAT exceeds EATA by 2.43 F1 points across 12 equally weighted dataset–backbone settings, using 9.49% fewer GFLOPs and 47.82% fewer updated parameters across five profiled configurations.
xJMHBa9LwL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating sensor abnormality from model-specific reliance is well motivated and avoids costly modality-subset enumeration.
xJMHBa9LwL.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the gains backbone-dependent and insufficiently attribute them to the learned reliance proxy rather than the routing policy.

VQohRNTl6U.one_liner: Embeds homodyne records with sliced Wasserstein geometry for low-shot quantum-state parameter regression.
VQohRNTl6U.problem: Extracting useful continuous-variable quantum-state information from few destructive homodyne measurements remains a central practical challenge.
VQohRNTl6U.method: QSWE maps quadrature marginals to a Euclidean vector with sliced-Wasserstein distances, analyzes displacement and squeezing geometry, and regresses cat-state parameters without state reconstruction.
VQohRNTl6U.key_idea: Maps measured quadrature quantiles into a Euclidean embedding whose distances equal sliced Wasserstein distances between homodyne marginals.
VQohRNTl6U.evidence: Experiments study displaced and squeezed state grids and cat-state regression against moment, energy-distance, and kernel mean-embedding features with Cramér–Rao comparisons.
VQohRNTl6U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the embedding's exact geometric properties connect cleanly to learning and are tested with carefully controlled measurement budgets.
VQohRNTl6U.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the empirical scope too restricted, particularly the simulated low-dimensional families and limited comparisons with direct or model-based estimators.

dNDavP9cQE.one_liner: Propagates hierarchical uncertainty through posterior-predictive likelihood ratios for record- and group-level membership inference.
dNDavP9cQE.problem: Membership attacks often ignore finite-reference uncertainty and fail to separate variation across stochastic queries, trained models, records, and groups.
dNDavP9cQE.method: The hierarchical Bayesian framework models signal variation under member and non-member hypotheses and yields posterior-predictive likelihood-ratio tests for diffusion, flow-matching, deterministic, and grouped observations.
dNDavP9cQE.key_idea: Models member and non-member signals hierarchically, separating query randomness from reference-model variation in a posterior-predictive likelihood-ratio test.
dNDavP9cQE.evidence: Experiments cover record- and group-level inference for denoising diffusion and flow matching, including CIFAR10, CelebA, and mixed-model reference pools.
dNDavP9cQE.claimed_gains: The attack outperforms state-of-the-art methods for record-level inference and adapted baselines for group-level inference, including with a mixed DDPM and flow-matching reference pool.
dNDavP9cQE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating stochastic-query and trained-model variation is sound, concrete, and useful for record- and group-level inference.
dNDavP9cQE.main_concern: Reviewers most often criticize the omission of BaVarIA, which prevents isolating the benefit of the new hierarchy from Bayesian regularization.

Vjmz8sCDFf.one_liner: Trains a 4B LLM agent with RL and group credit-splitting rewards to discover stable crystals via computational tools.
Vjmz8sCDFf.problem: Inorganic crystal discovery requires iterative search with stability feedback, where standard LLM generation or naive RL can repeatedly submit one valid structure.
Vjmz8sCDFf.method: The authors equip a 4B LLM with crystal-checking tools using Wyckoff representations and train it with multi-turn reinforcement learning. To prevent duplicate submissions, a group-level reward scores attempts together and splits credit across repeated structures while rewarding stability, novelty, and target properties.
Vjmz8sCDFf.key_idea: Trains a tool-using 4B crystal-search agent with group-level rewards that split credit across repeated structures to enforce diverse discoveries.
Vjmz8sCDFf.evidence: Evaluated on in-domain MP-20, out-of-domain WBM, band-gap targets, and lead-free perovskite search using held-out MLIPs and DFT validation.
Vjmz8sCDFf.claimed_gains: Reinforcement learning nearly doubles the S.U.N. structure rate over supervised fine-tuning and finds up to 7x more S.U.N. wide-gap materials for band-gap targets.
Vjmz8sCDFf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear multi-turn tool-use formulation with Wyckoff representations, group diversity rewards, and held-out MLIP/DFT validation.
Vjmz8sCDFf.main_concern: Reviewers point out that under equal stability-evaluation budgets SFT with best-of-k matches or beats RL, and note missing comparisons to recent evolutionary LLM materials-search baselines.

RiqkjlPZhc.one_liner: Compresses long-context KV caches from context alone via second-order rate-distortion rank and precision allocation.
RiqkjlPZhc.problem: Existing KV-cache compression methods struggle to reach extreme compression ratios without heavy training, external calibration data, or quality loss.
RiqkjlPZhc.method: RAPID models attention-output error around the uncompressed cache to jointly allocate cross-layer budgets, per-token low-rank dimensions, and per-dimension quantization bits. It refines layer-wise latent representations using only context query vectors and attention projections, requiring no training data or full-model passes.
RiqkjlPZhc.key_idea: Uses a second-order attention-output error model to jointly optimize per-token rank, mixed-precision quantization, and cross-layer budgets from context queries alone.
RiqkjlPZhc.evidence: Evaluated on LongHealth and RULER across Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B, GLM-4.7-Flash (MLA), and GPT-OSS-120B (MoE) at up to 20x compression.
RiqkjlPZhc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the unified rate-distortion integration and broad evaluation across dense, MLA, and MoE models.
RiqkjlPZhc.main_concern: Reviewers view individual components (low-rank, mixed precision, attention matching) as established in prior work and note insufficient characterization of compression-time and inference efficiency.

st9i6DXgw7.one_liner: Re-evaluates memory-based self-improving agents across multiple seeds and shuffled task orders, exposing high variance and order fragility.
st9i6DXgw7.problem: Evaluations of memory-based self-improving agents rely on single runs and fixed task orderings, masking instability and implicit curricula.
st9i6DXgw7.method: The authors re-evaluate two memory-based self-improving agent methods across multiple independent runs and randomly shuffled task sequences. They manually diagnose failure modes, identifying task and environment underspecification as a key driver of harmful memory accumulation.
st9i6DXgw7.key_idea: Audits memory-based self-improving agents across multi-seed runs and shuffled task sequences to isolate variance amplification and order sensitivity.
st9i6DXgw7.evidence: Multi-run and shuffled-order experiments on 12 domains and WebArena, plus qualitative failure analysis and specification-refinement ablations.
st9i6DXgw7.claimed_gains: With ReasoningBank, run-to-run variance increases in 10 of 12 domains, the best-worst gap on WebArena GitLab grows from 4.4 to 7.8 percentage points, and WebArena gain under default ordering (+1.5%) flips to a degradation (-4.5%) under shuffled task orders.
st9i6DXgw7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing single-run and fixed-order evaluation flaws in self-improving agents is timely and practically important.
st9i6DXgw7.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in multi-seed and order-shuffling evaluation practices, small sample counts (three runs), and mostly qualitative evidence for underspecification.

yT2c9WoYQI.one_liner: Builds a scalable long-horizon embodied environment and multi-clue QA benchmark to train and test long-context VLM agents.
yT2c9WoYQI.problem: Embodied AI lacks reproducible, arbitrarily long interaction benchmarks to evaluate and train VLM agents on distant-memory reasoning.
yT2c9WoYQI.method: Infinity-THOR generates unlimited reproducible trajectories paired with ground-truth actions and a Needle(s) in the Embodied Haystack QA task requiring scattered clues. The authors also evaluate interleaved Goal-State-Action representations, memory-augmented modeling, context extension, and Context Parallelism.
yT2c9WoYQI.key_idea: Synthesizes unlimited reproducible embodied trajectories with scattered multi-clue QA pairs and trains VLM agents using interleaved Goal-State-Action context extension.
yT2c9WoYQI.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic long-horizon trajectories, online planning, photorealistic sim-to-real transfer, and low-level manipulation integration.
yT2c9WoYQI.claimed_gains: The QA dataset alone improves photorealistic benchmark performance by up to +11.2%.
yT2c9WoYQI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the scalable long-horizon trajectory generator, multi-evidence QA formulation, and systematic architectural and training comparisons.
yT2c9WoYQI.main_concern: Reviewers question whether QA and online gains truly require visual memory rather than text action histories or recent frames, and note low online success rates and missing SOTA VLM baselines.

3TIgu4ggis.one_liner: Corrects trajectory bias in constrained masked diffusion decoding using automaton-twisted Sequential Monte Carlo.
3TIgu4ggis.problem: Per-step constrained decoding in Masked Diffusion Language Models satisfies constraints locally via dynamic programming, but composing exact per-step draws introduces trajectory bias relative to the model's valid path distribution.
3TIgu4ggis.method: The authors derive the exact trajectory bias caused by denoiser reconditioning and introduce TWISTER, an automaton-twisted Sequential Monte Carlo decoder. Using the step-exact decoder as a proposal, TWISTER computes exact Feynman-Kac twist corrections for regular language constraints from pre-computed dynamic programming quantities to target the unbiased Doob h-transform.
3TIgu4ggis.key_idea: Uses pre-computed automaton dynamic programming quantities as Feynman-Kac twists in Sequential Monte Carlo to unbias step-exact masked diffusion decoding.
3TIgu4ggis.evidence: The paper provides mathematical proofs of trajectory bias and unbiasedness, alongside synthetic token-class constraint and JSON generation experiments.
3TIgu4ggis.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper provides a clear, rigorous mathematical characterization of trajectory bias in constrained MDLM decoding and a principled correction mechanism.
3TIgu4ggis.main_concern: Reviewers note a lack of empirical evidence that removing trajectory bias improves downstream task quality or diversity, and point out the restriction to regular languages (DFAs) rather than CFGs.

FvKNkRhCBR.one_liner: Unifies pixel-space flow matching and contrastive learning in one encoder conditioned on either a global vector or CLS embeddings.
FvKNkRhCBR.problem: Strong image generators rely on class labels, frozen pretrained encoders, or separate autoencoders/tokenizers, making generation dependent on external supervision and pretraining.
FvKNkRhCBR.method: SCION trains a single pixel-space encoder conditioned on a timestep and a conditioning embedding. For contrastive representation learning, it uses a shared learned global vector and extracts the [CLS] token; for generative flow matching, it conditions the same encoder on the image's [CLS] embedding.
FvKNkRhCBR.key_idea: Conditions one pixel-space encoder on a shared global vector for contrastive [CLS] representation learning and on the [CLS] embedding for flow-matching generation.
FvKNkRhCBR.evidence: Experiments on ImageNet 256x256 evaluate generation FID, ImageNet linear probing accuracy, transfer benchmarks, and component ablations.
FvKNkRhCBR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying pixel-space generative modeling and self-supervised representation learning without labels or pretrained components is a challenging, interesting direction with thorough ablations.
FvKNkRhCBR.main_concern: Reviewers question whether SCION truly uses one model versus two, note test-set selection bias in transfer-8 regularization tuning, and observe that official baselines outperform SCION.

SfmcXkC3Zh.one_liner: Decouples representation learning from physical forecasting via masked reconstruction, JEPA prediction, and trajectory-level regime fingerprinting.
SfmcXkC3Zh.problem: Foundation models for spatio-temporal physical dynamics struggle to generalize across unseen systems, parameters, and operating conditions.
SfmcXkC3Zh.method: The authors combine universal 2D/3D patchification with self-supervised masked reconstruction, latent JEPA prediction, and regime fingerprinting (matching an early partial observation to a broader view of the same trajectory) to condition downstream models.
SfmcXkC3Zh.key_idea: Trains a regime-fingerprinting objective to match early partial observations to broader trajectory views, extracting time-persistent conditioning signals for downstream physics rollouts.
SfmcXkC3Zh.evidence: Evaluated on heterogeneous 2D and 3D spatio-temporal dynamics across parameter regression and few-shot/zero-shot forecasting tasks.
SfmcXkC3Zh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the universal patchification for 2D/3D systems and the goal of separating persistent regime inference from state forecasting.
SfmcXkC3Zh.main_concern: Reviewers question whether instance-discrimination regime fingerprinting actually captures regime-level versus trajectory-specific features, and note confounded forecasting ablations and long-term rollout instability.

k6vrWjWr33.one_liner: Uses a reasoning LLM to inspect execution logs during automated ML search and applies test-time RL to refine hypothesis selection.
k6vrWjWr33.problem: Heuristic tree-search methods like MCTS rank ML research nodes by score alone, conflating flawed implementations with poor hypotheses.
k6vrWjWr33.method: ARTS prompts a reasoning LLM to inspect code and execution logs to diagnose failure causes and select parent nodes, while ARTS* applies test-time RL over explored hypotheses to mitigate context degradation.
k6vrWjWr33.key_idea: Diagnoses execution logs to separate implementation bugs from hypothesis merit during tree-search node selection, reinforced via test-time RL.
k6vrWjWr33.evidence: Evaluated across 22 tasks from MLGym and MLEBench-Hard.
k6vrWjWr33.claimed_gains: Outperforms leading methods by a mean normalized score of 12.0% across MLGym and MLEBench-Hard, with a test-time-trained Qwen3-4B scientist matching or exceeding o3 on 6 of 12 MLGym tasks.
k6vrWjWr33.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the insight of inspecting execution logs to rescue promising hypotheses with buggy implementations.
k6vrWjWr33.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about reporting best validation scores without held-out test evaluation, unmatched compute budgets (24 vs. 8 GPU-hours), and missing MARS baseline.

f6WkgHrjhn.one_liner: Fine-tunes LLMs on a coreset while unlearning discarded non-coreset examples to preserve prior capabilities.
f6WkgHrjhn.problem: Fine-tuning LLMs on target-task data degrades general knowledge, reasoning, and safety alignment when non-target capabilities are unknown a priori.
f6WkgHrjhn.method: FUEL partitions target data into a coreset and non-coreset, then uses a leader-follower optimization that descends on the coreset loss while applying a reversed unlearning gradient perturbation from the non-coreset.
f6WkgHrjhn.key_idea: Reverses the fine-tuning objective on excluded non-coreset data to compute corrective gradient perturbations alongside coreset descent.
f6WkgHrjhn.evidence: Experiments across four target tasks, two model scales, and safety-aligned models compare FUEL against standard and coreset fine-tuning.
f6WkgHrjhn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target-data-only problem is practical and that FUEL consistently improves non-target accuracy at minimal cost to target performance.
f6WkgHrjhn.main_concern: Reviewers point out that Algorithm 1 closely resembles Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) and lacks comparisons with SAM and existing anti-forgetting baselines.

1x3Tip9ZaX.one_liner: Unifies document text blocks, masks, boxes, semantic tags, and CoT traces as visual anchors in ADOPD 2026.
1x3Tip9ZaX.problem: Document understanding benchmarks focus on element localization rather than joint reasoning over region semantics, spatial relations, and visual structure.
1x3Tip9ZaX.method: They construct ADOPD 2026 by enriching ADOPD 2024 anchors with human-cleaned captions, semantic tags, and grounded chain-of-thought traces under a shared visual-anchor vocabulary for tagging, grounding, and counting.
1x3Tip9ZaX.key_idea: Represents text blocks, visual entities, semantic labels, boxes, and polygon masks in a shared visual-anchor vocabulary with grounded CoT traces.
1x3Tip9ZaX.evidence: Evaluations of detectors and multimodal models across semantic tagging, unified grounding, and DocCount dense counting on ~2.5M tagged elements.
1x3Tip9ZaX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the substantial annotation scale of ~2.5M elements and the unified visual-anchor organization extending ADOPD 2024.
1x3Tip9ZaX.main_concern: Novelty is limited beyond dataset annotation, DocCount does not test Anchor-CoT usage during inference, and document-specialized detectors are omitted.

sKcibXcqfE.one_liner: Uses activation steering across nine extraction methods to show LLM self-report and risk-taking behavior follow near-orthogonal directions.
sKcibXcqfE.problem: Black-box prompting shows selective disagreement between LLM self-reports and actions, leaving unclear whether internal representations couple or dissociate them.
sKcibXcqfE.method: The authors extract steering vectors from nine methods spanning task-specific directives, model task choices, and dispositional descriptions, applying the same internal interventions to both behavioral tasks and psychometric self-report instruments. They further diagnose directive overlap via quantity-instruction projection controls.
sKcibXcqfE.key_idea: Applies nine activation-steering vector constructions identically to psychometric self-reports and behavioral tasks, revealing near-orthogonal internal control directions.
sKcibXcqfE.evidence: Evaluated across four open-weight LLMs on two behavioral risk-taking tasks (BART, CCT) and two psychometric self-report instruments with random and projection controls.
sKcibXcqfE.claimed_gains: Removing the quantity-instruction component leaves task-specific directives with only 32% of their behavioral effect.
sKcibXcqfE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representational activation-steering perspective and systematic comparison of nine extraction methods with careful controls are strong contributions.
sKcibXcqfE.main_concern: Reviewers note that extraction context confounds supervision source, behavioral risk is measured via log-odds over numeric thresholds rather than generation, and own-choice vectors lack held-out tasks.

NRNhzFBMRe.one_liner: Performs multiple optimization steps per on-policy rollout batch to reduce sampling and teacher-inference cost in distillation.
NRNhzFBMRe.problem: Standard on-policy distillation updates the student briefly after each rollout round, incurring high overhead when sampling and teacher inference are expensive.
NRNhzFBMRe.method: The authors modify on-policy distillation (OPD) by executing up to 128 optimization steps on each collected rollout batch before resampling from the updated student policy. This extracts more learning signal per teacher-labeled trajectory while keeping the top-k distillation loss fixed.
NRNhzFBMRe.key_idea: Decouples rollout generation from optimization by running many student gradient updates per on-policy batch before refreshing the rollout distribution.
NRNhzFBMRe.evidence: Evaluated on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B across mathematical reasoning benchmarks with ablations on replay frequency, learning rate, and KL regularization.
NRNhzFBMRe.claimed_gains: Taking 128 optimization steps per rollout batch achieves a 2.07x wall-clock speedup and uses 64.9% fewer FLOPs than vanilla OPD while maintaining or improving performance.
NRNhzFBMRe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modification is simple, practical for reducing rollout/teacher costs, and well-tested in controlled fixed-loss comparisons.
NRNhzFBMRe.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient differentiation from DistiLLM-2 and Proximal Policy Distillation and limited evidence of scalability or hyperparameter sensitivity beyond 1.5B.

l7SJubsrlt.one_liner: Maintains separate Active and History clinical memories using typed clinical relations and a read-time gate for longitudinal agents.
l7SJubsrlt.problem: Clinical LLM agents must track changing patient states without either retaining outdated facts as current or overwriting history needed for longitudinal reasoning.
l7SJubsrlt.method: STAM combines semantic retrieval with typed clinical relations at write time to move superseded or resolved entries from Active memory into History memory without deletion. At read time, a query-dependent gate selectively retrieves historical records alongside active state.
l7SJubsrlt.key_idea: Partitions clinical agent memory into Active and History stores using typed clinical-relation linking at write time and a query-dependent historical gate at read time.
l7SJubsrlt.evidence: Evaluated on four longitudinal clinical QA benchmarks (including MedMemoryBench and MIMIC-QA) with state-maintenance diagnostics and evidence-length-matched comparisons.
l7SJubsrlt.claimed_gains: On MedMemoryBench, STAM increases supersession-pair recall from 28.6 to 53.9, and shows six significant improvements with no decreases at matched evidence lengths.
l7SJubsrlt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation of active versus superseded clinical history is well-motivated and the write-time diagnostics and matched-budget evaluations are informative.
l7SJubsrlt.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons to related state-aware baselines (MedCache, StateMem, A-TMA) and modest or uneven downstream QA gains over append-only or full-context baselines.

f765f2Ll2g.one_liner: Audits trace-level detectors in LLM agent benchmarks using corrupted calculator outputs to expose silent overrides and label mismatches.
f765f2Ll2g.problem: Automated trace detectors for verification and fault propagation are rarely audited against ground truth for whether they accurately reflect agent behavior.
f765f2Ll2g.method: Corrupts calculator outputs on GSM8K and tests a chemistry retrieval task across eight models, comparing ground-truth tool values, model-used values, detector labels, and human adjudication.
f765f2Ll2g.key_idea: Injects corrupted tool outputs to create ground-truth traces that measure discrepancies between actual model behavior and automated trace-detector labels.
f765f2Ll2g.evidence: Evaluated across eight models on GSM8K (up to 1,000 traces per model) and a chemistry search-retrieval task with human trace review.
f765f2Ll2g.claimed_gains: Human review finds verification labels least reliable (kappa = 0.29).
f765f2Ll2g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled fault-injection setup for auditing trace-level measurement validity.
f765f2Ll2g.main_concern: Reviewers point out that GSM8K is saturated for modern models, detector agreement was re-measured on tuning data, and the empirical scope is narrow.

5oPCWZaFcp.one_liner: Solves exact minimum-event time-series explanation in 2^beta*poly time by exploiting shared-endpoint velocity resets.
5oPCWZaFcp.problem: Verifying whether at most k nonnegative velocity-jump events explain interval-valued time-series observations is NP-complete, and convex relaxations can falsely accept infeasible budgets.
5oPCWZaFcp.method: Identifies a shared-endpoint reset across intervals with exact endpoints and open timing windows, confining combinatorial branching to uncertainty blocks of max length beta for an exact 2^beta*poly(n, beta, L) dynamic program producing rational witnesses and certificates.
5oPCWZaFcp.key_idea: Uses exact-endpoint velocity resets to bound dynamic-programming branching to local uncertainty block length beta, yielding exact witnesses and rejection certificates.
5oPCWZaFcp.evidence: Constructs a five-interval relaxation counterexample and evaluates on 24 retail-log windows and two taxi-log panels against bound-based, enumeration, and MILP baselines.
5oPCWZaFcp.claimed_gains: Settles 666 of 672 retail-log queries versus 540 for a bound-based baseline, and runs about 28% faster than enumeration and MILP on taxi-log panels.
5oPCWZaFcp.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the exact mathematical witnesses/certificates and honest reporting of unresolved cases.
5oPCWZaFcp.main_concern: Reviewers highlight restrictive assumptions (monotone nonnegative jumps, exact checkpoints) causing exponential blowup when uncertainty is dense, plus low readability.

OCOVgCj6RD.one_liner: Inserts parameterized synthetic lesion probes into chest X-rays to expose conditional failure modes hidden by aggregate detection scores.
OCOVgCj6RD.problem: Aggregate object-detection metrics conceal how medical imaging models respond to changes in lesion size, contrast, intensity profile, and anatomical location.
OCOVgCj6RD.method: PULSE inserts parameterized disk and Gaussian lesion probes into fixed real chest X-ray host images and measures paired output changes across probe attributes and lung regions.
OCOVgCj6RD.key_idea: Uses paired synthetic lesion-probe interventions in fixed real X-rays to map detector sensitivity across size, contrast, profile, and location.
OCOVgCj6RD.evidence: Evaluated fourteen chest X-ray nodule detectors across discovery/held-out host banks and two external chest X-ray datasets.
OCOVgCj6RD.claimed_gains: A Faster R-CNN and DINO detector with similar conventional scores (0.772 and 0.793) detect 40.6% and 7.7% of valid synthetic-probe conditions (a 5.3-fold difference), and two detectors within 0.19 percentage points disagree on 27.1% of paired host-site evaluations.
OCOVgCj6RD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired-intervention design is well-controlled and convincingly demonstrates that aggregate scores hide sharp behavioral differences.
OCOVgCj6RD.main_concern: Synthetic smooth probes do not clearly transfer to real irregular pulmonary nodules, and dense jargon/acronyms make the manuscript hard to read.

EiH9UBPwJp.one_liner: Encodes true genomic distances between packed short DNA reads in RoPE to train 1 Mb-context genomic models efficiently.
EiH9UBPwJp.problem: Training genomic language models on long contiguous DNA sequences incurs high data-assembly and compute costs compared to abundant short-read sequencing fragments.
EiH9UBPwJp.method: Skip-RoPE modifies Rotary Position Embeddings to advance position indices by aligned genomic coordinates across packed short-read fragments, enabling long-range distance encoding and discontinuous sequence evaluation.
EiH9UBPwJp.key_idea: Sets RoPE position offsets using aligned genomic coordinates between packed short DNA fragments so models learn megabase-scale distances without contiguous inputs.
EiH9UBPwJp.evidence: Evaluated 100M-parameter models on distal retrieval, DNALongBench, and CRISPRi enhancer-gene interaction prediction with frozen-embedding linear probes.
EiH9UBPwJp.claimed_gains: Trains a 100M-parameter model to an effective 1 Mb context using 60% fewer FLOPs than full-length training and requires up to 2.1x fewer input tokens at inference.
EiH9UBPwJp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the position-skipping modification simple, practical, and promising for compute efficiency on genomic benchmarks.
EiH9UBPwJp.main_concern: The effective-context metric measures lack of perplexity degradation rather than true long-range usage, and enhancer-gene evaluations omit direct comparisons against existing position-skip baselines like Random-RoPE or PoSE.

H0zPbQh7oh.one_liner: Elicits LLM beliefs and choices to fit discrete-choice cost functions, testing internal coherence, verbalization faithfulness, and prompt steerability.
H0zPbQh7oh.problem: Standard factual-accuracy evaluations do not reveal the implicit outcome tradeoffs guiding LLM decisions or whether models can report and steer those tradeoffs.
H0zPbQh7oh.method: The pipeline elicits an LLM's probability distribution over unknown states alongside its decision choices, then fits a discrete-choice model to recover the implied cost ratios and compare them against verbalized objectives and user-steered prompts.
H0zPbQh7oh.key_idea: Infers implicit LLM cost ratios by fitting discrete-choice models to paired belief elicitations and decision outputs.
H0zPbQh7oh.evidence: Applied across four medical diagnosis domains using frontier and open-source models.
H0zPbQh7oh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the revealed-preference framing that separates beliefs from preferences clear, interpretable, and useful for studying alignment.
H0zPbQh7oh.main_concern: In binary-state three-action tasks the model has minimal refutable content beyond monotonicity, synthetic Bayesian-network posteriors lack clinical validation, and novelty over prior LLM revealed-preference work is questioned.

O6Pvsx8i7G.one_liner: Measuring SAE additivity residuals quantifies feature interactions, while pairwise models improve joint behavioral prediction and steering.
O6Pvsx8i7G.problem: It remains unclear how well individual sparse-autoencoder feature effects predict their combined impact on language-model behavior.
O6Pvsx8i7G.method: The study retains or removes subsets of SAE contributions and measures behavioral responses. SAE Additivity Residuals quantify variation from interactions beyond a chosen order, and pairwise models predict held-out feature combinations.
O6Pvsx8i7G.key_idea: Under independent subset sampling, SAR measures normalized interaction energy beyond a selected order and bounds errors in ranking feature combinations.
O6Pvsx8i7G.evidence: Experiments span 18 model-behavior settings with matched activation-subspace rotations and five benchmarks comparing pairwise and first-order steering models.
O6Pvsx8i7G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SAR is a useful interaction measure and that results consistently favor SAE coordinates and pairwise modeling across models and tasks.
O6Pvsx8i7G.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing utility- or semantics-aligned evaluation, leaving the practical value for meaningful explanations and new-input steering unclear.

vKE6fzFcrj.one_liner: Exact power-distribution sampling reveals that prior Metropolis-Hastings gains often reflect approximation artifacts resembling beam search.
vKE6fzFcrj.problem: Approximate power sampling confounds the sharpened target distribution with artifacts of the inference procedure used to sample from it.
vKE6fzFcrj.method: The paper constructs an exact sampler for the power distribution and compares it with beam search and Metropolis-Hastings. Experiments probe accuracy, completion behavior, initialization, and convergence across models and benchmarks.
vKE6fzFcrj.key_idea: Separating exact power-distribution sampling from approximate inference tests whether reported gains arise from global tempering or sampler-specific behavior.
vKE6fzFcrj.evidence: The evaluation covers a broad set of reasoning benchmarks and base models, with accuracy, completion-length, initialization, and beam-search comparisons.
vKE6fzFcrj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing the target distribution from its sampler is important and that exact sampling can clarify distribution-sharpening claims.
vKE6fzFcrj.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that the evidence does not fully establish that earlier gains must come from approximate sampling, with additional doubts about empirical exactness.

r5zeYgu6OA.one_liner: Distilling counterfactual training outcomes into a small gate schedules behavioral-diversity strength from multi-agent training dynamics.
r5zeYgu6OA.problem: Cooperative MARL methods fix diversity strength before training even though a helpful early value can harm later coordination.
r5zeYgu6OA.method: TIDE branches candidate diversity strengths from training checkpoints, converts their outcomes into preferences, and distills them into a 1,300-parameter gate. The gate uses inexpensive training-log statistics to reschedule diversity online.
r5zeYgu6OA.key_idea: Counterfactual branches provide training-state-dependent preferences that a lightweight gate converts into online diversity-strength decisions.
r5zeYgu6OA.evidence: Reviews describe evaluation with CIA, CDS, and LIIR across six SMAC maps, all 18 algorithm-map settings, additional SMACv2 scenarios, and tuned scheduling controls.
r5zeYgu6OA.claimed_gains: TIDE's deployment-time overhead is below 0.01%, with a one-time offline cost of approximately 175 GPU-hours per algorithm-map pair.
r5zeYgu6OA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that temporal diversity scheduling is well motivated and that counterfactual supervision works across multiple diversity-promoting algorithms.
r5zeYgu6OA.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that small gains over time-only and budget-matched controls do not establish a robust benefit from training-state feedback.

Djl8pGfRb5.one_liner: Transplanting fMRI-supervised ROI tokens across images probes which cortical representations drive semantic decoding and visual selectivity.
Djl8pGfRb5.problem: Conventional encoding and decoding analyses cannot separate what a brain region represents from which representations causally drive downstream semantic retrieval.
Djl8pGfRb5.method: BrainInterv routes self-supervised visual features into fMRI-supervised tokens for cortical regions of interest and decodes them through a frozen text-embedding readout. It transplants image-trained or fMRI-decoded ROI tokens between images to measure donor-semantic transfer.
Djl8pGfRb5.key_idea: Cross-image ROI-token transplantation acts as an in silico intervention that tests each region's contribution to downstream semantic retrieval.
Djl8pGfRb5.evidence: The study evaluates 1000-way semantic retrieval, voxel-to-token decoding, low-level visual probes, intervention controls, and consistency across four participants.
Djl8pGfRb5.claimed_gains: ROI-tuned image tokens reach R@10 = 0.942 ± 0.007, while fMRI-decoded tokens reach R@10 = 0.541 ± 0.085 with the same frozen readout.
Djl8pGfRb5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the framework connects visual features, fMRI supervision, and interventions coherently, with thoughtful token-transplant controls.
Djl8pGfRb5.main_concern: Two reviewers note that stronger semantic effects in high-level regions and stronger visual effects in early regions largely confirm established cortical organization.

17dGAnvZRM.one_liner: Scoring economic outcomes alongside legally grounded duties exposes tradeoffs and avoidable noncompliance in delegated real-estate agents.
17dGAnvZRM.problem: Task-success and safety benchmarks do not measure whether an agent fulfills professional obligations while pursuing a client's economic objective.
17dGAnvZRM.method: RealEstateBench simulates a continuing real-estate market where seller agents market properties and negotiate through structured actions and dialogue. Statute- and case-law-derived rubrics assess conduct against simulator ground truth, with an examiner validated on court-case trajectories.
17dGAnvZRM.key_idea: Fiduciary performance jointly evaluates retained outcomes and role-specific duties rather than treating task completion or refusal behavior as sufficient.
17dGAnvZRM.evidence: The benchmark evaluates eight models over 40 sessions and validates its examiner on 300 seller-buyer trajectories derived and checked against court cases.
17dGAnvZRM.claimed_gains: Compliance and commission have correlation ρ = -0.06, while the highest earner makes 55% more commission with 17 percentage points lower compliance.
17dGAnvZRM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly measuring economic outcomes and legally grounded professional conduct addresses a meaningful agent-evaluation gap.
17dGAnvZRM.main_concern: Two reviewers emphasize that only five independent sessions per model and no corrected pairwise significance make frontier and dominance conclusions uncertain.

shdKDWCNWY.one_liner: Retrieves similar medical cases zero-shot via vector candidate search followed by token-set to token-set VLM re-ranking.
shdKDWCNWY.problem: Vector-database retrieval over medical embeddings lacks clinical context sensitivity, whereas running multimodal foundation models over full databases is computationally prohibitive.
shdKDWCNWY.method: The authors propose a training-free two-stage retrieval pipeline: Stage 1 performs fast vector search to retrieve candidate cases, and Stage 2 re-ranks candidates using token-set to token-set similarity (via optimal transport) over context-conditioned VLM token embeddings.
shdKDWCNWY.key_idea: Combines fast vector candidate retrieval with zero-shot token-set to token-set optimal-transport re-ranking on context-conditioned VLM embeddings.
shdKDWCNWY.evidence: Evaluated across multiple medical retrieval encoders and six pathologies, including ablations and latency measurements.
shdKDWCNWY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the practical training-free two-stage design and reported top-ranked retrieval gains on challenging pathologies.
shdKDWCNWY.main_concern: Clinical context awareness is insufficiently validated (relevance is binary single-pathology matching), and the token-set optimal-transport similarity is not directly compared against MaxSim or mean-pooled cosine on identical embeddings.

GhhWCEKoib.one_liner: Studies when honesty character midtraining survives instruction tuning and RL using matched neutral controls and downstream rehearsal.
GhhWCEKoib.problem: Improvements in desirable traits after character midtraining do not guarantee that those behaviors persist after instruction tuning and reinforcement learning.
GhhWCEKoib.method: The authors conduct a controlled study of honesty-related behavior comparing character-midtrained models against neutral controls matched on corpus size, topic, and reasoning markers through SFT and RL, varying whether character text is rehearsed or supervised downstream.
GhhWCEKoib.key_idea: Tracks character-midtrained models versus topic-matched neutral controls across SFT and RL while varying downstream character rehearsal and supervision.
GhhWCEKoib.evidence: Controlled experiments on an open language model evaluating false-premise correction and uncertainty acknowledgment across midtraining, SFT, and RL stages.
GhhWCEKoib.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing whether character midtraining survives post-training with topic-matched corpus controls is an important alignment question.
GhhWCEKoib.main_concern: The design lacks a rehearsal-without-midtraining control to separate true survival of midtraining from fresh learning during rehearsal, and key evaluation details are missing.

bkjsLvvH1D.one_liner: DIALECT enables continuous-space multi-agent LLM communication via stochastic token-embedding mixtures and two-stage cross-model translation bridges.
bkjsLvvH1D.problem: Natural-language multi-agent communication incurs generation latency and discrete-token information loss, while incompatible embedding spaces hinder direct latent exchange across different LLMs.
bkjsLvvH1D.method: DIALECT constructs continuous thoughts as stochastic mixtures of token embeddings; for same-model agents they pass directly, while for heterogeneous frozen LLMs a two-stage trained bridge projects thoughts into the receiver's input embedding space.
bkjsLvvH1D.key_idea: Exchanges stochastic mixtures of token embeddings between agents and maps them across frozen heterogeneous LLMs via a two-stage trained translation bridge.
bkjsLvvH1D.evidence: Evaluated in a two-agent planner-solver setting on 13 benchmarks across math reasoning, knowledge QA, and code generation using four 3B–8B models from three families.
bkjsLvvH1D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical importance of heterogeneous continuous multi-agent communication and commend the broad 13-benchmark evaluation across model families.
bkjsLvvH1D.main_concern: Individual components (soft-token sampling, bridge training, losses) lack controlled ablations to isolate their contributions and clarify novelty over prior latent-communication work.

AI6HJpsgKP.one_liner: Carving learns sparse Transformer sublayer and connection topologies by jointly training edge gates with weights and compiling the remaining graph.
AI6HJpsgKP.problem: Standard and looped Transformers rely on fixed, homogeneously repeated blocks and hand-prescribed connections rather than learned computation topologies.
AI6HJpsgKP.method: Carving places learnable gates on every edge of a Transformer's computation graph, trains the gates jointly with model weights, and compiles the surviving subgraph into a sparser carved architecture.
AI6HJpsgKP.key_idea: Places learnable gates on computation-graph edges, trains them jointly with weights, and compiles surviving sublayers and connections into a sparse Transformer.
AI6HJpsgKP.evidence: Evaluated on standard and looped Transformers at 1.3B and 2.7B parameter scales against 1.7x larger base models and training-FLOP-matched shallower Transformers.
AI6HJpsgKP.claimed_gains: Carved 1.3B and 2.7B models beat 1.7x larger base models in validation loss with half the inference FLOPs, one-third and one-half the KV cache, and 3.5x and 2.1x faster decoding throughput, removing 35% of MLP and 53% of attention sublayers on average.
AI6HJpsgKP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the flexible graph-topology search space practical and note strong validation-loss and inference-efficiency gains.
AI6HJpsgKP.main_concern: Training protocols differ inconsistently between looped (retrained from scratch) and standard (continued from search weights) Transformers, obscuring how much gain comes from topology versus extra search compute.

hW8MtlRzY7.one_liner: Pretrains language models with a separate cross-attention control channel conditioned on SAE semantic features for robust steerability.
hW8MtlRzY7.problem: Standard language models mix instructions and data in a single token stream and defer alignment to late post-training, enabling jailbreaks and in-context alignment drift.
hW8MtlRzY7.method: The authors design an architecture and conditional pretraining method (producing Mancelle-3B and Mancelle-400M) where a dedicated encoder processes SAE-derived semantic features of upcoming text and feeds them via one-way cross-attention so the token stream cannot write back into the control channel.
hW8MtlRzY7.key_idea: Isolates SAE-derived semantic control signals in a dedicated encoder read via one-way cross-attention during pretraining so the token stream cannot overwrite control.
hW8MtlRzY7.evidence: Evaluates Mancelle-3B and a controlled Mancelle-400M baseline on steering strength, fluency, and black-box/white-box counter-steering against prompt- and activation-based methods.
hW8MtlRzY7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the creative architectural separation of control and data during pretraining and the strong empirical steering robustness.
hW8MtlRzY7.main_concern: Pretraining from scratch with SAE feature extraction incurs high overhead and degrades general capabilities (e.g., ChatCORE drops substantially versus Pythia-2.8B-SFT).

SJd9xOFo5S.one_liner: SWORD adapts multi-agent satellite-cluster policies to new mission objectives via combined low-rank and sparse parameter updates.
SJd9xOFo5S.problem: Multi-agent RL policies trained for one Earth-observation satellite mission degrade when transferred to new mission objectives, while full fine-tuning updates all parameters.
SJd9xOFo5S.method: SWORD (Sparse and loW-Rank Decomposition) fine-tunes pretrained on-policy MARL policies for new tasks by combining low-rank (LoRA-SVD) updates with Fisher-guided sparse parameter updates, accompanied by a theoretical analysis of PEFT in MARL.
SJd9xOFo5S.key_idea: Adapts pretrained MARL policies to shifted mission rewards by summing SVD-initialized low-rank updates with importance-masked sparse updates.
SJd9xOFo5S.evidence: Theoretical analysis plus experiments across 12 source-target transfer pairs in a heterogeneous Earth-observation satellite cluster environment.
SJd9xOFo5S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the concrete satellite-cluster application and a promising parameter-efficiency trade-off across 12 transfer directions.
SJd9xOFo5S.main_concern: The theoretical analysis and algorithm specification have misalignments, and the independent benefit of combining low-rank and sparse updates—as well as target-task return adaptation—is insufficiently established.

cDXVot4jor.one_liner: Trains a single-pass representative simulation router via reinforcement learning using an O(n^2(log n + k)) continuous social-choice reward.
cDXVot4jor.problem: Simulation-augmented generation selects representative population subsets via costly two-stage embedding prediction and clustering, while binary proportionality axioms yield sparse RL rewards.
cDXVot4jor.method: RL-SCA trains a lightweight router end-to-end with reinforcement learning using the continuous mEJR+ proportional-representation factor as a reward signal. The authors derive an O(n^2(log n + k)) exact algorithm to compute mEJR+, enabling single-forward-pass routing at inference without computing full-population embeddings.
cDXVot4jor.key_idea: Compute the continuous mEJR+ proportionality factor in O(n^2(log n + k)) time and use it as a dense RL reward to train a single-pass subset router.
cDXVot4jor.evidence: Supported by a correctness proof for the mEJR+ algorithm and experiments across three datasets (including Remesh) against random and PRS baselines.
cDXVot4jor.claimed_gains: Computes the mEJR+ proportional representation reward in O(n^2(log n + k)) time.
cDXVot4jor.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that turning a binary social-choice axiom into an efficiently computable continuous RL reward for end-to-end routing is clean and well-grounded.
cDXVot4jor.main_concern: Experiments lack a prompt-agnostic fixed-slate baseline (leaving unclear whether the router actually uses the prompt), omit supervised/LLM-selection baselines, and use only a single training seed.

fz5yrurMbs.one_liner: Fine-tunes a span-infilling protein language model with preference-conditioned multi-objective GFlowNets across up to 14 antibody CDRH3 proxies.
fz5yrurMbs.problem: Structure-based antibody design often optimizes single binding or structural scores, neglecting multi-objective developability constraints and sequence diversity needed to avoid downstream failures.
fz5yrurMbs.method: The authors introduce an autoregressive span-infilling variant of AMPLIFY-350M as a scaffold-conditioned CDRH3 prior and fine-tune it with a preference-conditioned multi-objective GFlowNet using up to 14 proxies (backbone compatibility, likelihood, immunogenicity, novelty, developability). A reward-reduction strategy preserves Pareto dominance across 623 SAbDab structures.
fz5yrurMbs.key_idea: Fine-tune a span-infilling AMPLIFY-350M prior with a preference-conditioned GFlowNet over up to 14 developability and compatibility rewards via Pareto-preserving reward reduction.
fz5yrurMbs.evidence: Evaluated on CDRH3 loop redesign across 623 SAbDab antibody structures against inverse-folding baselines using embedding diversity, pLDDT, Rosetta, and FoldX metrics.
fz5yrurMbs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that multi-objective developability-aware antibody sampling is practically important and the diversity gains persist after confidence and Rosetta filtering.
fz5yrurMbs.main_concern: The GFlowNet sampler consistently trails inverse-folding baselines on structural confidence and binding energies (FoldX/Rosetta), and comparisons do not isolate GFlowNet training or reward reduction from simpler reward-optimized baselines.

bOzJySQLDS.one_liner: Learns discrete VQ-VAE behavioral abstractions from execution videos to replace handcrafted search features in programmatic policy synthesis.
bOzJySQLDS.problem: Programmatic policy synthesis faces flat, non-smooth search landscapes and relies on domain-specific handcrafted behavioral features to guide exploration.
bOzJySQLDS.method: Video-Induced Exploration Space (VIES) trains a vector-quantized model on unlabeled execution videos of agents to map rollouts into short sequences of discrete symbols. These factorized behavioral codes guide search over both domain-specific language mutations and LLM-generated Python programs.
bOzJySQLDS.key_idea: Vector-quantize unlabeled agent execution videos into finite discrete symbol sequences that act as domain-agnostic behavioral descriptors for programmatic policy search.
bOzJySQLDS.evidence: Evaluated on MicroRTS and Can't Stop across best-response and self-play settings for both DSL-based and LLM-written program synthesis.
bOzJySQLDS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learned discrete behavioral abstractions integrate cleanly into search for both DSL and LLM programs and outperform no-guide search when handcrafted features vanish.
bOzJySQLDS.main_concern: An untrained quantizer achieves most or all of the gains (leaving VQ-VAE learning unmotivated on Can't Stop), rendering discrete programs into videos is weakly justified, and comparisons omit baselines like LLM-GS.

oldbCPzHmO.one_liner: Uses a hypernetwork over a shared embedding space to generate trial- and condition-specific low-rank RNN weights for neural dynamics.
oldbCPzHmO.problem: Data-constrained RNNs fit neural population recordings well in single tasks but fail to share statistical strength or generalize dynamical mechanisms across multiple behavioral conditions.
oldbCPzHmO.method: JEDI is a hierarchical hypernetwork model that maps condition/trial embeddings into low-rank recurrent connectivity weights directly in neuron-indexed space. This enables cross-trial sharing and direct spectral, fixed-point, and Lyapunov analysis of inferred neural dynamics.
oldbCPzHmO.key_idea: Generate trial- and condition-specific low-rank RNN connectivity weights from a shared hypernetwork embedding space to infer and compare multi-context neural dynamics.
oldbCPzHmO.evidence: Evaluated on simulated multi-task RNN datasets (fixed-point and spectral recovery) and monkey motor-cortex reaching recordings.
oldbCPzHmO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using a shared hypernetwork to generate low-rank neuron-space connectivity is clear, relevant to multi-context neural recordings, and supports rich dynamical analyses.
