oldbCPzHmO.main_concern: Because JEDI is autonomous, it absorbs external input differences into trial-specific recurrent weights rather than testing a shared-weight input-driven RNN baseline, undermining mechanistic claims about intrinsic dynamics.

dLkSBdTHub.one_liner: Simulates compromised minority agents in shared-memory multi-agent systems to measure and diagnose persistent false-belief lock-in.
dLkSBdTHub.problem: Persistent shared written memory in multi-agent LLM systems can propagate and lock in repeated false claims even after the compromised source is removed.
dLkSBdTHub.method: The authors instruct a minority of compromised agents to repeatedly endorse a false claim under controlled speaking orders and compare shared memory, live debate, and personal memory across group sizes, plus mitigations like saving uncertainty and hiding confidence scores.
dLkSBdTHub.key_idea: Compare shared memory against live debate and personal memory under matched speaking orders to isolate how storing confident endorsements while dropping uncertain judgments causes false-belief lock-in.
dLkSBdTHub.evidence: Evaluated primarily with Claude Haiku 4.5 (and other models such as GPT-4o-mini on familiar science, GSM8K, and SciTaT per reviews) across groups up to 100 agents.
dLkSBdTHub.claimed_gains: In groups of twelve with Claude Haiku 4.5, two compromised agents cause the other ten to endorse the false claim in 70% of final judgments.
dLkSBdTHub.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper investigates a practically relevant multi-agent safety risk using a well-controlled experimental design with matched speaking orders and group sizes.
dLkSBdTHub.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty relative to prior persuasion-bias and multi-agent poisoning work, and argue that protocols differ in multiple variables simultaneously, confounding the specific role of shared memory.

UWLD1ChErH.one_liner: Uses prediction residuals from a frozen nominal world model to compute bounded online action corrections for frozen RL policies.
UWLD1ChErH.problem: Deployed RL policies degrade under unexpected dynamics shifts or actuator faults when retraining, deployment rewards, and fault labels are unavailable.
UWLD1ChErH.method: SteerControl pairs a frozen nominal policy with a frozen nominal one-step dynamics model and uses the discrepancy between predicted and observed transitions to estimate a bounded residual correction to the policy's action mean online without weight updates.
UWLD1ChErH.key_idea: Compute bounded online action-mean corrections from the transition prediction error of a frozen nominal one-step dynamics model without rewards or parameter updates.
UWLD1ChErH.evidence: Evaluated across twelve continuous-control environments under constant and switching actuator faults and physical perturbations.
UWLD1ChErH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reward-free, parameter-free online adaptation setting is practical and the residual correction is simple and broadly tested across twelve control environments.
UWLD1ChErH.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty relative to disturbance observers and inverse-dynamics control, weak theoretical justification for cross-state transfer and stability, and missing details for fair baseline comparisons.

pY5hgAVvYG.one_liner: Tests whether activation steering alters the internal state used by downstream computation or merely biases outputs via out-of-distribution shifts.
pY5hgAVvYG.problem: Behavioral success in activation steering is often mistaken for mechanistic state editing, even though models can reach the same output via different internal pathways.
pY5hgAVvYG.method: The authors evaluate register-state editing on controlled non-commutative group state-tracking tasks with trace supervision and compare single-layer activation transplanting and natural-scale steering against standard steering vectors on language models.
pY5hgAVvYG.key_idea: Test whether an activation edit acts as a causal computational state by verifying downstream transition semantics and comparing steering magnitudes against natural source-to-target activation changes.
pY5hgAVvYG.evidence: Tested on synthetic state-tracking tasks (Q8 and D8 groups per reviews) and two LLM task settings using Qwen and Llama models.
pY5hgAVvYG.claimed_gains: Single-layer activation replacement yields under 2% of the all-layer patching margin gain, whereas steering vectors have norms 77x (Qwen) and 26x (Llama) the median natural change to produce 54% and 82% of the reference effect.
pY5hgAVvYG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly separates behavioral output shifts from genuine causal state editing using clean synthetic state-tracking controls.
pY5hgAVvYG.main_concern: Reviewers note substantial overlap with prior work on amnesic probing, causal abstraction, and off-pathway steering (e.g., Makelov et al.), and limited natural-language task coverage.

JBy9Au1cJ5.one_liner: Unifies KV-cache eviction and OBS-style mask compensation under exact post-output-projection reconstruction error with GQA cross-head terms.
JBy9Au1cJ5.problem: Heuristic KV-cache eviction perturbs attention outputs, ignores softmax renormalization and grouped-query attention cross-head coupling, and treats eviction and compensation separately.
JBy9Au1cJ5.method: ProjCache parameterizes eviction and compensation via attention-weight masks, derives an exact single-pair Taylor saliency score after the output projection (including renormalization and GQA cross-head terms), and adapts Optimal Brain Surgeon to jointly optimize retained token masks.
JBy9Au1cJ5.key_idea: Score KV eviction by exact post-W_O Taylor reconstruction error with renormalization and GQA cross-head coupling, then apply OBS quadratic optimization to compensate retained token masks.
JBy9Au1cJ5.evidence: Evaluated on LongBench and RULER with LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B across 108 eviction settings and 24 compensation settings.
JBy9Au1cJ5.claimed_gains: Improves performance in 106 of 108 settings by up to 3.4 points on LongBench and 25.6 points on RULER over heuristic scores, and reduces compensation reconstruction error by 17% to 44% across all 24 settings.
JBy9Au1cJ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the post-projection Taylor derivation accounting for renormalization and GQA cross-head terms is clean, well-grounded, and easily integrated into existing eviction pipelines.
JBy9Au1cJ5.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over ReST-KV, DropKV, and CriticalKV, marginal gains over strong recent baselines (with large drops on RULER-32K), minimal task-level benefit from compensation, and unmeasured runtime overhead.

bl2A41q92N.one_liner: Simulates program-level agent serving with coupled tool waits, shared KV-cache accounting, and admission control to discover faster scheduling policies.
bl2A41q92N.problem: Existing LLM serving simulators break down on multi-call agents because scheduling changes future call arrivals and shared KV-cache reuse depends on placement and copy completion.
bl2A41q92N.method: AgentServeSim models program-level execution history across LLM calls and tool waits, enforcing memory admission, single-charged shared prefixes, and copy-completion visibility, and couples the simulator with LLM-driven search to optimize KV-management and scheduling policies.
bl2A41q92N.key_idea: Simulate coupled agent trajectories with dynamic post-tool call releases, deduplicated shared-prefix memory accounting, and copy-aware KV availability to evaluate and search serving policies.
bl2A41q92N.evidence: Validated across 20 real-serving comparisons (four configurations by five arrival rates) and three six-policy ranking settings.
bl2A41q92N.claimed_gains: Predicts mean program job completion time with 4.74% MAPE across 20 real-serving comparisons, matches the winning policy in all three settings, and discovers a policy achieving 1.64-2.04x real-serving speedup over FCFS.
bl2A41q92N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the simulator addresses consequential agent-serving semantics (tool waits, shared prefixes, admission) and achieves accurate completion-time predictions and real-system speedups.
bl2A41q92N.main_concern: Reviewers note non-disjoint dev/test programs, single-instance search evaluation without multi-instance hardware validation, unclear boundaries vs. recent simulators, and rigid interfaces that exclude mid-tool prefetching or offloading.

8UR1gpRELz.one_liner: Propagates Gaussian energy-barrier uncertainty through chemical reaction-network kinetics and truncates Krylov solver rank to the epistemic noise floor.
8UR1gpRELz.problem: Reaction rates depend exponentially on quantum-chemistry energy barriers, so small barrier errors can flip predicted chemical products in automated reaction networks.
8UR1gpRELz.method: The proposed probabilistic kinetic solver models energy barriers as probability distributions, computes expected product populations via Monte Carlo averaging, and couples Krylov truncation effort to the barrier uncertainty level so solver cost drops as uncertainty grows.
8UR1gpRELz.key_idea: Average reaction-network populations over barrier-uncertainty distributions while truncating Krylov spectral resolution at the epistemic noise floor set by barrier uncertainty.
8UR1gpRELz.evidence: Validated quantitatively on synthetic reaction networks across topologies, temperatures, and reaction times, plus two qualitative literature reaction networks.
8UR1gpRELz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well-motivated and linking numerical solver effort (Krylov truncation) to input barrier uncertainty is a sound, interesting principle.
8UR1gpRELz.main_concern: Reviewers point out that quantitative gains are tested almost exclusively under the exact Gaussian error model assumed by the solver (where posterior-mean optimality holds a priori), without testing biased or misspecified quantum-chemistry errors.

SwaoOug3L7.one_liner: Replaces inference-time ControlNet activation scaling with training-time pixel-level control-map distortion and explicit strength-map conditioning.
SwaoOug3L7.problem: Modulating ControlNet strength by scaling adapter activations at inference pushes features out of distribution, blurs region boundaries on coarse feature maps, and causes erratic adherence variance.
SwaoOug3L7.method: DisControl applies per-pixel noise degradation to the conditioning control map during training according to a spatial strength map and passes the strength map as an extra input channel, enabling local pixel-resolution modulation without inference-time activation scaling.
SwaoOug3L7.key_idea: Train ControlNet on pixel-wise degraded control maps paired with an explicit spatial strength-map input channel instead of rescaling internal adapter activations at inference.
SwaoOug3L7.evidence: Evaluated on SD1.5 and SDXL across local modulation, boundary separation, cross-image adherence variance, and checkpoint conversion experiments.
SwaoOug3L7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a practical flaw in local ControlNet modulation with a simple, zero-inference-overhead input-conditioning approach.
SwaoOug3L7.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains are not cleanly isolated from explicit strength-map conditioning alone, baselines use under-trained custom ControlNets rather than public checkpoints, and strength response saturates in a narrow range.

7st3nKkVy8.one_liner: Replays 6,428 recorded agent trajectories to compute exact pass^k under budget-constrained sampling, voting, verification, and retry policies.
7st3nKkVy8.problem: Deploying consistent tool-use agents under a fixed inference budget requires deciding whether to spend compute on extra samples, voting, retries, or verification.
7st3nKkVy8.method: The authors build a trace-driven recursive evaluator that replays pre-recorded tau-bench and tau2-bench trajectories to compute exact pass^k for allocation policies without LLM API calls, analyzing how relative candidate-reading cost governs verifier vs. voting optimality.
7st3nKkVy8.key_idea: Evaluate budget-constrained agent allocation policies exactly via recursive replay of recorded trajectory pools and characterize voting-versus-verification tradeoffs by relative candidate-reading cost.
7st3nKkVy8.evidence: Replayed 6,428 trajectories across four frontier models and three domains from tau-bench and tau2-bench, plus theoretical cost-over-accuracy analysis.
7st3nKkVy8.claimed_gains: Single-attempt success averages 56.3% vs. 41.4% for pass^4; allocation raises pass^4 by +1.76 points at equal bytes and +4.49 at equal dollars; under equal byte pricing a perfect verifier reaches 43.6% (tying voting) vs. 53.2% if free, while at 0.03-0.10 list read pricing perfect verification beats voting by +8.0 points and the weakest verifier gains +3.1.
7st3nKkVy8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exact recursive replay over recorded trajectories and explicit accounting for candidate-reading cost are clean, reproducible contributions to test-time compute analysis.
7st3nKkVy8.main_concern: Reviewers stress that the headline voting-beats-verifier result hinges on charging full transcript byte costs per verification read, and that replaying finite temperature-0 trajectory pools introduces plug-in bias and may not reflect live sampling.

ZA7jafD41T.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-robot VLM teams on distributed hazard decisions and introduces HUDDLE for visually grounded structured deliberation.
ZA7jafD41T.problem: VLM-powered robot teams fail near chance level on high-stakes Proceed/Hold decisions when hazard-relevant evidence is split across robots' local observations and private context.
ZA7jafD41T.method: The authors model three household environments as Dec-POMDPs with communication and propose HUDDLE, a structured protocol requiring robots to share local context, ground visual claims in observations, coordinate inspection moves, and assess pooled evidence before deciding.
ZA7jafD41T.key_idea: Enforce staged context sharing, visual claim grounding, coordinated inspection, and pooled-evidence assessment in VLM multi-robot teams before collective Proceed/Hold voting.
ZA7jafD41T.evidence: Evaluated across three household Dec-POMDP environments (12 instances each per reviews) with unstructured baselines, full-information diagnostics, and trajectory failure analyses.
ZA7jafD41T.claimed_gains: Full-information diagnostics raise accuracy to 100% in some settings where unstructured communication falls to chance level.
ZA7jafD41T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the full-information diagnostic cleanly isolates distributed-communication failure from individual VLM limits and that active inspection in the bedroom task is well-motivated.
ZA7jafD41T.main_concern: Reviewers note that HUDDLE bundles communication structure, delayed action control, and review together without ablations isolating deliberation, lacks comparison to prior staged-exchange protocols, and uses a small 3-environment benchmark.

7tjAyMuPu9.one_liner: Applies CountSketch to per-sequence online RLVR rollouts to measure full-model policy-gradient noise and cross-prompt geometry.
7tjAyMuPu9.problem: RLVR algorithms make strong assumptions about policy-gradient variance and cross-prompt geometry that have not been directly measured across full LLM parameters at scale.
7tjAyMuPu9.method: The authors compress per-sequence gradients of online RLVR rollouts with linear CountSketch projections, validate sketch fidelity against exact gradients and LM-head proxies, and analyze within-prompt gradient noise, baselines, and rollout allocation offline.
7tjAyMuPu9.key_idea: Compress per-sequence full-model RLVR policy gradients with CountSketch during online rollouts to enable offline measurement of gradient variance and cross-prompt inner products.
7tjAyMuPu9.evidence: Validated across multiple model sizes and checkpoints with sketch-width sweeps, exact-gradient comparisons, and rollout pools up to 2,048 samples.
7tjAyMuPu9.claimed_gains: At 16 rollouts per prompt, median cosine similarity between a per-prompt gradient estimate and a held-out high-budget reference is between 0.02 and 0.20 depending on model and checkpoint.
7tjAyMuPu9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using CountSketch for full-model RLVR gradient measurement is a practical, well-validated methodology that outperforms LM-head proxies and yields useful insights on GRPO-style objectives.
7tjAyMuPu9.main_concern: Reviewers flag ambiguities in reference-pool reliability definitions and extrapolations beyond the 2,048 rollout pool, potential indexing/truncation issues for centered estimators, and somewhat disorganized exposition.

6kSp9p7OFU.one_liner: Models counterfactual token edits as activation cones and estimates multi-edit compositional contributions via path-sampled Shapley values.
6kSp9p7OFU.problem: Averaging hidden-state differences to find linear concept directions hides variation across lexical realizations and ignores how multiple simultaneous edits compose.
6kSp9p7OFU.method: The paper retains individual counterfactual activation changes as cone-shaped effect clouds (axis and width) across contexts and words, and decomposes multi-edit sentence lattices via Shapley values approximated by single-path sequential edit walkers.
6kSp9p7OFU.key_idea: Represent counterfactual edits as directional effect clouds (cones) rather than mean vectors and estimate compositional multi-edit Shapley shares by averaging single-path lattice walks.
6kSp9p7OFU.evidence: Evaluated across five models from three families on three manually written base sentences (judicial, medical, literary) plus a 16-edit long sentence.
6kSp9p7OFU.claimed_gains: Synonyms of an adjective scatter more than random adjectives in all 15 model-sentence combinations.
6kSp9p7OFU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree unifying directional concentration across contexts/words with walker-approximated Shapley attribution over edit lattices is a systematic, useful interpretability framework.
6kSp9p7OFU.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited text diversity from a few hand-crafted sentences rather than natural corpora and point out geometric imprecisions in defining cones via mean cosine concentration.

N3DesjnN82.one_liner: Incorporates membership-privacy alignment into two-stage diffusion post-training quantization via residual alignment and timestep-specific activation scaling.
N3DesjnN82.problem: Diffusion models leak training membership under membership inference attacks, while existing privacy-aware retraining defenses are costly and hurt image quality.
N3DesjnN82.method: PAQ-Diffusion performs layer-wise quantization reconstruction that aligns member and non-member quantization residual distributions, then optimizes timestep-specific activation quantization scales with a denoising-based privacy objective without retraining full-precision weights.
N3DesjnN82.key_idea: Align member and non-member quantization residuals layer-wise and tune timestep-specific activation scales via a denoising privacy loss during diffusion post-training quantization.
N3DesjnN82.evidence: Evaluated on three diffusion models (including DDPM and SD-Laion per reviews) against five membership inference attacks with stage ablations, reporting AUC, TPR@1%FPR, and FID.
N3DesjnN82.claimed_gains: Reduces SecMI-NN attack AUC by up to 20.62% while maintaining generation quality.
N3DesjnN82.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree integrating membership privacy into post-training quantization without full-precision retraining is practical and yields promising joint privacy and FID improvements on DDPM.
N3DesjnN82.main_concern: Reviewers warn that Stage 2 directly optimizes the Loss/SecMI attack statistic without testing adaptive attacks, and flag inconsistencies in dataset split sizes and reconstruction loss definitions.

8qzlh6QB6D.one_liner: Analyzes spectral collapse of gradient and update histories and mixes them with directed Ramanujan-graph matrices in Nesterov-Ramanujan descent.
8qzlh6QB6D.problem: Iterative optimizers exhibit sharp spectral energy concentration in their gradient and update histories, whose distinct dynamics and intervention potential remain understudied.
8qzlh6QB6D.method: The authors measure the spectral effective rank of recorded gradient and update sequences on convex problems and DNNs, and define Nesterov-Ramanujan descent (NRD), which multiplies history vectors by a sparse randomly directed 2-colored Ramanujan graph adjacency matrix to compute next steps.
8qzlh6QB6D.key_idea: Transform gradient and update history vectors using sparse directed Ramanujan-graph adjacency matrices to alter spectral concentration during accelerated descent.
8qzlh6QB6D.evidence: Empirical spectral-rank measurements on convex optimization problems and DNNs (CNNs and ResNets), with NRD evaluated primarily on convex problems.
8qzlh6QB6D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating gradient history from realized update history reveals an interesting spectral concentration contrast in momentum-based optimizers.
8qzlh6QB6D.main_concern: Reviewers note that higher effective spectral rank does not establish faster convergence, key objective-gap and iteration-count results are missing, and central theoretical and DNN questions remain unanswered.

fTFW5BBVmi.one_liner: Iteratively scores, replaces low-importance fine-tuned parameters with merged values using OBD-style Taylor expansion, and re-merges models.
fTFW5BBVmi.problem: Merging task-specific fine-tuned models creates parameter conflicts, and resolving them by selective replacement requires estimating the loss impact of each parameter change.
fTFW5BBVmi.method: OBMerge adapts Optimal Brain Damage via a Taylor expansion that estimates loss change from replacing a parameter with its merged value rather than zero, running an iterative score-replace-remerge loop on RegMean/RegMean++ alongside an LLM-generated synthetic calibration data pipeline.
fTFW5BBVmi.key_idea: Estimate loss change from replacing each fine-tuned weight with its current merged value via Taylor expansion, iteratively replacing low-scoring weights and re-merging.
fTFW5BBVmi.evidence: Evaluated on two vision and three language models (including Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.2-3B) with both real and LLM-generated synthetic calibration data.
fTFW5BBVmi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the iterative score-replace-remerge loop consistently improves RegMean/RegMean++ across all five models and that the synthetic calibration pipeline is practically useful.
fTFW5BBVmi.main_concern: Reviewers view the methodological advance as incremental over prior OBD-based and iterative saliency model-merging methods (such as OBIM and SA-Merging) and tightly coupled to reconstruction-based mergers.
